author: copilot
body:
Rewrites Deck Delver into **Memory Dungeon** — a 4×4 memory-match roguelite with progressive dungeon scoring, a memory-tax damage system, and a persistent high-score board.

## Core mechanic changes
- **Memory-tax damage:** flipping a previously-seen card without matching costs −1 HP; enemy cards cost −3 HP. First flip is always free. Card shakes laterally + HP stat shakes on penalty.
- **Fixed 4×4 grid** for all dungeon levels (was variable 3×4 → 5×6). Card scale locked at ⅔ of available wrap space so the grid breathes on both mobile and desktop.
- **Joker card:** unmatched flip secretly swaps the joker's position with a random face-down card (DOM front-face swap, no re-render).
- Removed the old flat "enemy flip = −1 HP" rule entirely in favour of the seen-count system.

## Cards & visuals
- **6 distinct enemies** (👺 Goblin → 🕷️ Spider) and **4 distinct weapons** (🗡️ → 🔱), each with a unique emoji and name — no more generic "Enemy Lv2".
- **Pip ranks** reduced to face cards only: A ⭐ K 👑 Q 💎 J ⚡.
- **3 new pip suits** beyond ♠♥♦♣: 🌸 Flower (rose), 🀄 Dragon (crimson), ♟ Pawn (slate) — each with a matching CSS colour theme.
- Deal animation: cards fly in from above one-by-one with a 55 ms stagger.

## Scoring & persistence
- Score = **dungeons cleared** (primary) + **total moves** (secondary, lower is better).
- Top-10 scores persisted in `localStorage` (`memoryDungeon.scores.v1`), sorted by levels DESC → moves ASC.
- Main menu shows the best run inline; dedicated high-scores table accessible from menu and game-over screen.

## State tracking additions
```js
state.seenCount = new Array(cards.length).fill(0); // reset per level
// incremented on tap; penalty fires when seenCount[i] > 1 on a miss
```

### Motivation
- The Actions workflow always chose `npm ci` for npm projects which fails when `package-lock.json` is absent. 
- The Pages job expects a static `out` directory but Next.js only creates it when static export is enabled.

### Description
- Update `.github/workflows/nextjs.yml` to use `npm install` when `package-lock.json` is missing and keep `npm ci` when a lockfile exists. 
- Add `output: "export"` to `next.config.mjs` so Next.js produces the `out` directory for GitHub Pages.
- Commit and open a PR with these changes.

author: jsgoecke
body:
## Summary

Closes #208.

Adds `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml` so the OME backend and frontend are built and **published as releases on GitHub** — specifically to the GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`), where they appear under this repository's **Packages** tab. Downstream integrators (e.g. the World Historical Gazetteer's K8s deployment described in the issue) can then pull prebuilt images instead of cloning the repo and building locally.

## What the workflow does

- Triggers on `push` to `main`, on pushing a git tag matching `v*.*.*`, and via `workflow_dispatch`.
- Uses a matrix to build two images in parallel:
  - `ghcr.io/iskme/open-metadata-exchange/server` (from `Dockerfile`)
  - `ghcr.io/iskme/open-metadata-exchange/frontend` (from `Dockerfile-fe`)
- Tagging via `docker/metadata-action@v5`:
  - On push to `main`: `:latest` and `:main-<shortsha>`
  - On `v*.*.*` tag push: `:1.2.3`, `:1.2`, `:1`
- Authenticates to GHCR with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` (no extra secrets needed).
- Uses BuildKit with GitHub Actions cache (`type=gha`) scoped per-image.
- Runs with least-privilege permissions: `contents: read`, `packages: write`.

The existing `ci.yml` is unchanged — testing and publishing stay in separate workflows.

## Docs

`README.md` gains a short "Prebuilt Docker images" section with the `docker pull` commands and a pointer to the workflow.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge to `main` → confirm workflow runs and `:latest` + `:main-<sha>` appear under Packages for both images.
- [ ] Push a `v0.0.1` tag (or similar test tag) → confirm semver tags `:0.0.1`, `:0.0`, `:0` are published.
- [ ] `docker pull ghcr.io/iskme/open-metadata-exchange/server:latest` succeeds from an unauthenticated client once the package is marked public (Package settings → "Change visibility").
- [ ] `docker pull ghcr.io/iskme/open-metadata-exchange/frontend:latest` likewise.

## Pre-existing test failure (not a regression)

`uv run pytest` fails to collect `tests/test_ome_node.py` locally because that module opens an NNTP connection at import time and no live NNTP server is running — this matches the scenario `CLAUDE.md` explicitly identifies as a known pre-existing failure. All other tests pass:

```
collected 27 items
tests/test_nntp_article.py ....                                   [ 14%]
tests/test_openstax_plugin.py .....                               [ 33%]
tests/test_schemas.py ........                                    [ 62%]
tests/test_whg_plugin.py ..........                               [100%]
============================== 27 passed in 0.16s ==============================
```

This change is workflow/YAML + README only and touches no Python code, so it cannot have introduced the NNTP failure.

## Notes / follow-ups

- **Package visibility:** GHCR packages default to private. After the first successful publish, a maintainer with admin rights will need to flip each package to **Public** (repo → Packages → package → Package settings → Change visibility).
- **Multi-arch:** Builds are `linux/amd64` only. Adding `linux/arm64` is a small follow-up (QEMU + `platforms:` on `build-push-action`) and is recommended for K8s consumers, but kept out of this PR to keep scope tight.

author: asinkpon
body:
This PR adds and wires the thumbnail-worker into Docker Compose with Redis and the catalog database. The thumbnail worker listens for Redis pub/sub transcode complete events, queues thumbnail jobs, simulates thumbnail extraction, writes thumbnail references to the catalog database, and publishes thumbnail complete events. It also exposes a health endpoint that reports queue depth, dead letter queue depth, and the timestamp of the last successfully processed job, so queue behavior can be observed during burst tests.

How to test it:
Start the full system:

`docker compose up --build`

Check the thumbnail worker health endpoint:

`curl http://localhost:3005/health`

Watch the thumbnail worker logs:

`docker compose logs -f thumbnail-worker`

Before publishing a test transcode-complete event, insert a matching video row into the catalog database. The thumbnail table has a foreign key to catalog.video(id), so the event's videoId must already exist in the catalog DB:

```
docker compose exec -T catalog-db psql -U catalog -d catalog <<'SQL'
INSERT INTO video (
  id,
  upload_id,
  user_id,
  title,
  original_filename,
  duration_seconds,
  status,
  metadata,
  uploaded_at
)
VALUES (
  '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001',
  '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111',
  'test-user',
  'Test Video',
  'test-video.mp4',
  60,
  'processing',
  '{"duration":60}'::jsonb,
  NOW()
)
ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;
SQL
```

Publish a sample transcode complete event with the same videoId:

`docker compose exec redis redis-cli PUBLISH transcode-complete '{"jobId":"test-job-1","videoId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001","metadata":{"duration":60},"status":"complete"}'
`
Check the thumbnail worker health endpoint again:

`curl http://localhost:3005/health`

Check that thumbnail references were written to the catalog database:

`docker compose exec catalog-db psql -U catalog -d catalog -c "SELECT video_id, thumbnail_url, timestamp_seconds FROM thumbnail ORDER BY timestamp_seconds;"`

Expected thumbnail rows should include simulated refs around 10%, 50%, and 90% of the video duration:

/thumbnails/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/6.jpg
/thumbnails/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/30.jpg
/thumbnails/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/54.jpg

**Service affected**

thumbnail-worker/
catalog-service/db/schema.sql
compose.yml

**Database change note:**
Docker only runs catalog-service/db/schema.sql when the catalog database volume is first created. If testing with an existing local catalog-db volume, recreate the volume or apply the schema manually before testing thumbnail writes.

author: balaji-embedcentrum
body:
Follow-up to #23. The idempotency guard there caught duplicate \`/done\` POSTs from the Traefik / proxy retry — but \`/events\` POSTs were still going through when retried, publishing \`typing\` + \`agent_chunk\` events to Den after the task was already terminal.

## Observed symptom (user report)

After a Hunt task completes:
1. Dispatch → \`Local is typing…\` appears ✓
2. Agent response renders in Den ✓
3. Task shows as Done ✓
4. A few seconds later — \`Local is typing…\` **appears again** ✗
5. 45 s pass with no real activity → auto-clear timer fires → indicator disappears
6. No new response ever arrives

## Root cause

\`/events\` had no status check. Traefik retries the same POST after the first \`/done\`. The delayed retry hits:

\`\`\`python
await pubsub.publish(chat_channel, {"type": "typing", ...})
\`\`\`

Den's listener registers it, shows the indicator, waits 45 s with no fresh typing events, times out. Classic phantom.

## Fix

Same one-line idempotency pattern as #23:

\`\`\`python
if task.status != "in_progress":
    return {"status": "ignored", "reason": "task terminal"}
\`\`\`

First \`/events\` call on an in-progress task: publishes chunk + typing as before.
Retried \`/events\` after task done: returns \`{ignored}\`, nothing published.

## Rollout

api-only rebuild. No migration, no frontend.

\`\`\`
cd ~/akela-ai
git pull origin main
sudo docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build api
\`\`\`

## Test plan

1. Dispatch a fresh local-agent task.
2. Watch Den: typing appears, response arrives, typing clears.
3. Watch for ~60 s: phantom \"Local is typing…\" should NOT re-appear.
4. Server log should show the first \`POST /events\` as 200, any subsequent retries also 200 but with log body \`{"ignored"}\`.

author: muanlartins
body:
## Summary

Renders each entry in a publication card's `IDENTIFIERS` block as a link when a canonical URL is derivable from the key. Resolver added as \`identifierLink(key, value)\` in \`web/assets/app.js\`.

| Key | Link pattern |
|---|---|
| \`doi\` | \`https://doi.org/<value>\` |
| \`openalex_id\` | \`https://openalex.org/<value>\` |
| \`arxiv_id\` | \`https://arxiv.org/abs/<value>\` |
| \`dblp_key\` | \`https://dblp.org/rec/<value>\` |
| \`semantic_scholar_id\` | \`https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/<value>\` |
| \`sbc_sol_id\` | \`https://sol.sbc.org.br/index.php/<slug>/article/view/<num>\` |
| \`isbn\` / \`issn\` / \`scopus_id\` | plain text (no clean landing URL) |

## Why

Papers with no top-level \`url\` (e.g., Marcos's 2017 CIMElec paper, which only has \`openalex_id: W2905978441\`) previously showed the identifier as plain text with no click-through. Now every identifier becomes a one-click destination, and papers like the 2018 SBSeg one gain a direct SOL-article-view link via \`sbc_sol_id\` alongside the existing DOI primary link.

## Test plan

- [ ] 2017 CIMElec paper (araujo-agregador-seguro-metrologia-2017) → \`OPENALEX_ID: W2905978441\` is clickable.
- [ ] 2018 SBSeg paper (araujo-secure-cloud-smart-meters-2018) → \`DOI\`, \`OPENALEX_ID\`, and \`SBC_SOL_ID\` all clickable; SBC_SOL_ID resolves to \`https://sol.sbc.org.br/index.php/sbseg/article/view/4274\`.
- [ ] Papers with \`isbn\` / \`issn\` keep plain text rendering.

author: tylerbutler
body:
## Summary
New package `@tylerbu/astro-tinylytics` — Astro components for [tinylytics.app](https://tinylytics.app) analytics, kudos buttons, and webmentions.

- `Tinylytics.astro` — renders the analytics embed `<script>` (with optional `?kudos` / `?hits` widget flags) **or** the webmention `<link>` endpoint. Props are a discriminated union so `webmention` is mutually exclusive with `kudos`/`hits` at the type level.
- `KudosButton.astro` — configurable kudos button (`label`, `countThreshold`, `suffixTemplate`, `icon`, `class`, `as`). A colocated `MutationObserver` strips the count out of the button and re-renders it as "— and so do N others" in a sibling suffix span once it clears the per-wrapper threshold.
- `styles.css` — opt-in default stylesheet driven entirely by `--tlt-kudos-*` CSS variables, wrapper rule uses `:where()` for zero specificity.

Also adds an `.astro` override in `biome.jsonc` disabling `noUnusedVariables`, `noUnusedImports`, and `noUndeclaredVariables` — Biome can't parse Astro templates, so variables referenced only in the template look unused to it. Mirrors the existing Svelte override pattern.

Extracted from `tylerbutler.com`'s local components; the site itself is not migrated to the published package in this PR.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm install` — lockfile resolves cleanly
- [x] `pnpm --filter @tylerbu/astro-tinylytics pack` — 5.5 KB tarball with `LICENSE`, `package.json`, `README.md`, and `src/{Tinylytics.astro,KudosButton.astro,styles.css}`
- [x] `astro check` — 0 errors / 0 warnings / 1 hint (stock "unused `Props` interface" hint that Astro reads by convention)
- [x] `pnpm check:deps` / `check:policy` / `check:format` / `lint` — clean for this package (pre-existing `fluid-svelte` failures untouched)
- [ ] Local smoke test in a consumer Astro project before the first real publish

## Summary

- Glissandograph: Play/Record from idle now starts at the rail's current beat (follows pan), not the stored position.
- Terminology: \"rail\" = stationary vertical line; \"planchette\" = movable dot riding it. Prepares for future harmony/chord mode (multiple planchettes per rail).

- `Composition` gains `loopStartBeats` and `loopEndBeats`. Old JSON files are backfilled on load (default 0 .. 2 measures); no version bump needed.

author: copilot
body:
The production deploy workflow was failing before SSH execution because required connection secrets were not available in the job context. The deploy step also relied on brittle inline secret interpolation inside the remote script.

- **Root cause addressed**
  - Bound the `deploy` job to `environment: Production` so environment-scoped secrets are resolved for the workflow run.

- **Secret propagation hardened**
  - Declared deploy secrets in the SSH step `env`.
  - Forwarded only required vars to the remote host via `appleboy/ssh-action` `envs`, avoiding direct GitHub expression interpolation inside shell script lines.

- **Remote `.env.prod` creation made deterministic**
  - Replaced fragile heredoc-style inline interpolation with atomic file generation from forwarded runtime env vars.
  - Kept existing deploy behavior (repo sync, web rebuild, health check) unchanged.

```yaml
- name: SSH and Deploy to GCP
  uses: appleboy/ssh-action@master
  env:
    ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
    ADMIN_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_SECRET_KEY }}
    POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.POSTGRES_PASSWORD }}
  with:
    host: ${{ secrets.GCP_VM_IP }}
    key: ${{ secrets.GCP_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    envs: ADMIN_PASSWORD,ADMIN_SECRET_KEY,POSTGRES_PASSWORD
    script: |
      {
        echo "ADMIN_PASSWORD=$ADMIN_PASSWORD"
        echo "ADMIN_SECRET_KEY=$ADMIN_SECRET_KEY"
        echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$POSTGRES_PASSWORD"
      } > /tmp/.env.prod.new
      mv /tmp/.env.prod.new ~/galantesjewelry/.env.prod
```

author: joaquinpary
body:
## Release 4.0.0 — Courier Firmware

### Overview

This release closes the final layer of the LoRa-CHADS logistics stack by introducing the **embedded firmware** that runs on physical courier devices, completing the end-to-end pipeline: hub/warehouse nodes → C++ core → Go API Gateway → courier firmware. It also ships comprehensive technical documentation for all previous releases.

---

### What's New

#### 1. Courier Firmware (firmware) — Zephyr RTOS on ESP32

A **Zephyr RTOS** application (`dhl_courier`) designed to run on ESP32 DevKitC hardware or simulated natively with `native_sim` for development.

**Key modules:**

| Module | File | Responsibility |
|--------|------|----------------|
| Main loop | `src/main.c` | WiFi connect, MQTT handshake, topic routing |
| GPS Telemetry | `src/gps_telemetry.c` | Simulated random-walk from Córdoba coordinates, published every 5 s |
| Provisioning | `src/provisioning.c` | NVS-backed SSID/PSK/employee-ID persistence via Zephyr Settings |
| Route Manager | `src/route_manager.c` | Parses JSON route arrays, tracks current stop, advances on delivery confirmation |
| UI Bridge | `src/ui/` | Qt5 widget UI (`native_sim`) or no-op stub (`embedded`) |

**MQTT topology:**

| Topic | Direction | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| `routes/<employee_id>` | Server → Device | Route assignment (JSON array of stops) |
| `alerts/sos/<employee_id>` | Device → Server | Emergency SOS trigger |
| `delivered/<employee_id>` | Device → Server | Stop delivery confirmation |
| `telemetry/<employee_id>` | Device → Server | GPS coordinates at 5 s intervals |

**Design decisions:**

- **Zephyr RTOS over bare-metal**: Provides POSIX sockets, SNTP, Kconfig, NVS settings, and a hardware abstraction layer that targets both `esp32_devkitc_procpu` and `native_sim` from the same codebase. This eliminates separate simulation and production builds.
- **MQTT over raw TCP**: The broker already exists in the docker-compose stack (RabbitMQ supports MQTT plugin). Reusing it avoids introducing a second protocol stack and keeps message routing centralized.
- **NVS/Settings for provisioning**: Credentials (SSID, PSK, employee ID) are stored in flash NVS via Zephyr's `settings` subsystem. This allows field reconfiguration without reflashing and survives reboots.
- **cJSON for JSON parsing**: Consistent with the rest of the C codebase (TP1 client/server) — same library, same serialization patterns, no extra dependencies.
- **Simulated GPS random walk**: Real GPS hardware is not required for integration testing. The random-walk model (centered on Córdoba, Argentina) produces realistic-looking telemetry payloads without a physical sensor.
- **Qt5 UI only for `native_sim`**: Qt cannot be compiled under Zephyr's cross-toolchain (`-nostdinc`, no C++ stdlib). The CMakeLists.txt compiles `ui_qt.cpp` with the host's `g++` and links the resulting object into the app, keeping the Qt dependency fully out of Zephyr's build graph. Embedded targets fall back to `ui_stub.c`.
- **flash.bin committed**: The pre-compiled binary is included to allow hardware flashing without requiring a full Zephyr SDK setup.

#### 2. Technical Documentation (docs)

Complete architecture-level documentation for all three previous releases:

| Release | Location | Coverage |
|---------|----------|----------|
| TP1 (1.0.0) | tp1 | Message protocol (`message_t`, 28 msg types, ACK mechanism), business flows (sequence diagrams), infrastructure (CMake, Docker, PostgreSQL schema) |
| TP2 (2.0.0) | tp2 | REST API process architecture, Ford-Fulkerson + Kaufmann-Malgrange algorithms, graph builder edge-cost formula, MongoDB result store |
| TP3 (3.0.0) | tp3 | Go API Gateway internals (Screaming + Hexagonal architecture), core bridge TCP protocol + DJB2 checksum, RabbitMQ fanout/shared-queue consistency model, circuit breaker, JWT + rate limiter middleware |

---

### Bottom Line

The firmware is an additive layer; the API Gateway, C++ core, and all existing Docker services are unchanged.
This adds last mile capabilities to the whole system, through a portable device with efficient communication.

author: shingonoide
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds three regression tests to `tests/test_frame_accumulation.py` covering frame accumulation behaviors that PR #61 introduced but did not directly exercise. Tests-only; no production code changes.

1. `TestTimerReset.test_timer_reset_extends_accumulation_window`
   Guards the watcher's mid-sleep restart in `_batch_watcher_loop` (the `if self._batch_wakeup.is_set(): self._batch_wakeup.clear(); continue` block in `openfilter/filter_runtime/filter.py`). A frame arriving while the watcher is already sleeping must extend the accumulation window rather than trigger a premature flush at the original deadline.

2. `TestFiniShutdownFlush.test_fini_drains_pending_results`
   Guards the `_batch_pending_results` drain in `fini()` (the `if self._batch_pending_results: ... self.mq.send(pending, POLL_TIMEOUT_MS)` block). Processed results stashed by `_process_frames_batched` but not yet consumed by `loop_once` must be flushed on shutdown instead of being dropped.

3. `TestLoopOncePendingResultsDrain.test_loop_once_sends_all_batch_results`
   Guards the `_batch_pending_results` drain in `loop_once` (the `if self._batch_pending_results: for pending in ...: self._send_frames(...)` block that runs before the final-result send). When `_execute_batch` returns `N > 1` results for a full batch, all `N` must reach `mq.send` in input order; the current path sends `results[:-1]` via the drain and `results[-1]` via the normal return path.

## Why is this needed?

PR #61 (frame accumulation) added three behaviors without direct regression coverage: the watcher's timer-reset path, the shutdown drain in `fini()`, and the multi-result send path in `loop_once`. Each is on a silent-failure trajectory if broken (premature flushes, dropped results on shutdown, or dropped intermediate results from a full batch). Adding focused unit tests makes future regressions surface in CI instead of production.

## How was it tested?

- `pytest tests/test_frame_accumulation.py` passes with all 28 tests green.
- Each new test targets a specific block of production code so a regression in that block surfaces as a clear test failure.

## Related Issues

- Follow-up to #61.

author: copilot
body:
Two new scripts (`dml_causal_metrics.py`, `run_monte_carlo_benchmark (2).py`) implementing the DML Control Quality Score metric contained one fatal runtime error and four logic/API issues.

## Changes

### Bug 1 — Fatal: `ModuleNotFoundError` on startup
`run_monte_carlo_benchmark (2).py` only inserted its own directory into `sys.path`, but `synthetic_dag_generator.py` lives in the sibling directory `因果的发现算法理论验证/`. Script was dead on arrival.

```python
# Before: only self-dir, import always fails
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

# After: also add sibling dir where synthetic_dag_generator actually lives
_dag_gen_dir = os.path.join(_parent_dir, "因果的发现算法理论验证")
if _dag_gen_dir not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _dag_gen_dir)
```

### Bug 2 — Graph logic: silent operator-precedence trap in `confounders`
Python's `-` (set difference) has **higher precedence** than `&` (intersection). The unparenthesized expression happened to produce a correct result for valid DAGs (mediators/colliders are T-descendants, never T-ancestors), but any future edit to the line would silently break it. Added explicit parentheses to make intent unambiguous.

```python
# Before (correct by accident, dangerous to maintain)
confounders = frozenset((t_anc & y_backdoor_anc) & all_vars - mediators - colliders)

# After (explicit, safe)
confounders = frozenset(((t_anc & y_backdoor_anc) & all_vars) - mediators - colliders)
```

### Bug 3 — API inconsistency: hardcoded threshold for true graph
`compute_dml_cqs` binarized the true graph with a hardcoded `0.05` while using the caller-supplied `threshold` for the predicted graph — asymmetric baseline when `threshold != 0.05`.

```python
# Before
adj_true_bin = binarize(adj_true, threshold=0.05)   # ignores param
adj_pred_bin = binarize(adj_pred, threshold=threshold)

# After
adj_true_bin = binarize(adj_true, threshold=threshold)
adj_pred_bin = binarize(adj_pred, threshold=threshold)
```

### Bug 4 — Type annotation: missing `Optional`
`DMLCQSResult.true_roles` / `pred_roles` default to `None` but were typed as `CausalRoles`; `Optional` was also absent from the `typing` import.

### Bug 5 — Docs: `[DML5] generate_role_distribution_report` never implemented
Docstring claimed a function that doesn't exist anywhere in the file. Removed the line to avoid misleading readers.

author: rmartz
body:
Implements the core Avalon quest loop across five action modules:

- **ProposeTeam** — Quest Leader selects the required number of team members, transitions to TeamVote
- **CastTeamVote** — Any player casts or changes an Approve/Reject vote
- **ResolveTeamVote / AdvanceFromTeamVote** — Tallies votes (approve > reject = pass); rejected vote increments consecutiveRejections, rotates leader; 5 consecutive rejections = Evil wins
- **PlayQuestCard** — Approved team members submit Success or Fail; Good-aligned players are server-side enforced to play Success only
- **ResolveQuest / AdvanceFromQuest** — Counts fails, records QuestResult (including teamPlayerIds), checks win/advance conditions; after 3 Good wins triggers Assassination phase if Assassin role exists

Also adds `teamPlayerIds` to the `QuestResult` type (required by the issue spec) and wires all actions into `AVALON_CONFIG`.

Closes #359

author: kmontag
body:
Adds a `directory` workspace type that lets macher work in arbitrary non-project directories. 

`directory` workspaces are disabled by default, as they expose the contents of all files under your buffer's `default-directory` to the LLM, which is potentially invasive when invoked from e.g. a gptel chat in the home directory. To enable them, do something like:

``` elisp
;; Try to resolve the workspace from a project.el project, otherwise fall back to a directory workspace.
(setq macher-workspace-functions '(macher-workspace-project macher-workspace-directory))
```

This PR also adds slightly more user-friendly error behavior when attempting to use macher tools with no available workspace.

Fixes #48.

body:
## Summary

- **Startup fixes**: map wildcard bind addresses (0.0.0.0, ::) to loopback for the opened browser URL; wrap bare IPv6 in RFC 3986 brackets; detect port conflicts at startup instead of silently failing; print the routable URL rather than the raw bind address
- **Filter bar redesign**: accordion rows for Models and Projects (collapsed by default), with Select all / Clear controls and sort options (Recent / A–Z); Custom date range picker with local-time-correct cutoffs; Today and 1d preset buttons
- **Project filter**: wired through all charts and tables using period-accurate data (from `daily_by_model`) rather than session lifetime totals
- **Preferences**: filter state persisted to `~/.claude/dashboard_prefs.json` via `/api/prefs`, restored on next load and merged with any URL params; JSON validated on read and write to prevent corruption
- **Timezone fix** *(pre-existing upstream bug)*: timestamps are stored in UTC but day boundaries were computed by truncating the raw ISO string, causing work done in the evening (in timezones west of UTC) to appear under the next day's date. Fixed by passing the browser's UTC offset to `/api/data` and applying it in SQL before bucketing by day; session table and CSV now display local time
- **Incremental auto-refresh**: auto-refresh now runs an incremental scan (no DB wipe) so new conversations appear automatically; configurable interval dropdown (Manual/30s/1m/5m/15m/1h, default 30s) inline in the header, saved to preferences; renamed Rescan → Refresh; added separate Rebuild DB button for full wipe; `/api/rescan` is now incremental-only, `/api/rebuild` does the full delete+rescan

author: 0xrum
body:
This pull request introduces persistent storage for memories using IndexedDB, adds support for a longer description field for each memory, and implements the ability to delete memories with a confirmation dialog. It also refactors and extends the photo details UI to accommodate these changes, ensuring that both captions and descriptions can be saved and edited. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

**Persistent Storage for Memories:**

* Added a new `storage.js` module implementing IndexedDB persistence for memories, including functions to load, save, and convert between in-memory and stored representations (`loadAllRecords`, `replaceAllRecords`, `memoryToRecord`, `recordToMemory`). (`[src/storage.jsR1-R126](diffhunk://#diff-0d294ef99fa537813aa2b3970c56b2d83c1b7077ce17c019a8f3e2b7fcf5216fR1-R126)`)
* Updated the app initialization to hydrate memories from persistent storage and persist changes after adding, editing, or deleting memories. 

**Memory Details and Editing Enhancements:**

* Added a `description` field to each memory, updated the UI in `photoDetails.html` to support editing both caption and description, and refactored the save logic to persist both fields.

**Memory Deletion Feature:**

* Implemented a delete memory workflow, including a confirmation dialog, summary of what will be deleted, and safe revocation of media URLs.

**Photo Staging and Upload Handling:**

* Refactored photo staging and upload logic to work with the new persistent storage and memory structure, ensuring that photo object URLs are normalized and cleaned up. 

**UI and Styling Improvements:**

* Added new styles for the delete button (`btn-danger`) and improved the photo details form layout.

These changes collectively enhance the user experience by making memories persistent across sessions, allowing richer memory details, and providing robust memory management features.

author: sliamh11
body:
## Summary
- **Closes the 10-PR Error & Async Discipline initiative.** PRs #1–#9 introduced the error taxonomy, bootstrap harness, async helpers, structured connect attribution, process.exit ban, datetime-TZ split, and SQL injection hardening. PR #10 is the regression gate that prevents these gains from silently eroding.
- New workflow `.github/workflows/truecourse.yml` runs `truecourse analyze --diff origin/main` on every PR; fails the build only on **NEW critical** findings; new highs warn but don't block.
- `truecourse@0.5.0` pinned in `package.json` devDependencies + four `npm run truecourse:*` scripts so contributors reproduce CI locally with the exact same version.

## How the gate works

```
1. Check out PR head (fetch-depth: 0)
2. setup-node@v6, setup-python@v6, cache .npm/_npx
3. npm ci                                          ← installs truecourse 0.5.0
4. Pre-create .truecourse/config.json with         ← skip "Run LLM rules?" prompt
   enableLlmRules: false
5. git stash → checkout origin/main → stash pop
6. npx truecourse analyze                          ← writes baseline
7. git stash → checkout PR_HEAD → stash pop
8. npx truecourse analyze --diff                   ← re-scan + compare
9. npx truecourse list --diff --all                ← surface findings in log
10. Count [critical] / [high] new lines:
    - new criticals > 0 → exit 1 (::error::)
    - new highs > 0    → ::warning:: (passes)
```

## Why a separate workflow file?
truecourse@0.5.0 was published 2026-04-19 (one day before this PR). If it crashes on edge cases or becomes flaky, the gate can be disabled by removing or commenting out the workflow file with no touch to `ci.yml`. Per Warden review.

## Why re-scan main every PR (vs committing a baseline)?
Committing `.truecourse/analyses/*.json` would mean every refactor needs an accompanying baseline-update commit (or every PR would diff against a stale baseline). The re-scan adds ~28s to CI but eliminates baseline-rot. The `.truecourse/` directory is gitignored locally (its own `.gitignore`).

## Why warn-only on new highs?
Per the original initiative ADR (`docs/decisions/error-discipline.md` §7 / "Migration plan"). Highs are useful signal but the false-positive ratio in TrueCourse's HIGH tier is meaningful (~50%; many flagged sites in PR #9 + #11 were structural-safe). Failing on highs would create review friction without a corresponding security gain. Criticals are gated because their false-positive ratio is much lower (real eval-injection / hardcoded-secret / command-injection patterns).

## What "new criticals" actually catches
Examples that would fail the gate:
- A new `eval(user_input)` site in any file
- A new hardcoded secret (API key, JWT) in code
- A new SQL injection pattern that doesn't follow the PR #9 `# safe:` annotation convention
- A new command-injection site (`subprocess.run(f"... {x} ...", shell=True)`)
- A new auth-bypass pattern (e.g., `if user.role == "admin" or True:`)

The 87 baseline criticals (mostly placeholder OAuth + intentional single-row UPDATEs) are explicitly ignored — the gate is for regressions only.

## Bootstrap self-test
This PR's workflow runs on this PR. If the workflow has a bug, the PR's own CI fails — that's the correct signal to fix it before merge. No `paths-filter` workaround.

## Files
- `.github/workflows/truecourse.yml` — new (96 lines)
- `package.json` — pin truecourse@0.5.0 + 4 npm scripts
- `package-lock.json` — auto-updated
- `docs/decisions/error-discipline.md` — new "PR #10 addendum" section + new "for future contributors" rule #8

## Local reproduction
```bash
# On main (one-time):
npx truecourse analyze

# After your changes:
npx truecourse analyze --diff
npx truecourse list --diff --all   # see the actual new findings
```

## Testing
- [x] `npx truecourse --version` → 0.5.0 (verified install)
- [x] `truecourse analyze` produces 7354 violations (87 critical, 1112 high, 4032 medium, 2123 low) — confirms the analyzer runs end-to-end on this repo
- [x] `truecourse analyze --diff` exits 0 with no new findings, exits 1 with no baseline (verified in worktree)
- [x] YAML validated via js-yaml (`node -e "require('js-yaml').load(...)"`)
- [x] Pre-creating `.truecourse/config.json` with `enableLlmRules: false` skips the interactive prompt (verified)
- [x] `python3 scripts/drift_check.py --all --base origin/main` — all checks pass (no pattern bumps needed; touched paths aren't in any pattern's governs)
- [ ] Bootstrap self-test: this PR's CI run is the gate's own first execution

## Closes initiative
- ✅ PR #1 errors taxonomy + ADR (#214)
- ✅ PR #2 bootstrap harness (#215)
- ✅ PR #3 wire bootstrap into entry points (#219)
- ✅ PR #4 async helpers (#216)
- ✅ PR #5 floating-promise migration (#221)
- ✅ PR #6 stream-error attribution (#223)
- ✅ PR #7 process.exit ESLint ban (#224)
- ✅ PR #8 datetime-TZ migration (#225)
- ✅ PR #9 SQL injection hardening (#226)
- 🟦 PR #10 TrueCourse --diff CI gate (this PR)

Plus closing-out PRs:
- ✅ #218 bootstrap mirror discipline (this branch is sequential to #228)
- ✅ #11 SQL backlog closure (#227)

author: shiba4life
body:
## Summary
- `NodeManager` now owns an `Arc<SledPool>` keyed on the storage path; it survives `invalidate_all_nodes()` so the same Sled file-lock holder is reused across cycles.
- `create_node` fetches (or lazily creates) that pool and passes it to fold_db's new `create_fold_db_with_pool_and_auth_refresh` entry point.
- `update_config` drops the pool only when the storage path actually changed.

## Why

Filed as alpha dogfood run-2 papercut: calling `/api/sync/status` within ~500ms of `/api/auth/register` returned HTTP 500 `NODE_CREATION_FAILED: Failed to open sled database after retries: could not acquire lock` ([report](https://github.com/EdgeVector/exemem-workspace/blob/master/docs/dogfood/alpha-e2e-dogfood-run-2-2026-04-19.md)).

Root cause: `register_with_exemem` spawns a background `bootstrap_from_cloud` that retains an `Arc<SledPool>`, then calls `update_config` → `invalidate_all_nodes`. Today's factory builds a fresh `SledPool` on every `create_node`, so the follow-up request raced the bootstrap task for Sled's OS file lock and lost.

## Acceptance criteria from the bug

- [x] Calling `/api/sync/status` within the first 500ms after `/api/auth/register` succeeds (unit test simulates the same pattern: invalidate while a handle is live, then immediately `get_node`).
- [x] Server log contains no `ERROR ... could not acquire lock` entries for the register → sync-status sequence (the retry path is never entered — the same pool is reused).

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --lib` — 752 passed, 0 failed (three new tests in `server::node_manager::tests`)
- [x] Manually traced: register → update_config (pool preserved) → bootstrap spawn (holds Arc) → sync-status → get_node → get_or_create_pool returns same Arc → factory reuses → no new `sled::open()` attempt on the already-open path.

## Depends on
- fold_db https://github.com/EdgeVector/fold_db/pull/562 (adds `create_fold_db_with_pool_and_auth_refresh`)

author: kent8192
body:
## Summary

- Move the `impl ResolvedUrls { pub fn ws() }` block inside `mod __namespaced_ws_resolvers` so `WsUrls.resolver` (private field) is accessible via struct-literal syntax.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Motivation and Context

The `#[routes]` macro generated `WsUrls { resolver: self }` from **outside** `__namespaced_ws_resolvers`, where `WsUrls.resolver` is a private field. This caused E0451 in any downstream crate that declares `pub mod ws_urls;` and uses `#[url_patterns(mode = ws)]`.

The HTTP counterpart (`urls.server()`) already places `impl ResolvedUrls { fn server() }` **inside** `__namespaced_resolvers` — giving it access to `ServerUrls.resolver`. This PR applies the same pattern for `WsUrls`.

Fixes #3834

## How Was This Tested?

- `cargo check --workspace` in the fix worktree passes cleanly.
- End-to-end verified in `reinhardt-cloud` dashboard migration: adding `ws_urls.rs` with `#[url_patterns(InstalledApp::auth, mode = ws)]` now compiles after `cargo update -p reinhardt-web`.

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines

- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-features` passes
- [ ] Tests cover the fix (trybuild test for ws mode E0451 can be added as follow-up)

ats watch ./my-project --skip e2e,security --debounce 1000

author: aaronpilk
body:
## Summary

Fourth engine in the router. Mirror of `ClaudeCodeBridge` but driving OpenAI's `codex exec`. Runs bill against your ChatGPT subscription when `codex login` is done, so it's the OpenAI-side analogue to the Claude-subscription savings we unlocked in PR #40.

### Invocation

```
codex exec
  --full-auto                            # workspace-write + on-request approvals
  [--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox]  # opt-in via settings
  [--sandbox read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access]
  [--model <name>]
  [--ephemeral]                          # don't persist sessions to disk
  [--cd <repo_path>]
  [--output-last-message <tempfile>]
  <goal>
```

### Design decisions

- **`--full-auto` is the default** (workspace-write + on-request) — same rationale as Claude Code's `bypassPermissions`: PILK already held a task-level approval so per-tool prompts would stall. Users who want the safer posture set `codex_sandbox_mode=read-only`. Users who want YOLO set `codex_yolo=true`.
- **Output via `--output-last-message <tempfile>`** — cleaner than stream-parsing `--json`. Engine reads the file, returns contents as `detail`. Falls back to stdout if the file isn't written (older CLI).
- **`--ephemeral`** — no session persistence, since PILK's plan store owns run history.
- **Tempfile cleanup** — happens in `finally` so failed runs don't leave orphans in `/tmp`.

### New env vars (all optional)

- `PILK_CODEX_BINARY` (default `codex`)
- `PILK_CODEX_YOLO` (default `false`)
- `PILK_CODEX_SANDBOX_MODE` (unset → `--full-auto` applies)
- `PILK_CODEX_MODEL` (unset → CLI default)

### Install (your side, post-merge)

```
npm install -g @openai/codex
codex login   # browser flow, pick your ChatGPT account
```

Then `/#/settings → Coding Engines → Refresh` — new **OpenAI Codex (local)** card flips to AVAILABLE.

## Test plan

- [x] 8 new tests, all offline (no real subprocess): missing binary / healthy probe / happy-path with output-file reading / yolo replaces `--full-auto` / explicit sandbox replaces `--full-auto` / model forwarding / non-zero exit surfaces stderr / run timeout
- [x] Full suite: **753 passed**, 0 failed
- [x] `ruff check` clean

## Router note

The router picks engines by availability + task scope. With Codex available you now have:

1. **Claude Code** — primary, subscription-billed, most capable
2. **Codex** — fallback or operator-preferred for Python/data tasks
3. **Agent SDK** — API-billed, read-only file access, runs on Railway
4. **API** — always-available bare-API draft

Per-task engine preference is already supported via `CodeTask.prefer_engine` — we can wire a preference toggle into the UI later if you want.

Reference: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference

body:
## Summary

Makes the `RenameModel` migration operation a no-op when the model already has a custom `db_table` defined. This prevents unnecessary database operations that can cause performance issues and unwanted side effects.

## Changes

- Modified `RenameModel.database_forwards()` and `RenameModel.database_backwards()` methods to check if the model has a custom `db_table` option
- When `db_table` is present, the operation now returns early without executing any database schema changes
- The model name is still updated in the migration state, preserving the logical rename while avoiding physical database operations
- Added comprehensive test coverage to verify the no-op behavior

## Testing

- Added test case `test_rename_model_with_db_table_noop` that verifies no SQL statements are generated when renaming a model with custom `db_table`
- Verified that the model name is still properly updated in the migration state
- Tested on both PostgreSQL and SQLite backends to ensure:
  - PostgreSQL: No foreign key constraints are dropped and recreated
  - SQLite: No table recreation occurs
- All existing migration operation tests continue to pass

Closes #606

author: cokobah16-creator
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent transient/runtime failures in duplicate detection or conflict persistence from being misclassified as "skipped" records so scans don't falsely report success. 
- Only intentionally skip records with invalid patient data (e.g., bad DOB or missing names) while letting operational errors bubble up so the dashboard can surface real failures.

### Description
- Reworked `scanForDuplicates` in `src/services/conflictQueue.ts` to remove the broad catch that previously converted all runtime errors into `skipped` counts. 
- Added explicit record validation (DOB / givenName / familyName) that increments `skipped` and emits a structured `logger.warn` when data is invalid. 
- Left calls to `patientDeduplication.findDuplicates`, `checkExistingConflict`, and `createConflict` unwrapped so operational/database errors propagate to callers. 
- Preserved periodic yielding (`setTimeout(..., 0)` every 10 records) to keep large scans responsive and retained the original `{ found, skipped }` return shape.

### Testing
- `npx tsc-files --noEmit src/services/conflictQueue.ts` was run and completed successfully for the modified file. 
- A full repo typecheck via `npm run typecheck` was attempted but failed due to pre-existing unrelated JSX/TSX syntax errors in other files (`PatientMessagesPanel.tsx` and `PatientLogin.tsx`), so full-project typechecking could not be completed here. 
- No behavioral/unit tests were changed; the change is limited to error-handling semantics in the duplicate-scan flow and validated with the file-level type check above.

author: fenghaitao
body:
💡 What: Implemented lazy-cached `Prompt` builder in `Generator` and optimized the call pipeline to avoid double-rendering the prompt.
🎯 Why: `Prompt` instantiation was expensive (~3.5ms for large templates) due to Jinja2 template parsing, and the prompt was unnecessarily rendered twice per call, adding redundant overhead.
📊 Impact: Reduces `Generator.call` local processing latency from ~2.4ms to ~0.19ms for small templates (approx. 12x speedup). For large templates, it eliminates the ~3.5ms instantiation overhead on subsequent calls.
🔬 Measurement: Verified with benchmark scripts using a `MockModelClient` and confirmed no regressions by running `pytest adalflow/tests/test_generator.py`.

author: erickaakcire
body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                                        
   
  Pages backwards through ChatGPT's `/backend-api/conversations` endpoint                                                                                           
  until a conversation's `update_time` is older than the lookback cutoff
  (or a hard page-count cap is reached). Previously the spider only
  fetched the first page (~28 most recent).

  The cutoff is anchored at install-time (`installTime − lookback_days`),
  not at `now`, so the pre-study buffer stays fixed for the duration of
  the study instead of sliding forward and silently dropping older
  conversations as time passes.

  Falls back to `now − lookback_days` when install time isn't known
  (e.g. rex-dev-extension).

  ## Configuration

  Three new server-config knobs under `spider.chatgpt`:
  - `lookback_days` (default 30)
  - `max_index_pages` (default 50, hard cap on paging loop)
  - `sleep_delay_ms` (default 10000, throttle between fetches)

body:
## Resumo

Corrige três bugs reportados pelo tester após a sessão de Unity Relay, e adiciona robustez ao sistema de Relay para builds em máquinas diferentes.

### Bugs corrigidos

- **Loop LobbyScene → Menu** (`LobbySceneUI.cs`): `VoltarParaMenu()` só trocava painel interno. Adicionado `IrParaMenuPrincipal()` que sai do lobby EOS, reseta o modo de jogo e carrega a `MenuScene` de verdade. Botão na cena pode ser nomeado `BtnVoltarMenuPrincipal`, `VoltarMenuPrincipal` ou `BtnMenu`.
- **Botão Iniciar sumia / só Samurai disponível após lobby** (`GameModeManager.cs`, `MenuManager.cs`): `CurrentMode` ficava como `Multiplayer` ao sair do lobby. `ChangeScene()` agora chama `ReturnToSingleplayer()` ao voltar para o menu.
- **Samurai duplicado no grid** (`GameDataManager.cs`): `Awake()` agora usa `HashSet<string>` para deduplicar `bibliotecaOriginalPersonagens`, ignorando entradas repetidas com warning no log.

### Melhorias de robustez (Relay / UGS)

- **`UGSBootstrap.cs`**: `SignInAnonymouslyAsync` agora faz até 3 tentativas com backoff exponencial (1 s → 2 s → 4 s) antes de desistir. Impede que falha transitória de rede trave o Relay definitivamente.
- **`LobbyManager.cs` — `ConnectClientViaRelayCoroutine`**: `JoinAllocationAsync` agora tenta 3 vezes (0 s, 1 s, 2 s de intervalo). Cobre drops temporários ao servidor de Relay.
- **`PlayerNetworkSetup.cs`**: Timeout do `PlayerIdentityBridge` aumentado de 2 s para 5 s; adicionado guard para `userId` EOS vazio (previne `RegisterPlayerServerRpc` com string vazia).

## Plano de testes

- [ ] LobbyScene → clicar botão "Voltar ao Menu" → deve carregar `MenuScene` sem loop
- [ ] Lobby → Sair → Menu → Jogar Solo → `EscolherPersonagem`: botão Iniciar visível, todos os personagens sem duplicata
- [ ] MPPM no editor: dois Virtual Players conectam, jogam, retornam ao menu sem problemas
- [ ] Build no mesmo PC: Host + Client via Relay conectam com sucesso
- [ ] Builds em PCs diferentes: Relay funciona; se Relay tiver latência, retry aparece no log e conexão completa

author: jessdf08
body:
Restores sorting images by `lastModified` (screenshot timestamp) without the iOS performance problem.

Previously the sort comparator called `f.lastModified` inside each comparison, triggering O(n log n) Photos bridge I/O calls on iOS. Fix: read all `lastModified` values in one O(n) `map` pass, then sort by the cached values — bridge I/O is now proportional to file count only.

author: marcusabisror
body:
### Motivation
- Improve usability on phones by providing a responsive layout and on-screen directional controls with large tap targets and safe-area padding. 
- Preserve the existing desktop experience while preventing layout overflow on narrow viewports. 
- Deliver a compact D-pad style control pad below the board for touch input without adding swipe gestures. 

### Description
- Added a viewport meta tag and wrapped the page content in a centered `#app` container to constrain and center the UI on small screens. 
- Refactored controls and status areas to use responsive grid and flex rules (`#controls`, `#top-bar`, `#top-bar-right`) so items wrap cleanly on phones while keeping the desktop layout intact. 
- Made the board responsive by replacing the fixed inline sizing with a `#game-wrapper` that uses constrained `width`, `max-width` and `aspect-ratio: 1 / 1` so the canvas scales without overflow. 
- Replaced the previous stacked touch rows with a compact 3x3 D-pad (`.dpad`) HTML/CSS layout rendered below the board on small screens and improved touch handling by wiring both `click` and `pointerdown` events to directional buttons (handlers call `queueDirectionByName`); keyboard controls remain unchanged and no swipe controls were added. 

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` to verify the diff had no whitespace or diff-check issues, and it completed successfully.

## What
Fix path issues to build on any general machine.

### Issue 1: Absolute symlinks in local registry
`generate_registry.py` used `.resolve()` to create symlinks, producing absolute paths baked to `/home/blorente/...`. Changed to `os.path.relpath()` for portable relative symlinks. All 28 existing symlinks converted.

`generate_registry.py` called `shutil.rmtree(MODULES_DIR)` which nuked the entire modules directory, including the manually-committed `rules_go` entry (with real tarball references and patches). Changed to only remove entries where `MODULE.bazel` is a symlink (i.e., generated entries).

### Issue 3: rules_go patch filename mismatch
`source.json` references `0003_add_execroot_relative_includes_to_cgo_actions.patch` but the actual file had a `_pr_4583` suffix. Renamed to match.

## Testing
The local registry resolves correctly on any machine and `rules_go` fetches its patches without error.

body:
## What

Release cut merging the idempotent workflow fix (#391) into main.

| Source | Summary |
|---|---|
| #391 | `fix(workflow): make post-release-develop-reset idempotent` |

## Why

Previous release (#389) landed the fixed workflow but it still failed on its first real run because `delete_branch_on_merge: true` auto-deletes develop the instant a release PR merges — before the workflow fires. The delete step then got 422. This release makes the workflow handle the missing-develop case as a normal path.

## Who

- Author: single-maintainer release cut.
- Reviewers: self-review sufficient.

## When

- Target: immediate merge on CI green. The merge will trigger the workflow; expected behaviour is: develop auto-deleted by the merge → workflow's compare step sees develop missing → create-only branch fires → develop ends up at main's SHA.

## Where

- `.github/workflows/post-release-develop-reset.yml`
- `docs/branching-strategy.md` §6

## How

### Testing Done

- YAML validated.
- develop and main are currently aligned.
- Manual API equivalent was verified in prior recovery.

### Test Plan for Reviewers

1. Wait for CI green.
2. Squash merge.
3. Observe workflow run on the resulting main push.
4. Expected: develop is auto-deleted by merge, workflow logs "develop is missing — will create fresh", POSTs refs, ends with develop at main's SHA.

### Breaking Changes

None.

Revert this PR. Workflow resumes at the non-idempotent state; manual fallback remains documented.

author: singlerider
body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** \`master\`
- **What changed and why:** Added \`[target.aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu]\` linker entry to \`.cargo/config.toml\` pointing to \`aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc\`. Without this, cargo's default lld linker attempts to link ARM64 objects against x86_64 ELF, failing immediately. This unblocks native cross-compilation to ARM64 Linux (Raspberry Pi 4/5, AWS Graviton) without requiring \`cross\` or Docker.
- **Scope boundary:** Dev tooling only — no source, CI, or runtime changes. Does not affect any existing build targets.
- **Blast radius:** None for existing users. Contributors without \`aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc\` installed will get a clear missing-tool error rather than a silent wrong-architecture link failure.
- **Linked issue(s):** N/A. Follow-up: wiki entry documenting ARM64 cross-compilation prerequisites and workflow.

**Prerequisite:** \`aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc\` must be installed before cross-compiling:
- Arch: \`sudo pacman -S aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc\`
- Debian/Ubuntu: \`sudo apt install gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu\`

Then:
```bash
rustup target add aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

## Validation Evidence (required)

- **Commands run:** Successful \`cargo build --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu\` on x86_64 host targeting Raspberry Pi 5.
- **Beyond CI — what did you manually verify?** Binary produced at \`target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/zeroclaw\`. CI does not exercise cross-compilation targets.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** \`cargo fmt\`, \`cargo clippy\`, \`cargo test\` — config-only change, no Rust source modified.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes — existing targets unaffected.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No — \`.cargo/config.toml\` is dev tooling only.

## Rollback (required for \`risk: medium\` and \`risk: high\`)

\`git revert <sha>\` — single-line config change, no side effects.

body:
Phase 2 of the PIR snapshot config-driven sync rollout. Phase 1 was the publisher CI in [vote-nullifier-pir#28](https://github.com/valargroup/vote-nullifier-pir/pull/28).

## Summary

### Backend — two service-level env vars + one runtime config endpoint

- **`SVOTE_UI_MODE`** (default `prod`) — gates developer-only widgets in the admin UI. Defaults to prod for any unset, empty, or unrecognised value so a forgotten `EnvironmentFile` in cloud-init cannot accidentally leak dev controls.
- **`SVOTE_PRECOMPUTED_BASE_URL`** (default `https://vote.fra1.digitaloceanspaces.com`) — CDN bucket origin this svoted's PIR siblings bootstrap snapshots from. Per-deployment so a staging/mirror svoted can point at an alternative bucket without forking the wallet-facing config. Trailing slashes are trimmed so consumers concat well-known subpaths (`/snapshots/<height>/…`) without doubled slashes.
- Both are resolved once at startup and exposed together via **`GET /api/ui-config`**, returning `{mode, dev_pir_controls, precomputed_base_url}`. Additive wire format — older UI builds continue to work against newer servers.

### Wallet-facing schema

- `admin.VotingConfig` (Go) and `chainApi.VotingConfig` (TS) gain optional **`snapshot_height`**, mirroring the bump in [token-holder-voting-config#4](https://github.com/valargroup/token-holder-voting-config/pull/4). Optional so older configs continue to deserialise.
- The bucket origin is deliberately *not* in this schema — it's a service-level concern, not a fleet invariant.

### UI plumbing

- New `UIConfigProvider` wraps the App tree and fetches `/api/ui-config` and `/api/voting-config` once at startup. Failures fall back to prod-safe defaults (`mode: "prod"`, null published config, null precomputed base) so an older svoted or an offline CDN cannot widen the surface.
- Context + Provider live in separate modules so Vite Fast Refresh keeps working for the Provider.
- `PIR_SNAPSHOTS_PATH = "/snapshots"` lives in `chain.ts` — the per-deployment `precomputed_base_url` names the bucket origin; the subpath under it is a fleet-wide convention owned here by the only consumer that walks it.

### `RoundEditor`

- `snapshot_height` is sourced from the published voting-config. PIR `/snapshot/status` is still polled to surface a "PIR height differs from published config" warning during deploys — the moment operators are most tempted to publish a round at a height the fleet hasn't yet caught up to.

### `SnapshotSettingsPage`

Split into two cards around the two distinct concerns:

- **Published snapshot** — always shown. Composes the manifest URL from `voting-config.snapshot_height` (what the fleet must agree on) + `/api/ui-config.precomputed_base_url` (this svoted's bucket) + `PIR_SNAPSHOTS_PATH`, fetches it from the CDN, and surfaces `created_at`, total size, publisher git ref/sha, and per-file sha256s. The displayed CDN base explicitly shows the `/snapshots` suffix so there's no ambiguity about which prefix the UI is hitting.
- **Local PIR (dev)** — the in-process `/snapshot/prepare` rebuild controls, only rendered when `SVOTE_UI_MODE=dev`. Local PIR server **status** is always shown so operators can see when a server is rebuilding without dev-mode access.

## Companion PRs

- [token-holder-voting-config#4](https://github.com/valargroup/token-holder-voting-config/pull/4) — declare `snapshot_height` in the live config.
- [vote-infrastructure#2](https://github.com/valargroup/vote-infrastructure/pull/2) — pin both env vars in cloud-init.
- Workspace `mise run start/chain` task already sets `SVOTE_UI_MODE=dev` for local development.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/admin/... ./app/...` pass
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vite build` clean
- [x] `eslint` clean on every file touched (3 pre-existing errors in untouched `App.tsx` / `store/rpc.ts` / `store/useStore.ts` remain out of scope)
- [ ] `mise run start` locally — Snapshot Settings page shows the **Local PIR (dev)** card (mise sets `SVOTE_UI_MODE=dev`); Published snapshot card fetches the manifest from the default bucket.
- [ ] `SVOTE_UI_MODE=prod mise run start` locally — Local PIR (dev) card disappears; Published snapshot card still renders.
- [ ] `SVOTE_PRECOMPUTED_BASE_URL=https://alt.example.com mise run start` locally — Published snapshot card's "CDN base" line changes accordingly.
- [ ] After vote-infrastructure#2 is merged + a host re-provisioned: `curl https://vote-chain-primary.valargroup.org/api/ui-config` returns `{"mode":"prod","dev_pir_controls":false,"precomputed_base_url":"https://vote.fra1.digitaloceanspaces.com"}`.
- [ ] After token-holder-voting-config#4 is merged: admin UI Snapshot page shows height/manifest sourced from the CDN with all-green status.

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The `@csrf_exempt` decorator was being used to bypass CSRF protection on the `demo_login` and `demo_portal_login` endpoints in `apps/auth_app/views.py`. These endpoints establish user sessions/tokens, meaning they are an authentication boundary. 
🎯 Impact: This created a Login CSRF vulnerability, which could allow an attacker to force a victim's browser to log into an attacker-controlled account without their knowledge. This can be used as a vector for further attacks or data harvesting in some scenarios.
🔧 Fix: Removed the `@csrf_exempt` decorators from these endpoints, as well as the unused import. The forms that submit to these endpoints already had the correct `{% csrf_token %}` included.

body:
## What I spotted in the screenshots
The student Hours page on mobile (Week calendar mode) shows the week of dates **twice, stacked**:
- Pill row: `Mon Apr 13 | Tue Apr 14 | Wed Apr 15 | Thu Apr 16 | Fri Apr 17 | Sat Apr 18`
- Right below, grid column headers: `MON Apr 13 | TUE Apr 14 | \u2026 | SUN Apr 19`

Same info at the same visual weight, one-on-top-of-the-other. And the pill row overflows narrow phones \u2014 Sunday was cut off.

## Fix

**Kill the redundancy where it exists:**
- Hide the pill row in Week calendar view. The grid column headers already label every day \u2014 nothing lost.
- Keep pills for **List view** (they're the day filter) and **Day calendar view** (they switch days). That's where they actually do work.

**Make the pills responsive where they remain:**
- Pills now flex-share horizontal space (`flex: 1 1 auto`) with `min-width: 48px`, so all seven fit on common phone widths without horizontal scroll.
- Kept `overflow-x: auto` as a safety net; hid the native scrollbar for a clean look.
- Tighter padding + 1px smaller font below 380px viewport for very narrow devices.

This pull request makes several updates to `cal.py` to improve sampling, batching, and logging during trace processing. The changes focus on making the sampling logic clearer, increasing batch size, and adding ETA (estimated time remaining) calculations to improve user feedback during long-running operations. * Added ETA (estimated time remaining) calculation and display for batch processing, giving users better feedback on progress.

body:
## Story
[S2-022] Implement AI Cover Letter Draft from Profile and Job Context

## What This PR Does
Implements the AI cover letter generator on the Document Library page.
Users can select any active job from their pipeline and generate a
tailored cover letter draft using their profile data and the job
details. The generation is powered by the Gemini 2.5 Flash API. The
draft is returned as an editable textarea so users can refine it before
copying or sending. The output is clearly labelled as an AI-generated
draft per S1-004.

## Changes
- Created src/app/api/ai/generate-cover-letter/route.ts — protected
  POST route that verifies session, fetches profile and job server-side,
  constructs the Gemini prompt, calls the API, and returns the draft.
  The API key is read from environment variables and never exposed to
  the client. user_id always comes from the session per S1-003 §5.4.
- Created src/components/documents/CoverLetterGenerator.tsx — UI
  component with job selector dropdown, generate button, loading
  skeletons, editable draft output, copy to clipboard, and regenerate
  button. Only jobId is sent from the client — all profile and job
  data is fetched server-side.
- Updated src/app/(app)/documents/page.tsx — replaced the placeholder
  page with the Document Library layout hosting the CoverLetterGenerator

## Tech Spec Sections Impacted
TECH-SPEC.md §3 (Data Ownership), §4 (API & Error Handling),
§5 (UI Implementation Standards), §7 (AI Generation Workflows)

## Environment Variables Required
GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in .env.local for local development.
This key must also be added to the deployment environment variables
before deploying to production.

## Security / Ownership Impact
The API route calls supabase.auth.getUser() as the first action.
Both the profile and job records are fetched server-side using the
verified session user.id — the client only sends the jobId. Ownership
of the job is verified via getJobById which includes .eq('user_id',
userId). The Gemini API key is stored in environment variables and
never sent to the client per S1-003 §8.1. Non-owners receive 404,
never 403, per S1-003 §5.5.

- [x] Draft is editable before copying
- [x] Copy to clipboard works correctly
- [x] Regenerate button works
- [x] Error state shows when generation fails

author: chie4hao
body:
**Description**
In general_work(), the tracking path calls ml_sync() with lookup_start = d_cp_start + 8. The internal buffers d_norm and d_corr are sized for lookup_start <= 2*fft_length + cp_length - 1 (4159 in 2K mode). However d_cp_start can reach 4153 after initial acquisition, making d_cp_start + 8 = 4161 and writing 2 elements past the end of the heap buffer. With a weak/noisy signal d_cp_start drifts further, causing double free or corruption (SIGABRT) at a data-dependent position in the input stream.
Fix: check that d_cp_start + 8 is within bounds before the narrow tracking search. If not, skip to the existing full-range retry which resets d_cp_start to a valid value.
**Related Issue**
None
**Which blocks/areas does this affect?**
gr-dtv: dvbt_ofdm_sym_acquisition
**Testing Done**
Reproduced the crash with a real DVB-T 2K signal recording that drops to noise midway. After the fix the crash no longer occurs.

`AggregateJoinPushDownRule` matched the MV's base table against scan tables using `Table.getId()`. ## Summary

**DRC-3258 — Backend: Server-side merged lineage**
- New Pydantic models: `MergedNode`, `MergedEdge`, `MergedLineage` in `recce/models/types.py`
- New `build_merged_lineage(LineageDiff) → MergedLineage` in `recce/models/lineage.py` — merges base+current nodes, computes edges from dual parent_maps, bakes diff into nodes
- `/api/info` now returns `{ nodes, edges, metadata }` instead of `{ base, current, diff }` for the lineage key
- Removed superseded `_strip_outbound_node()` and `_strip_outbound_lineage()` (Phase I, DRC-3263)
- Unchanged nodes/edges omit `change_status` from JSON via `exclude_none=True` (~330 KB savings for 10K-node projects)
- Internal `LineageDiff` untouched — `/select`, CLL, MCP server, `/api/model/{id}` all unaffected

**DRC-3260 — Frontend: Consume merged lineage**
- Rewrote `buildLineageGraph()` from ~160 lines of client-side merge/diff to ~40 lines of trivial mapping
- Removed `LineageFrom` type, `node.data.from`, and `node.data.data.base/current` from the graph model
- Added `schema` and `materialized` fields directly on `LineageGraphNode.data` (from merged response)
- Updated `toReactFlow()` and `toReactFlowBasic()` sort logic: `from` → `changeStatus`
- Migrated 20+ components from inline `node.data.data.base/current` to:
  - Merged node fields (`schema`, `materialized`, `changeStatus`, `change.columns`) for simple lookups
  - On-demand `/api/model/{id}` fetch via React Query for detail data (columns, raw_code, primary_key)
- Updated `NodeView`, `NodeSqlView` to accept `modelDetail` prop; wrappers (`NodeViewOss`, `NodeSqlViewOss`) fetch on-demand
- Updated `SchemaSummary`, `SchemaDiffView`, `GraphNodeOss` to use `change.columns` for schema change detection
- Updated `useModelColumns` to always use API fetch (no inline extraction)
- Updated all 40+ test and storybook fixture files

Improvement

- [x] 4 new frontend unit tests for rewritten `buildLineageGraph`

- **Backend:** `MergedNode` uses `extra="ignore"` so raw dbt manifest node dicts can be unpacked directly. `build_merged_lineage()` prefers current node metadata, falls back to base for removed nodes.
- **Frontend:** Components needing column/raw_code data now fetch via `/api/model/{id}` with 5-min React Query cache. `QueryForm` column autocomplete is temporarily empty (cross-model scan not feasible without inline data). `useMultiNodesAction` value diff primary_key detection deferred to on-demand fetch.
- **Breaking:** This is a Phase II breaking API change. Cloud frontend (DRC-3266) and Cloud backend (DRC-3259) will be updated separately.

author: groupsmix
body:
## Summary

Closes the soft-fail production env behaviour called out in SECURITY-AUDIT.md finding #4 and the related #1 tasks. Production misconfiguration now fails fast with a clear, operator-actionable error instead of silently degrading into a placeholder Supabase client that "succeeds" against a non-existent backend.

### 1.1 Canonical list of required prod env vars

Centralised in the new `lib/server-env.ts` with an owner file and description for every entry:

| Variable | Owner file | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `lib/supabase-server.ts` | Supabase project URL |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | `lib/supabase-server.ts` | Supabase anon/public key |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | `lib/supabase-server.ts` | Service role key (bypasses RLS, server-only) |
| `JWT_SECRET` | `lib/auth.ts` | Admin JWT + content preview token signing |
| `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` | `lib/internal-auth.ts` | Middleware to `/api/internal/*` shared secret |
| `CRON_SECRET` | `lib/cron-auth.ts` | `Authorization: Bearer` secret for scheduled cron job endpoints |

Recommended-but-not-required (warn only in prod): `RESEND_API_KEY`, `SENTRY_DSN`.

Preview tokens (`lib/preview-token.ts`) reuse `JWT_SECRET`, so no separate preview env var is needed. `RATE_LIMIT_KV` is a Cloudflare runtime binding (not a string env var) and is still validated separately in `instrumentation.ts`.

### 1.2 `requireEnvInProduction` now throws (`lib/env.ts`)

- In production runtime (`NODE_ENV === "production"` and `NEXT_PHASE` not set) a missing or whitespace-only value now throws an `Error` whose message names the variable.
- During `next build` (`NEXT_PHASE` set) or non-prod environments, the fallback is still returned so local dev and CI build remain unaffected.
- The `fallback` parameter is now optional (defaults to `""`).

### 1.3 Remove placeholder Supabase client behaviour (`lib/supabase-server.ts`)

- Deleted the `createClient("https://placeholder.supabase.co", "placeholder-key")` fallbacks in both `getServiceClient()` and `getAnonClient()`.
- Broken config now propagates the throw from `requireEnvInProduction`, which is caught by the API route / handler and returns a 500 — the correct behaviour for "server is misconfigured".
- `grep placeholder.supabase.co lib/supabase-server.ts` now returns zero matches.

> Note: `lib/supabase.ts` (browser client) still has a `placeholder.supabase.co` fallback because it is instantiated at module load on the client and cannot throw during build without breaking the browser bundle. That file is out of scope for this ticket — the spec explicitly named `lib/supabase-server.ts`.

### 1.4 Boot-time validator (`instrumentation.ts`)

- Reworked to use `validateServerEnv()` from `lib/server-env.ts` as the single source of truth so the required/recommended lists can't drift between the validator and tests.
- `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` and `CRON_SECRET` are now validated at boot (previously only warned or unvalidated).
- In production runtime the app throws with a formatted block that names every missing variable and points operators at `.env.example`.

### 1.5 Tests

Three new test files, 18 new test cases, all passing:

- `__tests__/env.test.ts` — `requireEnvInProduction` returns values, dev fallback works, build-phase fallback works, prod runtime throws for missing and whitespace-only, no silent fallback in prod.
- `__tests__/server-env.test.ts` — canonical list contains every required var, owner metadata present, recommended disjoint from required, `collectMissingEnv`/`validateServerEnv` behave correctly, formatted message names every missing var.
- `__tests__/supabase-server.test.ts` — `getServiceClient`/`getAnonClient` throw in prod when env is missing, do not construct clients against `placeholder.supabase.co`, still work with safe local dev values.

### CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `lighthouse.yml` now also set placeholder `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` and `CRON_SECRET` so build-phase instrumentation has no missing-var warnings to emit.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Confirm the production deploy already has `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` and `CRON_SECRET` set (Cloudflare Worker secrets). If not, deploying this PR will crash the worker on startup — that is the intended behaviour of this change, but you want to set those secrets *before* merging so there is no window of downtime.
- [ ] Verify the `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, and `JWT_SECRET` entries in Cloudflare Worker secrets are not empty.
- [ ] Smoke-test one admin route (e.g. `/admin/login`) in staging after deploy to confirm the boot-time validator runs clean and normal traffic still works.
- [ ] Decide whether to follow up with a similar hard-fail for `lib/supabase.ts` (browser client) and the `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN` dev fallback in `lib/internal-auth.ts` (audit findings #4 and #5) — out of scope here but the same pattern applies.

### Notes

- Local verification: `npm run lint` (0 errors, pre-existing warnings only), `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (396 passed / 44 skipped), `npm run build` all pass.
- Branch follows the `feat/` convention from CONTRIBUTING.md.

author: rednotfound
body:
Introduces a deploy/ subdirectory with everything needed to deploy Spatial CMS to AWS. Designed as a reusable kit — any team can fork this repo and deploy their own independent stack.

Architecture:
- Compute: Lightsail VM (~$10/mo, can be stopped when idle)
- Data: RDS Postgres 17 + PostGIS (~$15/mo, managed backups)
- Reverse proxy: Caddy with automatic Let's Encrypt HTTPS
- Auth: Keycloak (retained, not Cognito — keeps vendor neutral and fits single-tenant model)

Not deployed: viewer, workbench, directus (sample apps and dev tools, not part of the product itself).

Files added:
- deploy/README.md — complete step-by-step guide (AWS account setup, RDS, domain, Lightsail VM, deploy, verify, backup/recovery drill)
- deploy/docker-compose.deploy.yml — 3-service production compose
- deploy/Caddyfile — reverse proxy config (Keycloak paths + CMS)
- deploy/.env.example — environment variables template
- deploy/scripts/setup-rds.sh — RDS initialization (DBs + PostGIS)
- deploy/scripts/deploy.sh — one-command deploy/update on the VM

Cost: ~$25/mo running, ~$5/mo idle. Target: demo and MVP.

This PR addresses multiple requests related to the application's architecture, security, and usability. 

Key changes include:
1. **Security & Auth:** Upgraded the legacy password checker to use secure, signed HttpOnly cookies via `cookie-parser`. Unauthenticated API and Proxy endpoints now explicitly reject requests with a `401 Unauthorized`.
2. **Architecture:** Re-arranged Express middleware to properly parse forms *before* the authentication check, and explicitly re-added the `express.json({ limit: "50mb" })` middleware after the auth check to ensure emulator save states continue to work.
3. **Documentation:** Added comprehensive JSDoc comments to `src/index.js` (for proxy routing and streaming logic), `src/auth.js` (for the gateway payload), and `public/omni.js` (for frontend architecture). Also overhauled the `README.md` to be professional and include explicit deployment steps for Docker, HuggingFace, and Replit.

Phase 2 of the PIR snapshot config-driven sync rollout.

## Summary

- `snapshot_height: 3312890` — the Orchard nullifier-tree snapshot the PIR fleet must converge on for the next voting round. This is the height Phase 1's [`publish-snapshot.yml`](https://github.com/valargroup/vote-nullifier-pir/actions/workflows/publish-snapshot.yml) workflow published to DigitalOcean Spaces.
- README schema row updated with the constraints operators and wallet devs care about: multiple of 10, PIR servers must serve exactly this height, admin UI auto-populates round drafts from it.

The bucket origin for pre-computed snapshots is intentionally **not** part of this schema. It's a per-deployment service concern — each svoted resolves it from `SVOTE_PRECOMPUTED_BASE_URL` (see [vote-sdk#118](https://github.com/valargroup/vote-sdk/pull/118)) so a staging or mirror deployment can point at an alternative bucket without forking the wallet-facing config.

## Companion PRs

- [vote-sdk#118](https://github.com/valargroup/vote-sdk/pull/118) — svoted reads `snapshot_height`; admin UI sources round-draft heights from it and fetches the manifest for operator visibility.
- [vote-infrastructure#2](https://github.com/valargroup/vote-infrastructure/pull/2) — pin `SVOTE_UI_MODE=prod` and `SVOTE_PRECOMPUTED_BASE_URL=…` in cloud-init.

author: sameersegal
body:
…s/shared

Before: Role, ScopeLevel, Capability, CAPABILITIES_BY_ROLE, and the auth-user shape were declared on both sides — once in apps/api/src/{types,policy}.ts and again in apps/web/src/api.ts. 25 lines duplicated across two boundaries with nothing stopping them from drifting.

Now: a single pnpm workspace package `@navsahyog/shared` owns the wire-contract types. Both apps import from it.

Package layout:
- packages/shared/src/roles.ts      — Role, ScopeLevel
- packages/shared/src/capabilities.ts — Capability, matrix,
  capabilitiesFor(), can() (pure, for wire-shape users)
- packages/shared/src/user.ts       — BaseUser (DB shape),
  AuthUser (wire shape with capabilities)
- packages/shared/src/index.ts      — barrel

No build step: `main` and `exports` point at the TS source. Vite + wrangler both compile TS from workspace deps natively, so the lock-in is type-only.

Server (apps/api):
- types.ts becomes a thin shim: SessionUser = BaseUser, plus the Bindings / Variables types that are server-specific.
- policy.ts keeps the Hono middleware (requireCap) and the server-flavoured can(user, cap) that takes {role} and looks up the matrix. Matrix itself now imported from shared.
- Adds `@navsahyog/shared` as a workspace:* dep.

Web (apps/web):
- api.ts re-exports Role, Capability, User (= AuthUser), can from shared. Response-body shapes (Village, Child, …) stay local until they have a reason to share.

pnpm-workspace.yaml now includes packages/*.

Verified: all 35 tests pass (API 24 + Web 11), both apps typecheck and build clean. Web bundle: 192 KiB / 61 KiB gzipped (unchanged — shared re-exports compile to the same literals).

This is types only. Runtime validation (zod / valibot) stays deferred until L2 introduces a nested request shape that makes hand-rolled checks painful.

author: copilot
body:
The splash screen (`z-index: 9999`) would freeze indefinitely if the `<script type="module">` failed to execute (SyntaxError, failed ESM import), because its own dismissal timer never ran. Even a working login screen underneath was unreachable.

## Changes

### Plain-script splash safety timer
Added to the existing non-module `<script>` (dark-mode init block) — runs unconditionally outside the module. Forces splash removal after 8 s; a no-op on normal boots since the module clears it at ~4.2 s.

```js
var SPLASH_SAFETY_MS = 8000;
setTimeout(function() {
  var splash = document.getElementById('splashScreen');
  if (splash) {
    splash.classList.add('splash-done');
    setTimeout(function() { if (splash.parentNode) splash.parentNode.removeChild(splash); }, 750);
  }
}, SPLASH_SAFETY_MS);
```

### `showLoginFallback()` helper + `bootFromSession` outer catch
Extracted a shared `showLoginFallback()` (DOM-safe, logs errors). Added an outer `catch(fatalErr)` layer to `bootFromSession` — any error thrown before the app shell is revealed (e.g. from `updateLastSeen`, DOM calls) now falls back to the login screen instead of a blank/stuck state.

### Top-level boot try/catch with guaranteed `onAuthStateChange` registration
Wrapped `getSession()` + initial `bootFromSession()` in a try/catch. `onAuthStateChange` moved outside the try so it is **always registered** even if the initial boot throws — the user can always log in manually.

```js
let _initialUserId = null;
try {
  const { data: initial } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
  _initialUserId = initial?.session?.user?.id || null;
  await bootFromSession(initial.session);
} catch (bootErr) {
  console.error('[boot] Erreur critique au démarrage, affichage login:', bootErr);
  showLoginFallback();
}
supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(async (event, session) => { … });
```
