author: jpaljasma
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the cloud/local telemetry path and fixes the cloud-profile live data issues that were causing device cards and detail pages to show paused or zeroed realtime state.

Key changes:
- add self-healing JetStream consumer supervision for projection, archive, rollup, inference, and gap-repair workers
- keep the frontend k3d/cloud switch and DPU live-state improvements in the same branch
- improve DPU solar history fallback for sparse cloud samples
- fix hosted cloud public-app CORS so `https://localhost` can use the cloud profile safely
- fix the hosted cloud realtime gateway gRPC upstream so websocket subscriptions resolve against the cloud gRPC API
- add regression tests so cloud public-app CORS and cloud realtime/public upstream wiring do not drift silently again

## Why

The main production issue was not only UI interpretation. The cloud data path had several real reliability problems:
- downstream JetStream consumers could disappear after disruption and not recover without manual restarts
- localhost -> cloud public-app CORS dropped `https://localhost`
- the hosted realtime gateway was pointed at the wrong gRPC service name in cloud, which broke live websocket subscriptions even while the rest of the app could still load

This PR fixes those failure modes and keeps the related frontend changes together so the cloud profile is usable end to end.

## Validation

Automated validation run on this branch:
- `go test ./internal/telemetrybus ./internal/projectionworker ./internal/archiveworker ./internal/rollupworker ./internal/inference ./internal/gaprepair`
- `go test -race ./internal/telemetrybus ./internal/projectionworker ./internal/archiveworker ./internal/rollupworker ./internal/inference ./internal/gaprepair`
- `npm run -w apps/universal test -- src/features/telemetry/engine/TelemetryEngine.test.ts`
- `npm run -w apps/pulse-platform test -- test/solar_view.test.ts`
- `npm run -w apps/pulse-platform test -- test/config.test.ts`
- `npm run -w apps/universal typecheck`
- `npm run -w apps/universal lint`
- `npm run -w apps/pulse-platform typecheck`
- `make lint`

Live verification performed during rollout:
- cloud services rolled to `cloud-go1262-20260420-selfheal1`
- cloud public app rolled to `cloud-platform-20260420-selfheal1`
- localhost local-deploy completed successfully
- `https://localhost` serves the rebuilt web bundle
- `https://pulse.34.73.53.93.sslip.io` serves the rebuilt cloud bundle
- cloud JetStream consumers recovered and backlog drained to near-zero / zero
- deleting `projection-live-v1` caused the consumer to be recreated automatically without restarting the worker pod
- localhost -> cloud CORS for `/api/v1/me` and `/api/devices` now returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://localhost`

## Post-merge

After merge, the hosted Argo apps can follow `main` again.
There is one temporary operational tweak from live validation that should be reverted after merge:
- re-enable `selfHeal` on `pulse-platform-cloud`

### Motivation
- Prevent runtime failures when `memory.json` contains unexpected shapes because `_load` previously assigned raw JSON directly to `_data`, causing `add_pair` to call `extend` on non-lists. 
- Avoid sending a misleading generic error after a successful reply when a subsequent persistence failure (disk/permission) occurs because the write ran inside the same broad `try` that handles reply generation. 

### Description
- Add `_sanitize_loaded_data` to `MemoryStore` and use it from `_load` to validate that top-level keys are strings and each value is a list of `{"role": str, "text": str}` entries, dropping invalid keys/entries and applying `max_entries` during load (`ai/memory.py`).
- Treat valid JSON that is not a `dict` as empty state in `_load` to avoid leaving `_data` in a broken shape (`ai/memory.py`).
- Wrap `memory.add_pair(...)` in `text_handler` with a `try/except OSError` and log persistence errors so they do not change the user-facing outcome after `await message.answer(answer)` (`ai/main.py`).
- Changes touch `ai/memory.py` and `ai/main.py`.

body:
### Motivation
- `terminate` wurde in mehreren `pcall(...)`-Pfaden (insbesondere im Service-Manager und in einigen Services) als normaler Fehler behandelt und damit verschluckt, wodurch der ENERGY-Node nicht sauber stoppte.
- Die ENERGY-Node muss zuverlässig auf `terminate` reagieren, Services sauber herunterfahren und nützliche Laufzeit-Logs schreiben.

### Description
- Stoppt das Verschlucken von `terminate`-Fehlern, indem `is_terminate_error`/`rethrow_terminate`-Prüfungen eingeführt werden und terminate-artige Fehler aus `pcall`-Wrappers wiedergeworfen werden (`xreactor/services/service_manager.lua`, `xreactor/services/discovery_service.lua`, `xreactor/services/telemetry_service.lua`).
- Main-Loop der ENERGY-Node wechselt zu `os.pullEventRaw()` und erkennt `terminate` explizit, liefert einen geordneten Shutdown-Pfad und ruft `services:stop()` in einer neuen `shutdown(reason)`-Routine auf (`xreactor/nodes/energy/main.lua`).
- Top-Level `xpcall`-Guard um `init()` + `main_loop()` sorgt dafür, dass terminate-artige Fehler oder Laufzeitfehler nach dem geordneten Shutdown korrekt behandelt bzw. erneut geworfen werden.
- ENERGY-Logging standardmäßig aktiviert durch Setzen von `debug_logging = true` in den Node-Defaults und Default-Config, und gezielte zusätzliche Startup-/Loop-/Shutdown-Logs ergänzt (`xreactor/nodes/energy/main.lua`, `xreactor/nodes/energy/config.lua`).
- Tests ergänzt, die das Passthrough-/Propagation-Verhalten absichern: `tests/service_manager_terminate_propagation_test.lua` und `tests/service_terminate_passthrough_test.lua`.
- Manifest-Einträge/Hashes aktualisiert, damit die geänderten Dateien im Release/Update-Prozess korrekt erfasst sind (`xreactor/manifest.lua`).

### Testing
- `python3 scripts/cc_parse_guard.py --file xreactor/nodes/energy/main.lua` — bestanden.
- `python3 scripts/manifest_sync.py --write` — bestanden (Manifest synchronisiert).
- `python3 scripts/package_release.py --sync --output dist/tmp-release.zip` — bestanden (Paket gebaut, Konsistenz OK).
- Neue Lua-Regressionstests wurden hinzugefügt (`tests/service_manager_terminate_propagation_test.lua`, `tests/service_terminate_passthrough_test.lua`) but could not be executed here because `lua` is not installed in the execution environment; the test files exercise that `terminate` is rethrown and propagated.
- Bestehender Service-Manager-Backoff-Test (`tests/service_manager_backoff_test.lua`) left unchanged; environment did not run Lua tests.

author: alaister
body:
Fixes a false positive in the CREATE-TABLE-without-RLS warning modal added in #45008. The warning was firing on `CREATE FUNCTION` statements because the `SELECT..INTO` detector was matching plpgsql variable assignments inside `$$…$$` function bodies.

Reported example that triggered the modal with no table actually being created:

```sql
create or replace function schema_checks()
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
as $$
declare
  ret jsonb;
begin
  select jsonb_build_object('value', 'ok') into ret;
  return ret;
end;
$$;
```

**Changed:**
- `SQLEventParser.match()` now strips the body of `$tag$…$tag$` blocks before running detectors. Tags are kept as markers; content is blanked out so function bodies, DO blocks, and dollar-quoted string literals are never scanned as DDL.
- Updated a pre-existing parser test that asserted the buggy behaviour (it expected `CREATE TABLE fake` inside a `$$…$$` string literal to be detected — `$$…$$` is a string literal in Postgres, not DDL).

**Added:**
- Regression tests in `SQLEditor.utils.test.ts` covering: the exact reported function, DO blocks with `select into`, `create table` text inside a function body, mixed top-level `CREATE TABLE` + function with `INTO` assignments, and custom `$body$…$body$` tags.
- Parser-level regression test in `sql-event-parser.test.ts`.

## To test

- In the SQL editor, paste the function from the Slack report and run it — the RLS warning modal should not appear.
- Run `create table foo (id int8 primary key);` on its own — modal still appears as before.
- Run `create table foo (id int8); create or replace function bar() returns int language plpgsql as $$ declare v int; begin select 1 into v; return v; end; $$;` — modal should flag only `foo`, not `v`.
- Run an existing destructive query (`drop table x`) — unaffected, modal still works.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Parser no longer treats DDL/DML-like text inside PL/pgSQL functions, DO blocks, or dollar-quoted bodies (including nested/custom tags) as top-level CREATE TABLE/SELECT INTO, preventing false detections and UI warnings.

* **Tests**
  * Added unit and e2e regression tests covering dollar-quoted blocks, nested dollar tags, DO blocks, SELECT INTO inside functions, and positive controls with a real top-level CREATE TABLE.

body:
## Summary

Adds n8n 2.x stable to the docker-compose stack under a new `n8n` profile:
- Reuses the shared `postgres` service (dedicated `n8n` role/database created idempotently on first `up`)
- Owner pre-seeded via one-shot init container → first browser hit lands **directly in the editor**, no setup wizard
- Caddy site block + port publish + Cloudflare tunnel route at `https://n8n.theaustraliahack.com`

## How it works

Three services in the `n8n` profile, with a strict dependency chain:

```
postgres (healthy)
  └─ n8n-db-init   (CREATE ROLE n8n + CREATE DATABASE n8n, idempotent) ─ exits 0
     └─ n8n        (migrates schema, becomes healthy)
        └─ n8n-bootstrap   (UPDATE placeholder owner row + flip settings, idempotent) ─ exits 0
```

Schema-observation task (Task 1 in the plan) found that n8n 2.x **pre-seeds** a placeholder owner row on first migration, so bootstrap `UPDATE`s it in place rather than `INSERT`ing — keeps the auto-created `project`/`project_relation` rows consistent. See `docs/plans/n8n-schema-observations.md` for the full `\d` dumps and rationale.

## Files

**New:**
- `docker-compose/n8n/db-init.sh` — idempotent role + database creation (`postgres:16-alpine`, POSIX sh, `quote_literal` for injection safety)
- `docker-compose/n8n/bootstrap.sh` — idempotent owner seed (bcrypt via `htpasswd`, `psql -v` parameter binding)
- `docs/plans/2026-04-20-n8n-minimal-install-design.md` — design
- `docs/plans/2026-04-20-n8n-minimal-install.md` — step-by-step plan
- `docs/plans/n8n-schema-observations.md` — observed n8n 2.17.3 schema

**Modified:**
- `docker-compose/docker-compose.yaml` — three new services, `n8n_data` volume, port `5678` published for Cloudflare tunnel reachability
- `docker-compose/Caddyfile` — `n8n.theaustraliahack.com:443` internal TLS site block
- `docker-compose/.env.local.example` — `N8N_*` keys with generation commands
- `CLAUDE.md` — n8n in Service Ports table

## Deployment verified end-to-end

- [x] `docker compose --profile n8n up -d` — dependency chain completes cleanly
- [x] `n8n-db-init` logs `n8n role + database are ready`, exits 0
- [x] n8n healthy, `GET /healthz` returns `{"status":"ok"}`
- [x] `n8n-bootstrap` logs `owner seeded as adam_j_bradley@yahoo.com`, exits 0

author: lele872
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE models (e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B):

1. **Stale position IDs** — Add `shape[-1] == seq_length` check before reusing cached `_position_ids` in `LanguageModel.__call__()`
2. **gdn_sink compatibility** — Add `gdn_sink` parameter to `Qwen3_5MoeDecoderLayer.__call__()` and propagate to linear attention layer

## Problem 1: broadcast_shapes crash with stale position IDs

The Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model (MoE architecture based on `qwen3_5_moe`) crashes with:

```
ValueError: [broadcast_shapes] Shapes (1,16,60,64) and (1,1,28,64) cannot be broadcast.
```

when the `mlx_vlm.server` processes sequential requests with different token counts. The crash occurs in `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb()` during RoPE computation.

**Root cause**: `LanguageModel` caches `_position_ids` and `_rope_deltas` as instance variables that persist across independent requests since the `LanguageModel` object is reused by the server. In `LanguageModel.__call__()`, when `cache_offset == 0` (start of a new generation), the code short-circuits to reuse stale cached position_ids:

```python
if self._position_ids is not None:
    seq_length = inputs.shape[1]
    position_ids = self._position_ids[:, :, cache_offset : cache_offset + seq_length]
```

The existing check `self._position_ids.shape[1] == batch_size` (line 737) only validates the batch dimension, not the sequence dimension. When the current request has a different token count, MLX slicing silently returns a shorter array without error. This produces cos/sin tensors with the wrong sequence dimension for RoPE, causing the broadcast crash.

**Step-by-step flow**:
1. Request 1 (28 tokens): sets `self._position_ids` with shape `(3, 1, 28)`
2. Request 2 (60 tokens): enters `cache_offset==0` branch, finds `_position_ids is not None`, slices `self._position_ids[:, :, :60]` which MLX silently returns as `(3, 1, 28)` since the original array is shorter than 60
3. Wrong position IDs produce cos/sin with dimension 28 instead of 60
4. `apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb()` attempts broadcast between `(1,16,60,64)` and `(1,1,28,64)` — crash

**Fix**: Add a sequence length check:

```diff
                 if (
                     self._position_ids is not None
                     and self._position_ids.shape[1] == batch_size
+                    and self._position_ids.shape[-1] == seq_length
                 ):
```

When cached position IDs don't match the current input length, the code falls through to `get_rope_index()` which correctly recomputes them. This is complementary to the `_position_ids = None` reset introduced in commit `b97bc63` for the text-only path — while that reset handles the most common case, this shape check provides defense-in-depth protection regardless of whether the reset fires, covering edge cases like multimodal requests or batches with mixed lengths.

## Problem 2: gdn_sink incompatibility with MoE models

The current main branch passes a `gdn_sink` argument to decoder layers in `Qwen3_5Model.__call__()` (line 430). This parameter was introduced in commit `3947dd0` (Add DFlash speculative decoding) to capture intermediate Gated DeltaNet states for speculative decoding rollback.

`Qwen3_5DecoderLayer` was updated to accept and propagate `gdn_sink`:

```python
class Qwen3_5DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __call__(self, x, mask=None, cache=None, position_ids=None, gdn_sink=None):
        if self.is_linear:
            r = self.linear_attn(self.input_layernorm(x), mask, cache, gdn_sink=gdn_sink)
```

However, `Qwen3_5MoeDecoderLayer` was **not** updated, causing:

```
TypeError: Qwen3_5MoeDecoderLayer.__call__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'gdn_sink'
```

This is **blocking**: all `qwen3_5_moe`-based models (including Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and any Qwen3.5 MoE model) are completely non-functional on the current main branch. The crash occurs on the very first request.

The `qwen3_5_moe` module imports `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet` directly from `qwen3_5.language` (as `Qwen3_5MoeGatedDeltaNet`), so the linear attention layer already supports `gdn_sink` internally — only the decoder layer propagation is missing.

**Fix**: Add `gdn_sink` to `Qwen3_5MoeDecoderLayer.__call__()` and propagate to the linear attention layer:

```diff
     def __call__(
         self,
         x: mx.array,
         mask: Optional[mx.array] = None,
         cache: Optional[Any] = None,
         position_ids: Optional[mx.array] = None,
+        gdn_sink: Optional[list] = None,
     ) -> mx.array:
         if self.is_linear:
-            r = self.linear_attn(self.input_layernorm(x), mask, cache)
+            r = self.linear_attn(self.input_layernorm(x), mask, cache, gdn_sink=gdn_sink)
```

The full-attention path (`self.self_attn`) does not need `gdn_sink` since the Gated DeltaNet mechanism only operates in linear (non-full-attention) layers, consistent with the non-MoE decoder implementation.

## Testing

Verified on `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-MLX-4bit` (4-bit MLX quantization, Apple Silicon Mac with ~32GB unified memory):

**v0.4.4 with position IDs fix**:
- Single user-only request: OK
- Multi-message (system + user): OK (was crashing)
- Sequential requests with varying lengths: OK
- Short (2 tokens) followed by long (60+ tokens): OK

**Main branch with gdn_sink fix**:
- Single user-only request: OK (was crashing with TypeError)
- Multi-message (system + user): OK
- Rapid sequence of 5 requests with alternating lengths: OK
- The `_position_ids = None` reset from commit `b97bc63` correctly handles stale position state for text-only requests

Without the `gdn_sink` fix, installing from main branch crashes on the first request with `TypeError`. With the fix applied, all `qwen3_5_moe`-based models are fully functional.

## Files changed

- `mlx_vlm/models/qwen3_5/language.py` — Add `shape[-1] == seq_length` check (1 line)
- `mlx_vlm/models/qwen3_5_moe/language.py` — Add `gdn_sink` parameter and propagation (2 lines)

author: rietveldd92-crypto
body:
## Summary

- **Nieuwe module `agents/day_planner.py`** die sessies plaatst op basis van beschikbaarheid (avail-first), met harde regels die nooit stilletjes gebroken worden
- **`week_planner.build_week()`** roept `plan_days()` aan als eerste placement-pass; bij conflict valt het terug op coach-placement met warning
- **Coaches ongewijzigd** — ze leveren dag-suggesties die day_planner overschrijft (incrementele refactor, minder blast radius)

## Harde regels (afgestemd met Dennis 2026-04-20)

| Regel | Implementatie |
|---|---|
| R1. Longs (>100 min) eerst op hoogst-avail dagen | `longs_sorted` + `_rank_days()` desc |
| R2. Hards met ≥1 dag afstand van andere hard/long | `_placement_violates_hard_spacing` |
| R3. Runs nooit back-to-back (ook niet same-day 2 runs) | `_placement_violates_run_adjacency` |
| R4. Longs adjacent toegestaan als moet, niet als kan | `allow_adjacent_longs` + non-adj pool voorkeur |
| R5. Brick (run+bike zelfde dag) op al-gevulde dagen | brick-score in easy-placement |
| R6. Conflict → warning + fallback, niet silent cap | `SchedulingConflict` exception |

## Classificatie
- **long**: `duur_min > 100`
- **hard**: type/naam bevat threshold/sweetspot/vo2/interval/tempo/over_unders/cp/drempel/etc
- **easy**: rest
- Tolerance: sessie mag 10min over avail gaan (65min op 60min = OK)

## Key design decisions
- **Run-longs eerst gesorteerd** — bikes blokkeren geen downstream runs, maar runs wel. Dus run-long op earlier high-avail dag zodat zo/zaterdag vrij blijft voor runs.
- **No 2 longs same day** — expliciete check `not _has_long(d, placements)`.
- **Fallback bij conflict** — day_planner raised SchedulingConflict; week_planner prints warning + valt terug op coach-placement + oude avail-remap. User ziet reden in log, plan gaat toch door (niet-blocking voor daily workflow).

## Test plan
- [x] 20 nieuwe tests in `test_day_planner.py` — classify, long-placement, hard-spacing, run-adjacency, longs-adjacent-als-moet, brick, tolerance, edge cases
- [x] Alle 225 tests groen (was 205 + 20 nieuwe)
- [x] Live dry-run plan_week.py met realistische avail (ma/wo/zo=90, di/do=60, vr/za=240): plan voldoet aan alle regels
- [x] Live dry-run met krappe avail (60/dag): SchedulingConflict → fallback werkt correct met warning

body:
## Relevant issues

- Relates to #21345

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/test_litellm/` directory
- [x] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit`
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a Confidence Score of at least 4/5

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

### 1. Per-summary thinking blocks

Previously all reasoning summaries were concatenated into a single thinking block. This caused:
- Bold summary titles running into the previous paragraph without separation
- Under high reasoning effort (e.g. gpt-5.4 at `xhigh`), clients like Claude Code buffered all thinking content until the block closed — the UI felt stuck for 30+ seconds with no visible output

Each summary part now emits its own `content_block_start` / `content_block_delta` / `content_block_stop` cycle, so streaming clients can render each segment as soon as it completes.

### 2. Deduplicate message_start

When `response.created` fires after `message_start` has already been sent (either by an earlier `response.created` or by the `__anext__` fallback), the duplicate is now skipped. Previously this could produce two `message_start` events in a single stream.

**Files changed (2):**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.../responses_adapters/streaming_iterator.py` | Per-summary block emission + message_start dedup guard |
| `.../transformation.py` | 1-line tweak to support per-summary block indexing |

## Test plan

10 tests in `tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/test_streaming_iterator.py`:

**TestPerSummaryThinkingBlocks (6 tests):**
- Two summary parts → two independent thinking block cycles
- Single summary → exactly one cycle
- `reasoning` item.added does NOT emit content_block_start
- `reasoning` item.done does NOT emit content_block_stop
- Three summaries get monotonically increasing block indices
- Text output after reasoning gets the next sequential index

**TestDeduplicateMessageStart (4 tests):**
- Single `response.created` → one message_start
- Duplicate `response.created` → still only one
- Fallback message_start followed by `response.created` → only one
- Missing `response.created` → fallback triggers correctly

author: jpdippenaar
body:
## Summary

- Sanitize API response bodies before returning to LLM: strip Unicode attack vectors (bidi overrides, zero-width chars, Tags block, variation selectors, soft hyphen), collapse whitespace-padding runs (50+ spaces → `[WHITESPACE REMOVED]`)
- Detect injection patterns (16 regex patterns) in sanitized responses — observability only, content never suppressed
- Throttled detection logger: 1 event/hostname/60s, never logs matched content
- Optional spotlighting: wrap responses in per-request UUID sentinel tags (`config.enableSpotlighting`)
- Sanitize all user-controlled tool metadata (schema endpoint titles/descriptions/param descriptions, custom tool descriptions, auth tokens in prompt templates)

## Handoff Document

See `docs/work/handoff-feat-prompt-injection-defense.md` for full context, design decisions, and review guidance.

## Testing

- 66 new unit tests (58 for `sanitize.ts`, 8 for `detection-logger.ts`)
- All 396 tests pass (`npm test`)
- TypeScript compiles cleanly (`npm run build`)

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- Monitor logs for `[injection-defense] [...] InjectionDetected` entries — these indicate suspicious API response content
- Throttle (1/hostname/min) prevents log flooding; if a host fires repeatedly after each minute elapses, investigate the API
- No functional behavior change for clean responses — sanitization is a no-op on normal UTF-8 text

---
[![Compound Engineered](https://img.shields.io/badge/sixees-Compound_Engineered-blue)](https://github.com/sixees/sixees-marketplace)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
- Centralized constants still fragmented
  - Many numeric/list constants (50-space collapse, 200-char detection cap, 1000 description cap, 128 hostname cap, 60s throttle, binary MIME whitelist) are asserted in tests but remain module-scattered. Recent refactors reduced duplication (e.g., sanitize module, sanitizeAndDetect extraction) but a single shared constants/config hub is missing, increasing future-change friction.

- Pipeline SRP improvements and remaining local utilities
  - The sanitize+detect sequence was extracted to sanitizeAndDetect(), eliminating the prior pre/post-jq duplication and improving testability. However small predicates (isBinaryContentType) remain module-local in processor.ts and should be moved to shared utils to avoid inconsistent gating across code paths.

- Binary/content-type gating coverage and bypass risk
  - Binary MIME gating covers requested types (wasm/zip/gzip/x-gzip/x-tar/multipart/*) and is used to skip sanitization/detection for non-text responses. Because the predicate is local, some execution paths (schema-generated tools, certain save/file flows) can bypass spotlighting or sanitization; the PR documents these gaps but centralizing the gating predicate would reduce accidental bypasses.

- Spotlighting: safer sentinel format but partial application
  - Spotlighting was switched to opaque UUID-based sentinels (not XML) which reduces spoofing risk. It remains optional (enableSpotlighting) and does not apply to schema-generated tools; those coverage limits are documented. Operationally, optional spotlighting plus uneven application is an ongoing provenance/visibility risk.

- Detection-only posture with redacted, throttled logging
  - The system deliberately keeps a detection/observability-only stance (no content suppression). Logging is throttled per normalized hostname (60s) and redacted (no matched content), with a cleanup interval lifecycle implemented and tested. This design reduces runtime impact but transfers responsibility to monitoring/ops; SIEM integration must account for the documented log format.

- Regex-based detection: improved but inherently brittle
  - Detection regexes were expanded (persona takeover, "act as"/broadened variants, admin/system markers, exfil patterns) and re-run after jq decoding to close Unicode-escape bypasses. Still, static regex detection is susceptible to obfuscation (homoglyphs, encoding, novel phrasing). Additional strategy (canonicalization, ML-assisted signals, or broader canonical normalization) is recommended for obfuscation resilience.

- HTML/tag stripping gap
  - HTML comment stripping is implemented, but full HTML-tag/script/style removal and markdown image-beacon stripping were deferred and remain TODOs. These are realistic exfiltration/telemetry vectors and should be prioritized or explicitly scoped/mitigated.

- Test coverage: substantial but targeted gaps
  - Large test additions (sanitize, processor, detection-logger, jq integration, spotlighting, truncation) materially raise confidence. Missing/remaining items include dedicated jq unit tests, finalization of refactor test coverage for relocated utilities/constants, and broader obfuscation/attack-pattern tests. The size-guard early-rejection behavior is implemented and tested in processor.test.

- Maintainability and caller contract fragility
  - sanitizeDescription/sanitizeResponse centralization improves SRP and discoverability (exports added). However generateToolDefinitions/registerCustomTool intentionally delegate sanitizing schema .describe() fields to callers, creating a fragile trust boundary; README/JSDoc notes exist but example code (and enforcement) is still a follow-up item.

- Operational lifecycle and resource considerations
  - Throttled map + unref'ed cleanup interval is implemented and tested (start/stop/cleanup). Lifecycle correctness depends on start/shutdown wiring; process crashes or mis-wiring could allow map growth or missed logging—ops should validate the cleanup runs in deployed configurations.

- Recommended next-step priorities (concise)
  - Centralize shared constants and content-type gating into utils/config.
  - Move isBinaryContentType and related predicates into a shared module and verify all tool paths use them.
  - Implement full HTML tag/script/style and markdown-beacon stripping or clearly document scope/risks.
  - Provide README examples and/or enforce sanitization for schema field descriptions to remove caller contract fragility.
  - Add jq unit tests and more obfuscation-resilience tests (homoglyphs, encoded payloads).
  - Confirm ops/SIEM updates for the documented log format and validate cleanup interval behavior in production.

author: houshuang
body:
## Summary

Replaces the legacy "generate-then-rerank" sentence generation path with a single tool-enabled Claude CLI session that drafts, validates, and surgically self-corrects sentences for up to ~10 target lemmas at a time. Legacy path preserved behind `ALIF_USE_LEGACY_BATCH=1` for rollback.

Benchmark (N=10, see `research/experiment-log.md` 2026-04-20):
- Quality: 67% → **95%** (Haiku-v2 naturalness rerank)
- Throughput: 2.0 → **1.90** sentences/lemma (effectively unchanged)
- Cost: $0.247 → **$0.085** per lemma (2.9× reduction)

The critical quality lever was the tightened system prompt — rules A-E against unanchored 3rd-person verbs, bare definite subjects, demonstrative subjects, and tautologies. Without them the same batch came in at 65%. A unit test asserts the rules stay in the prompt so a future refactor can't silently drop them.

N=15 regressed quality to 56% (Sonnet gets sloppier per-target at scale), so N=10 is the hardcoded sweet spot when `batch_generate_material` is called with a larger list — callers cap at 10.

Also in this PR: documents the intentional `same_lemma` rejection in `apply_corrections` with a docstring guard block + inline comment. Pure hardening, no functional change. The rejection closes the wrong-lemma class of bugs fixed between 2026-03-21 and 2026-04-16.

## Rollback

`ALIF_USE_LEGACY_BATCH=1` on the backend restores the previous path end-to-end. Single-lemma callers (`learn.py`, `sentence_selector.py`, `leech_service.py`, `ocr_service.py`) are also covered by this switch.

author: hanneshayashi
body:
## Problem

The provider had a hardcoded 30s HTTP client timeout that caused `context deadline exceeded` errors for large API operations — specifically, allocations with 237+ rules that take 3+ minutes to process.

## Solution

### Two-layer timeout architecture

| Layer | Controls | Default | Configurable via |
| ----- | -------- | ------- | ---------------- |
| **Request timeout** (inner) | Each individual HTTP request | `120s` | `request_timeout` attribute or `DOIT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` env var |
| **Operation timeout** (outer) | Entire Terraform operation incl. retries | CRUD: 5m, Read: 2m | `timeouts {}` attribute on each resource/data source |

The operation timeout is the outer boundary — retries continue until the operation context deadline is reached. The retry loop sets `MaxElapsedTime = 0`, deferring entirely to Go context deadlines rather than maintaining a separate timer.

### Provider-level
- New `request_timeout` attribute (default `120s`, up from hardcoded `30s`)
- `DOIT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` environment variable support
- Validation that timeout is positive
- `Validate` call in `NewClient` wrapped with bounded context so provider init fails fast

### Per-operation timeouts (`terraform-plugin-framework-timeouts`)
- **9 resources**: `timeouts` nested attribute with `create`/`read`/`update`/`delete`
- **41 data sources**: `timeouts` nested attribute with `read`
- Uses nested attributes (not blocks) — no cosmetic plan diffs for existing users

### Testing
- 5 new mock-server tests verifying:
  - Per-request timeout enforcement with retries
  - Context cancellation propagation through retry loop
  - Retry loop respects context deadline (`MaxElapsedTime = 0`)
  - Custom and default timeout acceptance
- All existing acceptance tests pass
- Pre-commit hooks (golangci-lint with govet shadow) pass

### Documentation
- New `docs/guides/timeouts.md` covering both layers, their interaction, and troubleshooting
- Warning about setting `request_timeout` larger than operation timeout
- All resource/data-source docs regenerated with `timeouts` attribute

## Verification

Tested against customer's 237-rule allocation config:
- **Before**: `context deadline exceeded` at 30s
- **After**: Created successfully in **3m23s**, updated, label-assigned, and destroyed without errors

author: chesema
body:
PR #99879 added `sendProgress` at the end of `processInsertQuery` for both sync and async insert paths. This broke backward compatibility — old clients whose `RemoteInserter::onFinish` does not handle `Progress` packets fail with `UNEXPECTED_PACKET_FROM_SERVER` when inserting into a newer server (e.g. 25.8 → 26.4 via `INSERT INTO remote()`).

**Changes:**
- Remove `sendProgress` from the sync insert path (it was unintentional — PR #99879 aimed to fix async insert progress only, sync inserts never sent `Progress` at the end of `processInsertQuery` before)
- Gate the async insert path's `sendProgress` behind a new protocol revision `DBMS_MIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION_WITH_PROGRESS_IN_ASYNC_INSERT` (54484)
- Restore `test_old_versions` to use `CLICKHOUSE_CI_MIN_TESTED_VERSION` instead of the hardcoded `"25.12"` pin that was introduced as a workaround

Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/issues/54601
Related PR: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99879

- The OTP sheet itself is already dismissed by `ServerBackupVerificationScreen.deleteVault()` (which sets `isPresented = false` before firing the callback), so no extra sheet state reset is needed.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fast vault flow (new vault) via `VaultSetupScreen`: enter name/email/password, continue through keygen until OTP appears. Tap "Use a different email". Verify the app returns to the email step of VaultSetupScreen (not OTP, not a new blank screen).
- [ ] Fast vault flow (existing vault) via `FastVaultPasswordScreen` (single keygen / reshare path): reach OTP, tap "Use a different email", verify user returns to the email step of FastVaultPasswordScreen.
- [ ] Verify no duplicated routes in the back stack after pressing back from the email screen.

## Summary

Initialize \`CLAUDE.md\` at the root of this repo — a structured
knowledge card consumed by Claude Code / the \`core-tel-ai-agents\`
fs-knowledge agent to ground code-level lookups without guessing.

Public-safe (no internal ticket references). 238 lines, within the
\"large/complex tier\" target (250–350) for a massive-codebase repo.

## What's inside

- **Fork origin**: \`signalwire/freeswitch\` + Telnyx branch naming convention (\`telnyx/telephony/master\` as default, \`telnyx/telephony/deploy-development\` as dev, per-cluster / per-release branches)
- **Ecosystem position**: loaded into BOTH \`b2bua\` and \`b2bua-rtc\`; this repo branch-syncs to both images (distinct from most \`mod_*\` repos that only sync to \`b2bua\`)
- **Build integration**: \`telnyx_b2bua_builder/Makefile\` clones this repo, then drops sibling Telnyx modules (\`mod_telnyx\`, \`mod_homer_rtcp\`, \`mod_call_control\`, etc.) into \`src/mod/{category}/\` at build time. Combined tree builds into the \`telnyx_b2bua-*.deb\` consumed by both runtime images
- **Source tree map**: top-level directories (\`build/\`, \`clients/\`, \`conf/\`, \`docker/\`, \`docs/\`, \`libs/\`, \`src/\`, \`tests/\`, etc.) with role per entry
- **Core subsystem inventory**: \`switch_core.c\` (3,701), \`switch_core_media.c\` (20,432 — biggest file), \`switch_rtp.c\` (12,017), \`switch_channel.c\` (5,970), \`switch_ivr*.c\` family, \`switch_loadable_module.c\` — line counts and responsibility per file
- **Module map per category**: applications (61), codecs (22), endpoints (incl. \`mod_sofia\` at 35,454 lines), event_handlers, dialplans, etc.
- **Vendored libs in \`libs/\`** (APR, ESL, SRTP, xmlrpc-c, freetype, miniupnpc, libteletone, iksemel, libnatpmp, libscgi) vs external Telnyx libs pulled by \`fs_docker_deps\` (sofia-sip, spandsp, bcg729, libhdsp, lib3gpp-evs-fp, rnnoise-internal, soundtouch, libks, unimrcp, IXWebSocket)
- **GHA workflow** mapping: \`reviewpr.yml\` + \`trigger-b2bua-builder.yml\` — this is one of the repos whose branch-sync targets include \`b2bua-rtc\`
- **Core concepts reference**: module ABI (\`SWITCH_MODULE_DEFINITION\`), channel lifecycle (\`CS_NEW → CS_INIT → CS_ROUTING → CS_EXECUTE → CS_HANGUP → CS_DESTROY\`), RTP hooks (\`switch_rtp_set_create_probe\`, \`_rtcp_probe\`, \`CF_ENABLE_RTCP_PROBE\`), session-locking rules, SDP/media negotiation path
- **Sibling-module integration map**: which Telnyx \`mod_*\` repos drop into which \`src/mod/\` subdirectory at build time
- **\"Things to read when answering X\"**: quick index pointing the agent to the right file for common questions (bridge, codec negotiation, SIP INVITE handling, channel state transitions, RTP write path, dialplan resolution, event bus)

## Non-goals

- Does NOT duplicate \`.llm-repo-instructions\` (referenced for style/memory/threading notes)
- Does NOT duplicate the 23 FS coding rules from the fs-knowledge system prompt §9
- Does NOT try to describe every function in this massive codebase inline — agent uses \`fs_read_file\` on the specific line range when needed

## Rollout context

This is the second CLAUDE.md in the 43-repo FS ecosystem rollout. First was \`mod_homer_rtcp#28\`. The \`core-tel-ai-agents\` PR #18 (merged) wired up the \`fs_list_repos\` / \`fs_read_repo_docs\` / \`fs_read_file\` tools so the agent can actually consume these files at query time.

body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Implémente une authentification basée sur JWT avec un contrôle d’accès basé sur les rôles et introduit des APIs de gestion des étudiants, des classes et des profils utilisateur, reposant sur de nouveaux modèles Prisma et des migrations.

Nouvelles fonctionnalités :
- Ajout d’un endpoint de connexion basé sur JWT renvoyant un jeton d’accès et les données de profil utilisateur.
- Exposition d’endpoints authentifiés pour la récupération et la mise à jour du profil utilisateur.
- Introduction d’APIs CRUD pour les classes avec attribution optionnelle d’enseignant, sécurisées par un contrôle d’accès basé sur les rôles.
- Introduction d’APIs CRUD pour les étudiants avec relations optionnelles de classe et de parent, sécurisées par un contrôle d’accès basé sur les rôles.
- Ajout d’une configuration CORS pour autoriser les requêtes depuis le frontend à l’adresse http://localhost:5173.
- Ajout d’un service pgAdmin à docker-compose pour l’administration de la base de données.

Améliorations :
- Extension de l’inscription utilisateur pour capturer et persister des champs de profil de base.
- Stockage de champs utilisateur supplémentaires (prénom, nom, téléphone) dans la charge utile du JWT et dans la base de données.
- Introduction d’un décorateur de rôle et d’un guard pour appliquer l’autorisation basée sur les rôles sur les routes protégées.

Build :
- Enregistrement des fournisseurs JWT, Passport et des stratégies/guards associés dans le module auth, et ajout de la dépendance mapped-types pour les utilitaires de DTO.
- Ajout de la dépendance cuid et ajustement de l’ID utilisateur Prisma pour utiliser des clés primaires textuelles au lieu de séquences.

Déploiement :
- Extension de docker-compose avec un conteneur pgAdmin pour la gestion locale de la base de données.

Tests :
- Ajout de fichiers de scaffolding de tests pour les modules classes, students et users afin de supporter de futures implémentations de tests.

Tâches diverses :
- Ajout de migrations Prisma pour prendre en charge les champs de profil utilisateur et les nouveaux modèles et relations Class et Student.

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Implement JWT-based authentication with role-based access control and introduce student, class, and user profile management APIs backed by new Prisma models and migrations.

New Features:
- Add JWT-based login endpoint returning access token and user profile data.
- Expose authenticated user profile retrieval and update endpoints.
- Introduce CRUD APIs for classes with optional teacher assignment, secured by role-based access control.
- Introduce CRUD APIs for students with optional class and parent relationships, secured by role-based access control.
- Add CORS configuration to allow requests from the frontend at http://localhost:5173.
- Add pgAdmin service to docker-compose for database administration.

Enhancements:
- Extend user registration to capture basic profile fields and persist them.
- Store additional user fields (first name, last name, phone) in JWT payload and database.
- Introduce role decorator and guard to enforce role-based authorization on protected routes.

Build:
- Register JWT, Passport, and related strategy/guard providers in the auth module and add mapped-types dependency for DTO utilities.
- Add cuid dependency and adjust Prisma user ID to use text primary keys instead of sequences.

Deployment:
- Extend docker-compose with a pgAdmin container for local database management.

Tests:
- Add test scaffolding files for classes, students, and users modules to support future test implementation.

Chores:
- Add Prisma migrations to support user profile fields and new Class and Student models and relationships.

</details>

author: yozaz
body:
The `clawhub` CLI doesn't pick up `version:` from SKILL.md frontmatter — it requires `--version` on its own command line. Easy to drift, and the error message (`--version must be valid semver`) isn't discoverable.

This PR adds `scripts/publish-skill.mjs` which parses the frontmatter version and shells out to `clawhub publish` with it. Single source of truth stays in `SKILL.md`; bump the version there and run:

```bash
pnpm skill:publish
```

Skill README updated to point at this command.

body:
## Summary

Enables agents to upload their own compliance documents and re-upload after HR rejection, completing the A2c milestone from `docs/hr-roadmap.md`.

### New RLS policies (migration `20260420100001`)

| Policy | Table/Bucket | Effect |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| `agents_insert_own_documents` | `employee_documents` INSERT | Agent can insert `pending_review` rows for their own `employee_id` |
| `agents_update_rejected_documents` | `employee_documents` UPDATE | Agent can update only `rejected` rows → `pending_review` for themselves |
| `agents_storage_insert_own` | `storage.objects` INSERT | Agent can upload files under their own `employee_id/` prefix |

Agents cannot: modify pending/approved docs, set status to approved, or upload for other employees.

### UI changes (EmployeeHome.tsx)

- **Missing docs:** Upload button shown with type name + description
- **Rejected docs:** Re-upload button shown alongside rejection reason
- **Pending/Approved:** Read-only (no action buttons)
- File validation: PDF/JPG/PNG only, 10 MB max
- RLS-denied uploads show "Unable to upload — contact HR" error toast

### Shared constants

New `src/lib/documentUpload.ts` with `ACCEPTED_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, `ACCEPTED_DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS`, `MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE_BYTES`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Agent with no docs: upload a PDF → status becomes "Pending review", filename visible
- [ ] Admin rejects that doc with a reason
- [ ] Agent sees rejection reason + "Re-upload" button → upload different file → status back to "Pending review"
- [ ] Agent with approved doc: no Upload/Re-upload button renders
- [ ] Agent devtools: `supabase.from("employee_documents").update({status:'approved'})` → RLS blocks
- [ ] Agent devtools: upload with a different employee's ID → RLS blocks
- [ ] File validation: try uploading .docx → error toast; try 15 MB file → error toast

author: zhouxiaolong-01
body:
## Related Issue
Fixes #13075  

## What does this PR do?

This PR improves the memory/skill nudge trigger logic by:

1. **Preventing Duplicate Memory Reviews**: By moving the `_should_review_memory` check to occur after tool calls, we effectively prevent redundant memory reviews.
   *Note: Previously, if _should_review_memory was true and a memory tool was invoked within the loop, a duplicate review would still be triggered after the loop finished, even though the counter had already been reset.*
2. **Implementing Conditional Counter Resets**: Nudge counters for skills and memory are now reset only upon the confirmed initiation of the background review process. 
   *Note: Previously, nudge counters were reset immediately upon reaching the interval threshold. However, if the review operation was not executed—due to an empty `final_response` or an interruption—the accumulated progress was lost, forcing a restart of the counter accumulation.*

This approach is correct because it ensures:
1.  No duplicate memory reviews occur.
2. Nudge opportunities aren't lost due to interruptions or conversation failures—no need to restart accumulation from scratch.
3. The code has clearer, more intuitive semantics.
4. Memory and skill nudge behavior is consistent.

## Type of Change

- [✅] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [✅] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)


## Changes Made

- `run_agent.py`: Moved memory nudge trigger check from conversation start to end
- `run_agent.py`: Moved memory/skill counter reset logic to only happen when background review is actually spawned
Aligned memory nudge logic with skill nudge logic for consistency
- `tests/run_agent/test_memory_skill_nudge_trigger.py`: Added comprehensive unit tests for the new logic


## How to Test

1. Normal nudge trigger test :
   - Set _memory_nudge_interval = 2 (in code or via config)
   - Have 2 conversation turns
   - Verify memory nudge triggers after the second turn
2. User-initiated memory tool test :
   - Set _memory_nudge_interval = 2
   - Have 1 conversation turn (counter = 1)
   - In the second turn, manually call the memory tool (counter resets to 0)
   - Verify no duplicate memory nudge is triggered
3. Conversation interruption test :
   - Set _memory_nudge_interval = 2
   - Have 1 conversation turn (counter = 1)
   - Start a second turn but interrupt/fail it
   - Verify the counter remains intact and nudge triggers on next successful turn

The app startup failure was caused by Hibernate configuration drift: project dependencies are on Hibernate 6, while runtime dialect settings still referenced legacy `MySQLDialect`. This updates configuration to Hibernate 6-compatible MySQL dialect values.

- **Configuration alignment**
  - Updated Hibernate dialect in Spring Java config fallback:
    - `src/main/java/com/events/config/AppConfig.java`
  - Updated Hibernate dialect in externalized properties:
    - `src/main/resources/database.properties`

- **Why this matters**
  - Ensures consistent dialect resolution for Hibernate 6.x and avoids startup-time misconfiguration tied to outdated dialect declarations.

```java
// AppConfig.java
props.put(
    "hibernate.dialect",
    env.getProperty("hibernate.dialect", "org.hibernate.dialect.MySQL8Dialect")
);
```

```properties
# database.properties
hibernate.dialect=org.hibernate.dialect.MySQL8Dialect
```

The application crashes at startup with Spring context initialization failure because the configuration is using deprecated Hibernate 5 imports with Hibernate 6.4.4.

   - `import org.springframework.orm.hibernate5.LocalSessionFactoryBean;`
   
2. **Lines 137-138**: Using deprecated `MySQLDialect` which should be `MySQL8Dialect` in Hibernate 6

Update `AppConfig.java` to use Hibernate 6 compatible classes:

1. Change imports from `org.springframework.orm.hibernate5.*` to `org.springframework.orm.hibernate6.*`
2. Update dialect from `MySQLDialect` to `MySQL8Dialect` (Hibernate 6 standard)
3. Ensure Spring ORM version is compatible with Hibernate 6
4. Optionally add `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` or ensure `spring-orm:6.1.5` includes Hibernate 6 support

author: adamjbradley
body:
## Summary

- iPhone EUDI wallet was rejecting auth-op login with "The requested document is not available in your EUDI wallet" despite holding a valid AU PID (`urn:au:gov:mygovid:pid:1`).
- Root cause in `eudi-lib-ios-wallet-kit` Openid4VpUtils.swift:154-159 — its `CredentialQuery.docType` only reads the first entry of `vct_values`, and `DefaultDcqlQueryable.getCredential` does single-string equality. Our query listed `urn:eudi:pid:1` first, so every other VCT was invisible to that wallet.
- Fix: emit one credential query per VCT (single-element `vct_values` each), union under a required `credential_sets` option. Spec-compliant, sidesteps the iOS matcher bug, backwards-compatible with walt.id/Android wallets and verifier-api2.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced on iPhone EUDI-AU wallet — verifier-api2 saw `GET /verification-session/<id>/request` with no `/response` follow-up (wallet silently rejected DCQL)
- [x] Patched composer, rebuilt jib image, deployed via remote SSH
- [ ] Confirm iPhone login succeeds end-to-end (`POST /verification-session/<id>/response` fires, RP login completes)
- [ ] Confirm Android walt.id wallet still logs in (no regression)
- [x] Cross-stack compatibility audit — iOS wallet-kit, Android wallet-core, walt.id DCQL matcher, verifier-api2 all implement matching "any option satisfies a required set" semantics

author: rasmusfaber
body:
## Summary

This is basically the branch I have been using to analyze and test the OOM fixes (just cleaned up a bit). I think we should get it on main to keep it from drifting.

Enabling this with `runner.oom_diagnostics_enabled` will run an always-on memray allocation tracker in the runner and upload a diagnostics bundle (memray allocations, py-spy all-thread stacks, cgroup state, process tree) to `s3://<log_dir>/diagnostics/` whenever the run approaches OOM (>90% of the cgroup limit or sustained memory pressure), crosses the 50%/75% one-shot thresholds, 60s after startup (baseline), or on `SIGUSR1` at a 5-15% cost in memory and CPU. It is off by default.

Two changes apply to all runner jobs, not just ones with diagnostics enabled:

- Memory monitor poll interval 30s → 5s (it now also feeds the trigger check).
- Near-OOM warning threshold 95% → 90% of `memory.max` (raised toward `memory.max` when `memory.high` is set, same as the trigger).

## Test plan

[x] On a dev stack with `oom_diagnostics_enabled: true`: confirmed the startup log line, a `SIGUSR1` manual capture, and a near-OOM trigger capture each upload a complete bundle to `s3://<log_dir>/diagnostics/`.

author: stevenbtw
body:
## Summary

Automated update triggered by [Grafeo v0.5.40](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/releases/tag/v0.5.40).

- Bumped `package.json` version to 0.5.40
- Updated `@grafeo-db/wasm` to 0.5.40
- Updated `@grafeo-db/wasm-lite` to 0.5.40
- Added changelog entry
- Typecheck and tests passed before PR creation

## Grafeo Release Notes

## [0.5.40] - 2026-04-20

Unified hybrid queries (graph + vector + text), lazy streaming results, structured Python errors, catalog hierarchy hardening, and compact-store fixes.

### Added

- **Unified hybrid queries**: `text_score()` and `text_match()` usable as filter expressions, with planner pushdown of score predicates to `TextScan` / `VectorScan` operators, compound AND/OR joins, top-K recognition, and score projection. Inspired by [#287](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/pull/287) ([@temporaryfix](https://github.com/temporaryfix)); reimplemented via the `GraphStoreSearch` subtrait.
- **BM25 text scan operator**: `TextScanOperator` with top-K and threshold modes. `InvertedIndex` gains `score_document`, `search_with_threshold`, `bm25_term_score`. ([#287](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/pull/287), [@temporaryfix](https://github.com/temporaryfix))
- **Native Float64 and Float32Vector codecs**: CompactStore stores them directly instead of falling back to dictionary encoding. Mixed `Int64+Float64` columns coalesce to Float64. ([#286](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/pull/286), [@temporaryfix](https://github.com/temporaryfix))
- **Streaming query results** (experimental): `Session::execute_streaming` returns a `ResultStream` that pulls one `DataChunk` at a time, bounded memory regardless of result-set size. Exposed across bindings: Python `execute_lazy()`, Node.js `executeStream()`, C# `ExecuteStream()`, Dart `executeStream()`, and Go and C FFI equivalents. Rejects mutations, EXPLAIN/PROFILE, session commands, and push-only plans.
- **Python `GrafeoError` exception**: subclass of `RuntimeError` carrying `error_code` (`"GRAFEO-Q001"`) and `is_retryable`. Legacy `except RuntimeError:` paths keep working.
- **Error codes reference**: user-guide page documenting every `GRAFEO-*` code, retry semantics, and a Python retry-loop sample.
- **Catalog hierarchy docs** (ISO/IEC 39075): user-guide page covering schemas, named graphs, session state, isolation, and cross-schema transactions.

### Changed

- **`DatabaseStats.memory_bytes` reflects the full heap breakdown**: now equals `memory_usage().total_bytes` (store + indexes + MVCC + caches + string pools + buffer manager) instead of just buffer-manager-tracked bytes.
- **Schema and graph names reject `/`**: `CREATE SCHEMA` / `CREATE GRAPH` now fail on names containing `/`, which Grafeo uses internally as the compound `schema/graph` storage-key separator.

### Fixed

- **Multi-schema transaction atomicity**: `SESSION SET SCHEMA` mid-transaction no longer loses pre-switch writes on COMMIT. Fix centralizes "touched graph" tracking inside the session setters so every active-key change is recorded.
- **Commit failure auto-rollback**: a failed COMMIT now discards pending writes and returns the session to a clean state, instead of leaving the transaction in-flight with uncommitted writes still visible.
- **Parser keyword anti-pattern**: `try_accept_keyword` helpers fix four `CREATE CONSTRAINT ... FOR`, `ON REPLACE`, and similar sites where identifier-fallback tokenization accepted the wrong keyword.
- **Vector strict pushdown boundary leak**: `euclidean_distance(...) < t` and `manhattan_distance(...) < t` now correctly exclude rows at exactly the threshold; strict comparisons attach a residual filter above the vector scan, which was previously dropped.
- **MERGE index lookup**: `MERGE (n:Label {prop: value})` now uses property indexes when available, eliminating O(n) scan on large graphs. ([#288](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/issues/288))
- **Index and search after `compact()`**: ~26 vector/text index methods no longer panic with "no built-in LpgStore" or silently return empty results. ([#286](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/pull/286), [@temporaryfix](https://github.com/temporaryfix))
- **`LayeredStore` new-node visibility**: `get_node` / `get_node_property` fall back to the overlay for nodes added after `compact()`. ([#286](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/pull/286))
- **Named graphs across `compact()` / `recompact()`**: graphs existing before compaction are carried into the new overlay; `list_graphs`, `drop_graph`, `create_graph`, `set_current_graph` see them.
- **Layered scan lock holding**: `nodes_by_label` acquires `dirty_node_ids` once per scan instead of re-locking in the chunk loop. ([#278](https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/pull/278), [@temporaryfix](https://github.com/temporaryfix))

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/GrafeoDB/grafeo/compare/v0.5.39...v0.5.40

## Checklist

- [ ] Review changelog entry (add new API surface if applicable)
- [ ] Verify tests pass in grafeo-web CI
- [ ] Merge when ready (release is created automatically)

`tests/unit/test_synthetic_dataset.py:54` hardcoded bare `"python"` as the subprocess command, forcing PATH resolution to an arbitrary interpreter rather than the one running pytest. When bare `python` is absent (common on Windows CI agents, where `py.exe` / `python3` are canonical) or points to a system interpreter without `numpy`, all 32 generator-backed tests fail.

Switched to `sys.executable`, which always points to the currently-running interpreter. The same file already uses this pattern at lines 887-888 and 900-901 — this aligns the third subprocess site with the existing convention.

Strictly more cross-OS-robust; not a behaviour change on CI where `python` on PATH already is the test interpreter.

author: evangodon-ls
body:
## Summary

Registers a native DOM capture-phase `keydown` listener on `document`. When Escape is pressed while a tooltip is open, `preventDefault()` is called before the modal's bubble-phase handler fires — the modal checks `evt.isDefaultPrevented()` and bails out, leaving the modal open. The tooltip is then dismissed by the existing `keyup` listener.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4421ed83-bf79-4afc-a885-4bedf0d625a0



## Why capture phase?

The modal registers its `keydown` handler on `$document` when it opens (bubble phase). The tooltip service registers at app boot — but tooltips inside modals cause the service to boot *after* the modal opens, so the modal's handler is always at index 0 in jQuery's queue. `stopPropagation` and `stopImmediatePropagation` on bubble-phase handlers can't win this race.

Native `addEventListener(..., true)` (capture phase) always fires before any bubble-phase handler, regardless of registration order.

## WCAG

Fixes [1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html) (Level AA) — **Dismissible**: Escape closes the tooltip without closing the parent modal (GOLF-4538)

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a reservation's View Receipt modal
- [ ] Hover the affiliation type badge to show the tooltip
- [ ] Press Escape — tooltip should close, modal should stay open
- [ ] Press Escape again — modal should close normally

## Problem

Gunicorn is configured to load `app:app` (module:variable), but `app.py` only defined a `create_app()` factory function with no module-level `app` variable, causing the crash "Failed to find attribute 'app' in 'app'" on every startup.

## Solution

Added `app = create_app()` at the bottom of `app.py` so that importing the module eagerly creates and exposes the Flask instance. Gunicorn can now resolve `app:app` successfully and the service starts without error.

author: gitbakko
body:
## Summary

Incident 2026-04-20 00:01-00:09: three positions (WTIUSD, NATGAS, DE40) persisted with P&L 30-55% off actual broker values. Root cause: `_detect_broker_closed` fell into a legacy heuristic fallback that computed `pnl = (exit - entry) * size` — a formula that ignores contract multipliers and always writes invented numbers. Fallback was taken because the Transaction History API match had two independent failure modes (wrong timestamp format, wrong identifier in `txn.reference`).

This PR replaces the whole close-detection path with a three-tier flow:

1. **Primary** — Transaction History API hardened with correct UTC params, 24h window, and three matching strategies (`deal_reference` deterministic, `deal_id` legacy, normalized-instrument-name fuzzy).
2. **Deferred** — if no match, position held in `_pending_close_detections` for up to 10 min of retry without writing to DB or firing alerts.
3. **UNRECONCILED** — after timeout, writes the close with `pnl=NULL`, `close_reason='UNRECONCILED'`, and fires a dedicated `POSITION_STUCK` alert with the CLI command to recover manually.

Legacy `_fallback_close_detection` is removed entirely. No code path can invent P&L anymore.

## Changes

- Capital.com Transaction History: UTC normalization, no Z/offset suffix (broker rejects), 24h window, 60s cache
- Position model + DB migration for `deal_reference` — 4 open-time persistence sites patched
- `_match_transaction` rewritten with 3 strategies (Strategy 3 handles WTIUSD via `Oil - Crude` normalization; DE40 has an `xfail` documenting that Strategy 3 can't match 'Germany 40' and must rely on Strategy 1)
- `_detect_broker_closed` rewritten as 3-tier orchestrator with DB bridge for `deal_reference`
- `_on_position_closed` guarded against `pnl=None` (Kelly/CB/equity-filter immune)
- `_persist_position_close` guarded against `pnl=None` (UNRECONCILED path)
- Orphan re-injection at startup with 2-day age filter (skips legacy backlog)
- SQL aggregations (win-rate, P&L sum, equity stats) exclude `close_reason='UNRECONCILED'`
- Prometheus counter `mantis_close_detection_path_total{path, epic}`
- `scripts/reconcile_position.py` CLI for manual P&L recovery
- Broker auth retry on 429 with exponential backoff, CRITICAL alarm on final fallback
- Transaction.pl_value currency-mismatch warning (no FX conversion)

## Test plan

- [x] 2446 tests passing, 20 pre-existing baseline failures (unchanged), 1 documented xfail
- [x] Unit + integration tests for 3 match strategies, deferred flow, UNRECONCILED timeout, orphan reinject, CLI reconcile, broker auth retry
- [x] e2e test: broker returns `[]` for 3 iterations, matching transaction on 4th → primary path fires, real P&L written, pending dict empties
- [x] Manual verification on demo (2026-04-20): CLI reconciliation of 3 corrupted records (IDs 2119, 2120, 2121) — DB now matches broker values

## Docs

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-20-close-detection-pnl-robustness-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-20-close-detection-pnl-robustness.md`

## Follow-ups (tracked, out of scope)

- Refactor `_match_transaction` → `@staticmethod` to remove `_Stub` workaround in CLI
- Policy decision on `POSITION_STUCK` alert severity (WARNING vs CRITICAL routing)
- `get_historical_prices` uses same naive strftime pattern (deferred)
- UX: unify 'Paper Trading' vs 'Positions' views to reduce mode-switch confusion
- Investigate 20 pre-existing baseline failures

author: paulrberg
body:
Replaces the misplaced v2.0+ ABI shipped under `airdrops/v1.3` for `SablierMerkleLockup` with the actual v1.3 ABI, sourced from [sablier-labs/airdrops@1.3.0](https://github.com/sablier-labs/airdrops/tree/v1.3.0). The old payload exposed the oracle-driven min-fee model (`ORACLE`, `calculateMinFeeWei`, `minFeeUSD`, `lowerMinFeeUSD`) and the v2.0 `SABLIER_LOCKUP` rename, so any consumer resolving this ABI against a real v1.3 MerkleLL/MerkleLT campaign would mis-simulate calls and fail to decode `FEE()`.

The fixed ABI uses the immutable `FEE` pattern, the pre-v2.0 `LOCKUP` naming, and drops the v2.0-only entries. Since v1.3 has no concrete `SablierMerkleLockup` contract, the ABI reflects the shared Lockup-level interface between `SablierMerkleLL` and `SablierMerkleLT` (base functions + `LOCKUP`, `STREAM_CANCELABLE`, `STREAM_TRANSFERABLE`, and the `Claim` event with `streamId`).

Closes #174

body:
## Summary

Fixes #78 - removes extra trace lines in post-processing step.

## Root Cause

The `simplifyPath` function in `lib/solvers/TraceCleanupSolver/simplifyPath.ts` had **two identical passes** that both remove collinear points:
- First pass (lines 10-22): removes redundant collinear points
- Second pass (lines 25-38): does the exact same thing again

The second pass was completely redundant and could potentially introduce visual artifacts in the trace rendering.

## Changes

- Removed the duplicate second loop (16 lines deleted)
- Single pass is sufficient to simplify the path
- No behavior change expected for valid inputs

## Testing

The existing test suite should pass as this is a pure optimization that produces the same output for valid inputs.

body:
## Summary

Reverts commit [3c128c8](https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase-package-manager/commit/3c128c828018b8224903ee53d6392b9fa26090fa), which was pushed directly to \`master\` without PR review.

That commit renamed \`master\` → \`main\` in workflows, docs, and one runtime URL. The intent is correct, but it needs to be coordinated with the actual GitHub default-branch rename — merging it before the rename breaks \`publish-release.yml\` (which does \`git push origin main\` to a branch that doesn't exist yet) and silences CI triggers on \`master\`.

## Why revert

- Landed on \`master\` without review
- Commit message missing the \`DAT-22095:\` ticket prefix required by project convention
- Will break release automation if left in place before the GitHub-side branch rename

## Plan after this merges

1. Merge this revert to restore \`master\` to a working state
2. Reopen the rename work as a proper PR on \`DAT-22095\` with a conventional commit message
3. Merge that PR + perform the GitHub default-branch rename (\`master\` → \`main\`) in coordination, per the steps in the DAT-22095 discussion

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm \`master\` HEAD after merge matches the pre-3c128c8 state for the 10 affected files
- [ ] Confirm CI (test.yml, codeql.yml) is triggering again on pushes to \`master\`
- [ ] Confirm next release workflow dry-run doesn't attempt \`git push origin main\`

body:
## What

Replace the external `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` action in the desktop smoke and desktop bundle workflows with a repo-local Rust bootstrap action that uses `rustup` directly.

## Why

`main` is currently flaking on macOS during workflow setup before checkout/build begins. The failure is not in app code; GitHub Actions is intermittently failing to download the `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` action tarball for macOS jobs.

That leaves `Desktop Smoke (macOS)` and `Bundle (macOS Apple Silicon)` red on otherwise healthy commits. Using a local action removes that extra third-party action fetch while keeping the same stable Rust toolchain behavior.

## How

- added `.github/actions/setup-rust/action.yml`
- install stable Rust with `rustup` directly on Unix and Windows runners
- keep optional target installation for bundle builds
- switched `.github/workflows/desktop-e2e.yml` to the local Rust setup action
- switched `.github/workflows/build.yml` to the local Rust setup action

## Related Issue

Closes #70

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [x] CI / tooling
- [ ] Chore (dependencies, config)

- [x] Verified no remaining `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` references in tracked workflows

Commands run:

```bash
ruby -e "require 'yaml'; %w[.github/actions/setup-rust/action.yml .github/workflows/build.yml .github/workflows/desktop-e2e.yml].each { |f| YAML.load_file(f); puts \"OK #{f}\" }"

```

`plan.md` called out incorrect directional intra prediction as a high-impact source of visible decode artifacts (gray/non-human-readable output quality). This PR applies the smallest concrete fix from that plan: remove non-spec gradient bias from V/H intra prediction.

- **Intra prediction correction (Phase 1 from `plan.md`)**
  - Updated `stbi_avif__av1_predict_block` for:
    - `V_PRED` to use pure top reference copy
    - `H_PRED` to use pure left reference copy
  - Removed synthetic gradient terms previously added to both modes.

- **Plan alignment**
  - Marked the corresponding Quick Wins in `plan.md` as completed:
    - V_PRED gradient removal
    - H_PRED gradient removal

```c
/* before */
case 1u: /* V */
   val = (int)top[tix] + ((int)(2u * x + 1u) * amp) / (int)(2u * (bw ? bw : 1u)) - amp / 2;
   break;
case 2u: /* H */
   val = (int)left[tiy] + ((int)(2u * y + 1u) * amp) / (int)(2u * (bh ? bh : 1u)) - amp / 2;
   break;

/* after */
case 1u: /* V */
   val = (int)top[tix];
   break;
case 2u: /* H */
   val = (int)left[tiy];

```

author: vslnk
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes several security vulnerabilities found in the plugin.

### [HIGH] Unauthenticated API credential disclosure via `?debug_comeet_plugin`

The `plugin_debug()` function in both `comeet.php` and `comeet-data.php` would output full debug information — including the Comeet API token and UID embedded in the API request URL — to **any unauthenticated visitor** who appended `?debug_comeet_plugin` to a careers page URL.

**Fix:** Added `current_user_can('manage_options')` check before executing debug output. Debug info is now only visible to site administrators.

Affected: `comeet.php:1986`, `includes/lib/comeet-data.php:335`

---

### [HIGH] Reflected XSS via `?coref` GET parameter

The `$_GET['coref']` parameter was concatenated directly into a `<link rel="canonical">` tag and passed through the `wpseo_canonical` / `wpseo_opengraph_url` filters without any sanitization or escaping. An attacker could craft a URL such as:

```
https://example.com/careers?coref="><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>
```

and trick a user into clicking it to execute arbitrary JavaScript in their browser.

**Fix:** The value is now sanitized with `sanitize_text_field(wp_unslash(...))`, encoded with `rawurlencode()`, and the full URL is passed through `esc_url()` before output.

Affected: `comeet.php:269`, `comeet.php:312`

---

### [MEDIUM] JSON-LD job schema built via string interpolation

`add_job_posting_js_schema()` constructed `<script type="application/ld+json">` output by interpolating raw API values directly into a JSON string. A job position with a name or description containing `"` or `\` characters would produce invalid or injectable JSON.

**Fix:** The schema is now built as a PHP associative array and serialized with `wp_json_encode()`, which handles all escaping correctly.

Affected: `comeet.php:163`

---

### [MEDIUM] Unescaped output in OG/meta tags

`update_header()` output `og:title`, `og:image`, `og:description`, and `og:url` using bare `<?=` without any escaping functions, making them susceptible to XSS if any of those values contained HTML special characters.

**Fix:** All meta tag values now use `esc_attr()` or `esc_url()` as appropriate.

Affected: `comeet.php:367`

---

### [MEDIUM] Unescaped API data in public-facing templates

Position data returned from the Comeet API (job titles, locations, employment types, experience levels, image URLs, CSS class names) was output in all template files without escaping. Any malicious content in API responses would be rendered as raw HTML.

**Fix:** All dynamic values in templates now use `esc_html()`, `esc_attr()`, `esc_url()`, or `wp_kses_post()` (for intentional rich-text fields like job descriptions).

Affected: `templates/comeet-careers.php`, `templates/comeet-position-page-common.php`, `templates/comeet-sub-page-custom.php`

---

### [MEDIUM] Stored XSS in admin settings fields

Admin settings input fields (token, UID, colors, URLs, button text, template names) echoed option values from the database directly into HTML attribute `value=""` without `esc_attr()`, enabling stored XSS on the settings page.

**Fix:** All admin field values now use `esc_attr()` or `esc_url()`.

Affected: multiple functions in `comeet.php`

---

### [LOW] Unauthenticated cache flush via `?comeet_disable_cache`

Any unauthenticated visitor could force the plugin to bypass its 5-minute API cache and make a fresh request to the Comeet API on every page load by appending `?comeet_disable_cache` to any URL, potentially causing rate-limit issues with the API.

**Fix:** Added `current_user_can('manage_options')` check.

Affected: `includes/lib/comeet-data.php:57`, `includes/lib/comeet-data.php:70`

---

### [LOW] Missing direct-access guard on template files

Template and include files lacked `defined('ABSPATH') || exit;`, meaning they could be accessed directly via URL, producing PHP errors that leak server paths and other diagnostic information.

**Fix:** Added `defined('ABSPATH') || exit;` to all template files.

Affected: all files in `templates/`

---

## Test plan

- [ ] Careers page renders correctly with positions listed
- [ ] Individual position page renders with correct title, location, job details
- [ ] Sub-page (by location/department) renders correctly
- [ ] JSON-LD schema is valid — verify with [Google Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results)
- [ ] Appending `?debug_comeet_plugin` as a logged-out visitor produces no output
- [ ] Appending `?debug_comeet_plugin` as an admin produces debug output
- [ ] Appending `?comeet_disable_cache` as a logged-out visitor does not trigger a fresh API call
- [ ] Appending `?coref=test` produces a valid canonical URL
- [ ] Admin settings page saves and displays values correctly

author: songproducer
body:
PR #757 added auto-restart of the recrawl job on peer boot by writing event_kind=regular/event_action=startup to the API table when the job starts. On stop, it tried to clear this by calling selectLastExecutedApiCall() with the stoprecrawl POST - but that POST contains 'stoprecrawl' while the stored API URL has 'recrawlnow', so the URL-based lookup returns null and the off-switch is never written.

Fix: on stoprecrawl, scan the API table directly for any row belonging to IndexReIndexMonitor_p with event_action=startup and clear it there. This ensures that stopping the job before shutdown prevents it from auto-restarting on the next boot.

author: profvjreddi
body:
## Summary

Adds a no-downgrade guard to both \`tinytorch-publish-live.yml\` and \`book-publish-live.yml\`.
Catches a real footgun in the next release: triggering with the default \`release_type=patch\`
silently regresses TinyTorch from \`0.10.0\` → \`0.1.10\` and Vol II from \`v0.5.1\` → \`v0.0.1\`.

## The footgun in concrete terms

| Workflow | Source-of-truth | Current value | Latest tag | Default \`patch\` would write | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \`tinytorch-publish-live\` | \`pyproject.toml\` | \`0.10.0\` | \`tinytorch-v0.1.9\` | \`0.1.10\` | **DOWNGRADE** |
| \`book-publish-live\` (vol2) | \`index-vol2.qmd\` doi | \`v0.5.1\` (legacy inheritance) | none → seeds \`v0.0.0\` | \`v0.0.1\` | **DOWNGRADE** |
| \`book-publish-live\` (vol1) | \`index-vol1.qmd\` doi | \`v0.5.1\` | seeds from \`book-v0.5.1\` | \`v0.5.2\` | OK (forward) |

Both downgrades complete with no error and silently overwrite the source.

## How the guard works

After version computation, before any \`sed\` write:

1. Read the bare version from the source-of-truth file.
2. Use \`sort -V\` to compare against the planned new version.
3. If planned \< source (strict), fail with a remediation message that names the exact dispatch
   input to use (\`explicit_version=X.Y.Z\` for tinytorch, \`previous_version=vol{N}-vX.Y.Z\`
   for the book).
4. Equality (no-op write) is allowed — needed for the v0.10.0 release where \`pyproject.toml\`
   is already at the target.
5. Site-only mode skips the guard (no version write happens at all).
6. Missing \`index-vol{N}.qmd\` warns rather than fails (defensive against future routing changes).

## Verification

Tested \`semver_lt\` locally against 9 cases:

\`\`\`
PASS  0.1.10 vs 0.10.0 → LT     ← the TinyTorch footgun
PASS  0.10.0 vs 0.1.10 → GE
PASS  0.10.0 vs 0.10.0 → GE     ← equality allowed
PASS  0.0.1 vs 0.5.1 → LT       ← vol2 patch regression
PASS  0.1.0 vs 0.5.1 → LT       ← vol2 minor still regresses
PASS  0.6.0 vs 0.5.1 → GE       ← vol1 normal forward bump
PASS  0.5.2 vs 0.5.1 → GE
PASS  1.0.0 vs 0.99.99 → GE
PASS  0.5.1 vs 0.5.10 → LT      ← naive lex sort would get this wrong
\`\`\`

YAML parses cleanly for both workflows. \`CI: Check workflows are safe for fork PRs\` hook passes.

## What this unblocks

The actual staged rollout (TinyTorch v0.10.0, Book vol1 v0.6.0, Book vol2 v0.1.0) can now be
triggered without worrying about the default-button creating a silent regression. Each volume's
first release just needs the right \`previous_version\` / \`explicit_version\` override, and the
guard tells you exactly which one to set if you forget.

## Tổng quan

Pull Request này triển khai tính năng **Chỉnh sửa hàng loạt bài học** cho trang quản lý bài học trong hệ thống e-learning.
