### 1. Xử lý hành động hàng loạt ở Backend (Java)

**Tệp:** `LessonManagementController.java`

* Chuyển từ việc từ chối POST requests thành xử lý ba hành động chính: `archive` (xóa), `duplicate` (nhân bản), `update_status` (đổi trạng thái).
* Nhận danh sách ID bài học từ form thông qua tham số `item-checkbox` **(getParameterValues())** và thực hiện tương ứng.
* Trả về thông báo thành công với số lượng bài học được xử lý và chuyển hướng lại trang _có bảo toàn tham số tìm kiếm._

### 2. Thêm Utility Functions cho xử lý dữ liệu (Java)

**Tệp:** `StringUtils.java`

* Thêm phương thức `generateCloneTitle()` sử dụng Regex để tạo tên bài học nhân bản với định dạng:

  * `Tên gốc (Bản sao 1)`
  * `Tên gốc (Bản sao 2)`
  * ...
* Tự động tăng số thứ tự nếu bài học đã tồn tại.

**Tệp:** `RequestUtils.java`

* Thêm phương thức `getParameterAsListInt()` để xử lý mảng dữ liệu từ các checkbox, chuyển đổi thành danh sách `Integer` với lọc và xử lý lỗi.

### 3. Mở rộng Data Access Layer (DAO)

**Tệp:** `LessonDao.java` & `LessonDaoImpl.java`

* Thêm 3 phương thức:

  * `deleteLessonByIds()`
  * `findMaxOrderIndexByCourseId()`
  * `updateLessonsStatusByIds()`
* Sử dụng JDBI để thực hiện bulk operations hiệu quả.

### 4. Mở rộng Service Layer (Business Logic)

**Tệp:** `LessonService.java` & `LessonServiceImpl.java`

* Thêm các phương thức:

  * `deleteLessonByids()`
  * `getMaxOrderIndexByCourseId()`
  * `bulkDuplicateLessons()`
  * `changeLessonsStatusByIds()`
* `bulkDuplicateLessons()` xử lý logic nhân bản:

  * Tạo bản sao của từng bài học.
  * Gán tên mới dựa trên Regex.
  * Đặt trạng thái thành `INACTIVE`.
  * Cập nhật chỉ số thứ tự.

### 5. Tối ưu Controller Base

**Tệp:** `BaseController.java`

* Thêm phương thức `handleSuccess()` để xử lý thông báo thành công, lưu vào session và chuyển hướng.

### 6. Cải thiện Frontend - JavaScript

**Tệp:** `lesson-management.js`

* Chuyển từ jQuery sang Fetch API hiện đại.
* Thêm logic click vào hàng để chọn checkbox tự động.
* Giữ lại debounce 500ms cho tìm kiếm/lọc nhưng sử dụng Fetch thay vì AJAX.

**Tệp mới:** `bulk-action.js`

* Tạo module `BulkActionManager` để quản lý chọn hàng loạt và gửi hành động.
* Xử lý sự kiện checkbox (đơn lẻ và "Chọn tất cả").
* Hiển thị/ẩn thanh action bar dựa vào số checkbox được chọn.

**Tệp:** `modal.js`

* Mở rộng logic modal confirm để hỗ trợ hành động hàng loạt.
* Thêm hàm `openConfirmBulkAction()` với cấu hình động cho các action:

  * `delete`
  * `duplicate`
  * `update_status`
* Thay đổi màu sắc, biểu tượng và nút bấm động tùy theo loại hành động.

### 7. Cập nhật giao diện - HTML/CSS/JSP

**Tệp:** `confirm-modal.css`

* Điều chỉnh `z-index` từ `1001` thành `200` để phù hợp với hệ thống phân tầng.
* Xóa màu cứng cho title, thêm class động:

  * `title-danger`
  * `title-primary`
  * `title-dark`
* Thêm kiểu cho nút và icon theo action:

  * `btn-danger`
  * `btn-primary`
  * `btn-dark`

**Tệp:** `action-bar.css`

* Giảm `z-index` từ `9999` thành `100` để phù hợp với hệ thống layering.

**Tệp:** `bulk-action-bar.jsp`

* Chuyển từ JavaScript inline sang `data-action` attributes cho nút hành động.
* Sử dụng JSTL tags thay vì scriptlet.
* Ẩn thanh mặc định, chỉ hiện khi có checkbox được chọn.

**Tệp:** `confirm-delete.jsp`

* Làm cho modal confirm tái sử dụng cho mọi hành động (không chỉ xóa).
* Thêm ID `confirm-modal-title` để cập nhật động.

**Tệp mới:** `lesson-fragment.jsp`

* Tách phần nội dung bảng (table + action bar + pagination) thành fragment riêng.
* Sử dụng khi AJAX lấy dữ liệu mới để chỉ render phần thay đổi.

**Tệp:** `lesson-management.jsp`

* Bọc table + action bar + pagination bằng form POST (`bulkActionForm`).
* Di chuyển script tags xuống cuối trang để tối ưu tải.
* Thêm script inline để khôi phục trạng thái bộ lọc từ `localStorage`.

**Tệp:** `lesson-table-body.jsp`

* Thêm thuộc tính `name="item-checkbox"` vào checkbox để dễ lấy dữ liệu từ backend.

**Tệp:** `management-default.css`

* Cập nhật màu hover của bảng.
* Đặt `cursor: auto` cho các thành phần hành động.

### 8. Xóa tệp cũ

**Tệp:** `action-bar.js` (xóa)

* Chức năng được tích hợp vào `bulk-action.js`.

## Chi tiết kỹ thuật

### Luồng xử lý nhân bản bài học

1. Người dùng chọn một hoặc nhiều bài học từ bảng.
2. Nhấp nút **"Nhân bản"** trên thanh action bar.
3. Modal confirm hiện lên với thông báo động.
4. Khi xác nhận, form gửi POST request với:

   * `action=duplicate`
   * Danh sách ID.
5. Backend xử lý từng bài học:

   * Lấy bài học gốc từ database.
   * Xác định chỉ số thứ tự tiếp theo trong khóa học.
   * Sử dụng regex để tạo tên:

     * Nếu bài đã có tên dạng `"Tên (Bản sao N)"` → tăng `N`.
     * Nếu chưa có → thêm `"(Bản sao 1)"`.
   * Tạo bản sao với trạng thái `INACTIVE`.
6. Trả về thông báo thành công và chuyển hướng.

### Luồng AJAX cho tìm kiếm/lọc

1. Người dùng nhập/chọn trên form bộ lọc.
2. Sau 500ms debounce, gửi GET request với `renderType=partial`.
3. Backend trả về HTML của fragment (chỉ phần bảng + action bar + pagination).
4. JavaScript thay thế nội dung `#lessonTableBody` bằng HTML mới.
5. State checkbox được reset (do fragment mới không có checkbox đã chọn trước).

### Xử lý hành động hàng loạt

* **Xóa (Archive):** Gọi `archiveLessonsByIds()` với lý do xóa.
* **Nhân bản (Duplicate):** Gọi `bulkDuplicateLessons()` để tạo bản sao.
* **Đổi trạng thái (Update Status):** Gọi `changeLessonsStatusByIds()` để toggle `ACTIVE ↔ INACTIVE`.

## Kiểm thử

Các scenario cần kiểm thử:

* Chọn checkbox:

  * Click vào checkbox hoặc click vào hàng bảng nên hiển thị/ẩn thanh action bar.
* "Chọn tất cả":

  * Bấm checkbox ở header nên chọn tất cả hàng.
* Bỏ chọn một:

  * Nếu bỏ chọn 1 hàng, checkbox "Chọn tất cả" nên tự bỏ chọn.
* Nhân bản:

  * Chọn bài học → bấm "Nhân bản" → xác nhận.
  * Bài học nhân bản phải có tên `(Bản sao 1)`, `(Bản sao 2)`, ...
* Xóa:

  * Chọn bài học → bấm "Xóa" → xác nhận.
  * Bài học nên bị xóa (archive).
* Đổi trạng thái:

  * Chọn bài học → bấm "Đổi trạng thái" → xác nhận.
  * Trạng thái nên toggle.
* Bộ lọc AJAX:

  * Nhập từ tìm kiếm, chọn khóa học, chọn ngày.
  * Bảng nên cập nhật mà không tải lại trang.
* Pagination sync:

  * Khi chuyển trang, phân trang nên được bao gồm trong AJAX response để không lệch.

## Kết quả đạt được

* Triển khai hoàn toàn tính năng chỉnh sửa hàng loạt bài học với ba hành động: xóa, nhân bản, đổi trạng thái.
* Cải thiện UX bằng cách cho phép click vào hàng bảng để chọn checkbox.
* Sử dụng SSR + AJAX để lọc/tìm kiếm mà không tải lại trang toàn bộ.
* Modal confirm động với kiểu và thông báo khác nhau tùy theo hành động.
* Xử lý tên bài học nhân bản thông minh bằng regex, tự động tăng số thứ tự.
* Mã backend sạch sẽ với phân tách rõ ràng giữa Controller → Service → DAO.
* Code JavaScript hiện đại, loại bỏ jQuery AJAX, sử dụng Fetch API.
* Bảo toàn tham số bộ lọc khi thực hiện hành động hàng loạt.

author: copilot
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This content was generated by GitHub Copilot.

Calling a C++/CLI managed static with 17+ `const T&` parameters from native code throws `HRException` on .NET 9/10 (worked on .NET 8). Reproduction requires Windows + MSVC + IJW, which is not available in this environment, so no code change is being proposed — this PR is an investigation report with a pointer to the likely regression.

## Description

- No source changes. Investigation-only PR.
- Likely regression: **PR #106000 / #106424** (commit `cfa0cc5b0282`, "Inject IJW Copy Constructor calls in the JIT instead of in the IL stubs"), which re-enabled GS (buffer security) checks on Reverse P/Invoke IL stubs.
- Likely site: `Compiler::gsCopyIntoShadow` in `src/coreclr/jit/gschecks.cpp`. There is a `TARGET_X86 && FEATURE_IJW` branch that, for `opts.IsReversePInvoke()`, inserts the shadow copy **after** `CORINFO_HELP_JIT_REVERSE_PINVOKE_ENTER` (i.e. after the GC transition). The fall-through path used on x64 inserts the copy at the **start** of `fgFirstBB` — before the transition:

```cpp
// non-x86/IJW fall-through, inserts BEFORE the reverse-PInvoke transition:
GenTree* src   = gtNewLclvNode(lclNum, varDsc->TypeGet());
GenTree* store = gtNewStoreLclVarNode(shadowLclNum, src);
LIR::AsRange(fgFirstBB).InsertAtBeginning(src, store);
```

- Hypothesis: with 18 byref params, GS marks all of them as vulnerable pointers (`lvIsPtr = 1`) and emits a shadow copy per param. The "17" threshold is probably where cumulative frame / stack-arg load first surfaces a latent ordering bug against the P/Invoke-enter helper. This is unverified.
- Ruled out (by reading, not by running):
    - `ijwhost` `start_runtime_thunk_stub` and `TheUMEntryPrestub` prologues — both preserve the caller's stack-arg region across register/XMM save+restore and `TAILJMP_RAX`. Alignment and shadow-space math check out for >16 args.
    - `patch_vtable_entries` / `FixupVTables` / `UMEntryThunk` — no arg-count-dependent code paths.
- Existing IJW tests (`src/tests/Interop/IJW/**`) do not cover managed static vtfixup entries with ≥17 by-ref parameters, which is consistent with the regression slipping through.

## Suggested next steps (for a reviewer with a Windows box)

- Run the repro with `DOTNET_JitDump=IL_STUB*` / `DOTNET_JitDisasm=IL_STUB*` and confirm whether shadow copies for the 18 params are emitted before `JIT_REVERSE_PINVOKE_ENTER`.
- If confirmed, generalize the `TARGET_X86 && FEATURE_IJW` branch in `gsCopyIntoShadow` (and the matching branch in `gsParamsToShadows`) to fire for all `opts.IsReversePInvoke()` targets.
- Add a regression test under `src/tests/Interop/IJW/` covering a C++/CLI static exposed via vtfixup with ≥17 `const T&` parameters.

cc @AaronRobinsonMSFT @jkoritzinsky.

author: jbailes
body:
## What changed
This fixes Wolf UI's in-container API access and split-mode layout behavior.

- The API client no longer assumes `http://localhost/...` and instead uses the mounted Wolf socket path correctly inside the container.
- The Dockerfile is updated to build cleanly again on a current Ubuntu base.
- The Godot stretch configuration is adjusted so split-mode seats fill the available render area correctly.

## Why
Party mode was blocked by two separate Wolf UI issues during live validation:

- the app tried to reach the Wolf API over `localhost:80` instead of the mounted socket-backed path
- the split layout stayed vertically compressed because the project stretch settings were too restrictive for the narrower render target

## Impact
Wolf UI can launch inside a party-mode seat, talk to the local Wolf API correctly, and render into the split viewport without the half-height layout issue.

## Validation
- `docker build -t wolf-ui:local /home/virant/gow/wolf-ui`
- live validation through Wolf party mode on a Moonlight session

body:
## Motivation

The backlog safety hook used unbounded `.*` bridges, so legitimate design guidance could be blocked when words like `from`, `queue`, or `task` appeared far apart or inside filenames. This change narrows the matcher to nearby task-pickup phrasing and adds regression coverage for both the backlog hook and the audited `/exit` hook.

## Summary

- tighten `.claude/hooks/block-autonomous-backlog.sh` to use bounded, word-aware matches instead of greedy cross-sentence bridges
- add `.claude/hooks/block-autonomous-backlog.test.sh` to pipe real hook payloads through the backlog and `/exit` hooks and assert block vs allow outcomes
- wire the hook regression script into `make test` through a dedicated `test-hooks` target

## Testing

- `./.claude/hooks/block-autonomous-backlog.test.sh`
- `for i in $(seq 1 100); do ./.claude/hooks/block-autonomous-backlog.test.sh >/dev/null; done`
- `make test-hooks`
- `make vet`
- `make test`  
  Observed existing unrelated failures in `internal/daemon`: `TestRunProcessReloadOverUnixSocket`, `TestRunProcessAssignResumeAndCancelOverUnixSocket`, `TestRunProcessCancelOverUnixSocketIgnoresDeadPane`, and `TestRunProcessBatchOverUnixSocket` all timed out waiting for Unix sockets after relay disconnect errors.

## Review focus

- whether the bounded matcher still catches the intended autonomous-backlog prompts without crossing into filenames or distant design text
- whether the shell harness covers the right regression cases for both hooks without overfitting to command formatting

Closes LAB-1413

author: musab-creator
body:
## Summary

Phase 0 + Phase 1 of the CRM redesign plan agreed with Musab.

- **Phase 0 — Roadmap & epics.** `docs/CRM_ROADMAP.md` traces every requirement from the April 2026 holistic specification to an implementation phase. `docs/CRM_EPICS.md` stands in for GitHub Issues (disabled on this repo) with one epic per functional area, Critical → Nice checklists, and links back to the roadmap.
- **Phase 1 — Domain model.** One Supabase migration + matching TypeScript types. Adds the tables every later phase needs, with no UI changes and no existing tables modified. Reps keep using what works.

## New tables (all in `public`)

| Table | Supports |
|---|---|
| `lead_source`, `territory`, `lead_status`, `bad_lead_reason`, `carrier` | §4.1, §4.3 — seeded with Jacksonville/Middleburg/St. Augustine/Ponte Vedra, the full pipeline, reason codes, and 10 common carriers |
| `rep_profile`, `rep_territory` | §4.2, §4.9 — default 50 % commission share and $1,800 overhead cap |
| `lead`, `lead_activity` | §4.1, §4.2 — pre-customer record with unified activity log; promotes (not merges) to `customer` on contingency signature |
| `claim`, `supplement`, `supplement_line_item`, `supplement_template` | §4.3 — ESX-ready (paths stored for import/export) |
| `call_center_agent`, `call_center_lead_submission` | §4.6 — $280 base + $15/confirmed + $5/bad defaults, `Asia/Amman` timezone |
| `request` | §4.5 — structured replacement for most rep-to-office text traffic |
| `commission`, `job_pnl_snapshot` | §4.2, §4.4, §4.8 — 50/50, 25/25/50, and per-deal overrides; snapshots drive margin outlier alerts |

## Design decisions

1. **Money in cents, bigint.** Float rounding on commissions is unacceptable.
2. **Lead ≠ Customer.** Bad leads never pollute customer history. `lead.promoted_customer_id` links when a lead closes.
3. **Claim hangs off lead, not customer.** The lead is the stable anchor across the promotion.
4. **No RLS yet.** Policies deferred to a Phase 1.5 follow-up once rep accounts are seeded — keeps this PR purely additive.
5. **Additive only.** Zero changes to `customer`, `invoice`, `quote`, etc.

## Phase order (from `docs/CRM_ROADMAP.md`)

| # | Phase | Spec sections |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Roadmap + epics *(this PR)* | All |
| 1 | Domain model *(this PR)* | 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.6, 4.8 foundations |
| 2 | Lead Management & Intake | 4.1 Critical |
| 3 | Sales Pipeline + Commission engine | 4.2 |
| 4 | Claims & Supplements | 4.3 (likely 4a + 4b) |
| 5 | Job P&L + Documents | 4.4, 4.7, 4.8 (likely 5a + 5b) |
| 6 | Communication + Call Center | 4.5, 4.6 |
| 7 | Reporting, Team, Marketing | 4.8, 4.9, 4.10 |

## Open decisions flagged in the roadmap

1. Telephony vendor for Phase 6 (JustCall / RingCentral / Five9)
2. Xactimate ESX sample files from Musab for Phase 4b
3. Exact trigger for lead-to-customer promotion (currently "Contingency Signed")

## Apply the migration

```sh
# Via Supabase CLI (recommended)
supabase db push

# Or apply directly in the Supabase SQL editor
# Paste supabase/migrations/20260420000000_crm_domain_expansion.sql
```

The migration is additive and idempotent (uses `if not exists` + `on conflict do nothing` on seed rows).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` passes (tsc strict + vite)
- [ ] Apply migration to a Supabase dev project and confirm all tables/indexes/triggers created
- [ ] Confirm seed data lands: 4 territories, 12 pipeline stages, 6 reason codes, 7 sources, 10 carriers
- [ ] Reviewer sanity-checks the schema against `docs/CRM_EPICS.md`

body:
## Summary

Add visible batch-configuration controls to the SendFIL UI without implying unimplemented execution capabilities are already live.

## What changed

- added a wallet-type selector in the left rail with `Single-signer` as the default active v1 lane
- added visible `Transaction method` and `Error handling` toggle groups above the recipient workflow
- added a reusable unavailable-capability modal so clicking unsupported options keeps the UI visible while preserving the current defaults
- added shared batch-configuration types and labels
- surfaced the active batch configuration in the review modal and sticky footer summary
- updated the review modal test coverage for the configuration summary

## Why

The DevSpec calls for sender-visible batch configuration. This PR puts the UI structure in place now while keeping unsupported paths honest:

- `Multi-sig` remains unavailable in v1 and shows a notice
- `ThinBatch` remains visible but unavailable until the execution lane is wired
- `Atomic` remains visible but unavailable until the strict execution path is implemented
- defaults reset on refresh; nothing is persisted in local storage

## Validation

- `yarn test`
- `yarn lint`
- `yarn typecheck`

## Follow-up

Subsequent PRs can wire these controls into the underlying execution and estimation paths as those capabilities land.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/herkingdom/agent-runs/69e601f8f5e13c8f6ed8553c

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** an issue with policy pages its not fetching on front of the website look into that kindly

✅ **Result:** The storefront policy pages (Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Refund Policy) were not rendering the content seeded into the database — visitors saw the fallback "Content not available." copy even though the admin panel could read and edit the same policies.

## What was wrong

The three public policy pages (`/privacy-policy`, `/terms-of-service`, `/refund-policy`) were querying the `policies` table directly with the Supabase anon key, while every other path that successfully reads this table — the admin list endpoint and the CRUD endpoint — uses the service-role client, whose helper comment in `lib/supabase/admin.ts` explicitly calls out that it "bypasses RLS." With row-level security effectively blocking anonymous reads of `policies`, the anon-key query returned no rows and the pages silently fell back to their placeholder content. A secondary bug compounded the problem: the pages were reading a `last_updated` column that does not exist in the schema (the column is `updated_at`), so even if the fetch had worked the "Last updated" date would always have shown the hard-coded fallback.

Errors were also being swallowed — the old code destructured only `data` and ignored `error`, so nothing showed up in server logs to point at the root cause.

## What changed

The three storefront policy pages and the public `/api/policies/[slug]` route now fetch through the service-role admin client, matching the pattern used by the rest of the policy code paths. The query adds an explicit `is_published = true` filter so unpublished drafts stay hidden from the storefront even though the read now bypasses RLS. Each fetcher also logs Supabase errors and exceptions instead of swallowing them, which will make future issues obvious in the deploy logs. Page-level ISR (`revalidate = 300`) was added so admin edits appear on the public pages within five minutes without requiring a redeploy. The "Last updated" label now reads the real `updated_at` column, so the timestamp reflects the most recent admin save.

No schema, environment variable, or admin-side changes were required. The seed data added in the previous commit (`027_seed_policies.sql`) is now surfaced correctly on the storefront, and any subsequent edits made through the admin policies screen will flow through to the public pages on the next revalidation.

body:
## Summary

- `scripts/ralph-stop-hook.sh` — the tiny portable Stop hook. Runs `codex1 status --json`, reads `data.stop.allow`, exits 2 to block Stop or 0 to allow. Never touches plan files, subagent state, or `.ralph/`.
- `scripts/README-hook.md` — wiring docs for `~/.codex/hooks.json` (or per-repo `.codex/hooks.json`), verification steps, and uninstall.
- `crates/codex1/tests/ralph_hook.rs` — Rust integration tests that run the shell script against a mocked `codex1` binary. Covers: `stop.allow: true`, `stop.allow: false`, empty output, no `codex1` on PATH, malformed JSON, and executable-bit check.

### Notable design decision

The hook reads `.data.stop.allow` directly instead of `.data.stop.allow // true`. jq's `//` alternative-operator treats literal `false` as "missing" and would have flipped a real block into an allow. Null / missing is handled explicitly by the shell `case *)` branch.

## Smoke test

```
$ cd /tmp/codex1-u12 && codex1 init --mission demo
$ codex1 --json status --mission demo
  ... "stop": { "allow": true, "reason": "idle", ... }
$ CODEX1_BIN=/path/to/codex1 bash scripts/ralph-stop-hook.sh; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
```

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)

author: vamzi
body:
I have optimized the frame decoding process in both the `openhost-daemon` and `openhost-client` crates.

Previously, incoming frames were buffered in a `Vec<u8>`, and processed frames were removed using `buf.drain(..consumed)`. This is an $O(N)$ operation as it requires shifting all remaining bytes in the vector.

I replaced these buffers with `bytes::BytesMut`, which allows for $O(1)$ buffer advancement using `buf.advance(consumed)`. This provides a significant efficiency gain, especially when handling large frames (up to 16 MiB) or a high volume of small frames.

**Changes:**
- In `crates/openhost-daemon/src/listener.rs` and `crates/openhost-client/src/session.rs`:
    - Changed the inbound buffer type from `Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>` to `Arc<Mutex<BytesMut>>`.
    - Updated `on_message` callbacks to use `buf.put_slice(&msg.data)` (requiring `BufMut`).
    - Updated frame decoding loops to use `buf.advance(consumed)` (requiring `Buf`).

**Performance Impact:**
- Reduces the cost of consuming $N$ bytes from an $M$-byte buffer from $O(M)$ to $O(1)$.
- Measurable improvement in CPU efficiency for high-throughput data channels.

**Verification:**
- Verified that all workspace tests pass (`cargo test --workspace`).
- Verified that the code compiles without warnings (`cargo clippy`).
- Verified logic correctness through existing integration tests that exercise the full request/response cycle over data channels.

author: pavankrish123
body:
Added an automated benchmarking system for all 5 obstudio skills. It runs each skill via claude -p against example apps, then runs the same task without the skill (baseline), and grades both against assertions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  How pass % works: each eval has concrete assertions (e.g., "inventory.md is created", "Spans table has 5+ signals"). Pass rate = assertions passed / total assertions. Delta = skill minus baseline — positive means the skill is adding   
  value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  First run results:                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  Skill                                With Skill   Baseline   Delta
  splunk-audit                      97%       100%      -3%                                                                                                                                                                                           
  splunk-instrument            71%        71%       0%                                                                                                                                                                                           
  splunk-observe                60%        60%       0%                                                                                                                                                                                           
  splunk-provision              62%        71%      -9%                                                                                                                                                                                           
  splunk-verify                    45%        45%       0%                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  Takeaway: No skill outperforms baseline yet — meaning our current assertions test for things Claude already knows how to do (add OTel packages, create setup files). The skills' real value — correct inventory format, SLI definitions,   
  fault domains, semconv compliance — needs more targeted assertions. This gives us a clear roadmap for both skill improvements and better eval cases.                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  What's in the PR:                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  - tests/run_skill_eval.py — eval runner (runs with/without skill, grades, benchmarks)
  - skills/*/evals/evals.json — 10 test cases across all 5 skills                                                                                                                                                                            
  - evals/ excluded from release binary (dev-only)               
  - Makefile: make skill-eval SKILL=splunk-audit / make skill-eval-all                                                                                                                                                                       
  - CI job ready (commented out for now)                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  - Full writeup: docs/skill-evals.md

## Overview
Add support for animated vs. instant scroll modes in the console framebuffer. During the boot sequence, scrolling should appear gradual/animated (shifting line-by-line with visual feedback). Once the shell starts, scrolling should be instant (all lines shift up at once).

  - Shift all lines in sequence until the screen is scrolled

author: pedronfigueiredo
body:
## Problem observed in testing

The perps direct deposit flow could include a synthetic gas-funding leg, generated internally for native ETH on Arbitrum, with targetAmountMinimum: '0'. That leg was optional and not the real asset the user was trying to deposit, but the Across strategy support check still evaluated it as if it were a required quote leg. As a result, a valid perps deposit request could be marked unsupported before quote resolution, because the optional gas leg made the whole request set fail strategy validation.

The fix was to make Across treat those zero-minimum synthetic gas legs consistently everywhere. A shared helper was introduced to identify “real” Across quote requests, and both quote fetching and strategy support now filter out requests where targetAmountMinimum === '0' unless it is a max-amount flow. In practice, that means the real deposit leg can proceed while the optional gas top-up leg no longer disqualifies the route. The turn also added a regression test covering exactly that case: one real perps deposit leg plus one synthetic native-token gas leg, and the strategy now correctly returns supported.

## Summary
- ignore synthetic zero-target gas legs when evaluating Across support
- share the same request filter between Across support checks and quote building
- add coverage for perps direct deposits that include a synthetic gas leg

## Testing
- yarn jest --config packages/transaction-pay-controller/jest.config.js --watchman=false packages/transaction-pay-controller/src/strategy/across/AcrossStrategy.test.ts --coverage=false

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Across strategy request filtering, which affects whether routes are considered supported and which legs are quoted; mistakes could cause valid quotes to be skipped or unsupported routes to be attempted.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Across strategy validation/quoting to **ignore synthetic “gas” legs** (requests with `targetAmountMinimum: '0'`) so they don’t cause perps direct deposits to be marked unsupported.
> 
> Introduces a shared `isAcrossQuoteRequest` helper and applies it consistently in both `AcrossStrategy.supports` and `getAcrossQuotes`, and adds regression tests covering mixed real+synthetic legs, all-synthetic legs, and `isMaxAmount` zero-minimum behavior.

author: jbailes
body:
## What changed
Adds 2-seat party-mode split rendering to Wolf, layered on top of #419's zero-copy / gst-interpipe context-sharing work.

- **Rebased onto #419** (`fix/amd-dma-buf-negotiation`) — this PR now targets #419, not `stable`, because the GPU-aware split compositor depends on #419's gst-interpipe `GST_QUERY_CONTEXT` forwarding (so VA/CUDA elements share a context across the interpipe boundary) and its generic-DMABuf runtime negotiation.
- **Party-mode session management + API** for join, promote, and teardown; secondary "hidden seat" sessions; local-gamepad join path.
- **GPU-aware split compositor.** The split is composited entirely in GPU memory, selected per detected vendor so solo and party sessions stay zero-copy:
  - VA/QSV: `vapostproc` + `vacompositor` (VAMemory)
  - NVIDIA: `cudaconvertscale` + `cudacompositor` (CUDAMemory)
  - software fallback: `videoconvertscale` + `compositor`
  The old unconditional system-memory `videoconvertscale` could not ingest CUDAMemory/DMABuf at all, so it would have broken zero-copy streaming for every GPU session; the per-vendor sources fix that.
- **Config bumped to v9** (migration `version <= 8`) so existing v8 (10-bit) installs are re-migrated and pick up the party pipeline. `config.v9.toml` carries the software party source plus `default_source_va` / `default_source_cuda`; `configTOML` selects by vendor.
- Restart-runner-in-place so the primary app relaunches at split render size without dropping the Moonlight session; render size decoupled from `display_mode` via `render_display_mode`.
- Hardened session-id parsing across all session endpoints (`parse_session_id`), preserve producer caps features on resize, dedup the two-seat geometry.

## Verification
- `cmake` build of wolf (full Docker image) green against #419's pinned gst-interpipe.
- VA (`vacompositor`) and CUDA (`cudacompositor`) split-compositor chains validated standalone with `gst-launch` on real hardware — both negotiate the split entirely in GPU memory (no host round-trip), reach PLAYING, no caps errors.
- Real wolf binary boots, migrates config to v9, and selects the correct GPU party source per vendor: "zero copy pipeline on Nvidia" (RTX 5080, renderD128 -> CUDA source) and "zero copy pipeline on Intel" (UHD 770, renderD129 -> VA source).
- Pending: end-to-end Moonlight client stream with a live party join (decode/visual check across vendors).

## Depends on
- #419 (`fix/amd-dma-buf-negotiation`) — base branch.
- `games-on-whales/wolf-ui#12`, `games-on-whales/gst-wayland-display#27` (companion changes).

author: gnufede
body:
## Description

In Bazel payload-files mode, `PayloadFileTelemetryAPI` was building a synthetic telemetry payload by hand: it accumulated CI visibility metrics locally and wrote a single `generate-metrics` batch on `finish()`. This payload was missing several things required for the backend to recognise and display the telemetry:

- **`seq_id`** — required by the telemetry v2 protocol for ordering/deduplication
- **`app-started`** lifecycle event — backend uses this to register the telemetry session
- **`app-closing`** lifecycle event
- **Real integration, dependency, and configuration info** — only available through the actual `TelemetryWriter` lifecycle
- **Correct metric format** — count and distribution metrics must be in separate `generate-metrics` / `distributions` events using the `points`-based wire format

As a result, telemetry payloads were uploaded (HTTP 202) but not visible in the backend.

**Fix:** swap the `telemetry_writer`'s HTTP client with a `_PayloadFileTelemetryClient` that writes each outgoing batch to a file. The real `TelemetryWriter` lifecycle runs as normal — collecting integrations, dependencies, configurations, CI metrics — and the output is redirected to `payloads/telemetry/` instead of the network.

On `finish()`, `periodic(force_flush=True, shutting_down=True)` is called directly (not `app_shutdown()`, which guards on `self.started`) so the flush batch includes `app-started`, all accumulated events, and `app-closing`. `writer.started` is reset beforehand so `app-started` is re-emitted with real content after the client swap.

Files changed:
- `ddtrace/testing/internal/telemetry.py`: replace synthetic accumulator with `_PayloadFileTelemetryClient` + client-swap; remove now-unused imports
- `tests/testing/internal/test_payload_files.py`: update tests to match real writer output (`points`-based metric format, lifecycle events, structural `message-batch` assertions)

## Testing

Verified against a live Bazel CI run: telemetry payloads now appear in the backend. Updated unit tests cover:
- At least one `message-batch` file written on `finish()` with `seq_id`, `application`, `host`
- `app-started` and `app-closing` present in the emitted events
- CI visibility count and distribution metrics present with correct `points`-based format

## Risks

Low. The change only affects `PayloadFileTelemetryAPI`, which is only instantiated in Bazel payload-files mode (`DD_TEST_OPTIMIZATION_PAYLOADS_IN_FILES=true`). Normal (HTTP) telemetry is unaffected. If `telemetry_writer` is a `NoOpTelemetryWriter` (telemetry disabled), the code falls back to the base `TelemetryAPI.finish()` with a warning log.

body: ## Status Quo Currently, a logged-in provider **cannot** file lab results on behalf of another provider. --- ## Change We have added functionality to allow a provider to **file results on behalf of other providers**. (Example shown logged in as `doctor oscardoc`.) > [!IMPORTANT] > This PR is designed to **minimize support burden on OpenOSP**. > - By default, this PR will NOT change any behaviour because the functionality defaults to "off" for all providers. > - Only if providers **actively turn on this feature within the user preferences** will this option to "file on their behalf" become enabled. > - Note that for Magenta, we decided to turn on this feature for all providers automatically in our production, without any significant complaints. --- ## Main Workflow ### Case 1: 0 or 1 provider attached to the lab: - Clicking `Acknowledge` opens the updated acknowledgement dialog, but **no file options are shown**. - ### Case 2: More than 1 provider attached to the lab: - Clicking `Acknowledge` opens a **combined modal** where the user selects providers to file for and adds an acknowledgement comment. - - - User adds comment and **selects providers** to file on their behalf, then clicks `Submit`. - - **After confirmation**, the UI updates accordingly: - --- ## Preferences Providers can configure the behavior under **Preferences**: 1. **Control the file dialog accordion** Toggle the option: *"Automatically expand "File Document on Behalf of Others" in comment box"* - If **disabled**, the accordion is **collapsed by default** when the modal opens: - - If **enabled**, the accordion is **expanded by default** when the modal opens: - 2. **Prevent others from filing on your behalf** Turn off the option: *"Allow other providers to file results on your behalf when they acknowledge HL7 lab results "* - --- ## Additional Features 1. Even if a user has **already acknowledged a lab**, they can still file it for other providers using the `File for…` button. - - - 2. If the provider has acknowledged version 1 and, after some time, version 2 is released. - If the provider then acknowledges version 2: - Old behaviour: The status of version 1 was changed from A → F. - - New behaviour: The status of version 1 is not changed if it is already A. - ## Summary by Sourcery Add provider-level preferences and UI workflows to allow filing HL7 lab results on behalf of other providers while preserving existing behaviour by default. New Features: - Introduce optional "File Document on Behalf of Others" workflow in the HL7 lab acknowledgement UI, including a combined acknowledge/file modal and a separate "File for…" dialog when multiple providers are linked to a lab. - Allow providers to file HL7 lab results on behalf of other providers via a new backend action that files labs up to a selected version with an auto-generated audit comment. - Expose new provider preferences to control whether the combined file-on-behalf section auto-expands and whether other providers are allowed to file results on their behalf. Bug Fixes: - Prevent older lab versions from being automatically filed when acknowledging a newer version if the older version is already acknowledged. - Avoid JavaScript errors when interacting with lab windows whose opener has been closed. Enhancements: - Refine lab filing logic to respect existing comments, avoid overwriting when filing on behalf, and centralize privilege checks for filing operations. - Extend provider lab routing status to include a filed state and make lab queue removal utilities reusable. - Modernize the lab comment preference page to a Bootstrap-based UI and integrate it with the new HL7 lab result preference flows.

author: roaminro
body:
## Summary

The Mastra AG-UI adapter did not tell the client about the authoritative thread history stored in Mastra memory, and the converter on the way in stripped message IDs. Together this caused every follow-up turn on an existing thread to duplicate previously-persisted messages and left the CopilotKit UI out of sync with what Mastra had on disk.

## What changed

- **Preserve AG-UI message IDs** when converting to Mastra `CoreMessage`, so Mastra's `MessageHistory` processor and storage layer can deduplicate by ID on subsequent turns.
- **Emit `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT`** before `RUN_FINISHED`, sourced from `memory.recall()`, so the client can reconcile its local history with the server's view of the thread.
- **Add `convertMastraMessagesToAGUI`** with full multimodal support:
  - User image/audio/video/document parts round-trip through AG-UI `InputContent`, decoding base64 data URLs back to raw base64 + mimeType and leaving plain URLs as `url` sources.
  - Tool result messages use a deterministic id of the form `` `${parentMessageId}:${toolCallId}:result` `` so snapshots are stable across repeated emissions.
- **Guard `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` emission** on the converted AG-UI message count (not the raw recalled count) so a system-only history does not produce an empty snapshot that would wipe client-side state.

## Test plan

- \`pnpm test\` — 132 tests passing across 7 files.
- \`tsc --noEmit\` — clean.

New tests:

- \`mastra-to-agui-conversion.test.ts\` — text, multimodal round-trips (image/audio/video/document), stable tool-result IDs, snapshot stability.
- \`messages-snapshot.test.ts\` — ordering vs `STATE_SNAPSHOT` and `RUN_FINISHED`, remote-agent and empty-history no-op cases, system-only no-op case, best-effort failure handling, tool-call messages.
- \`message-conversion.test.ts\` — updated expectations for ID preservation.

Related CopilotKit issues:

- CopilotKit/CopilotKit#1969
- CopilotKit/CopilotKit#1881

author: rkthomps
body:
## Summary
This PR completes the proof that the big-step semantics and bounded evaluation semantics for the Imp language are equivalent. The implementation adds the missing theorems to `Examples/Imp/Semantics.lean` and removes the placeholder from `Examples/Scratch/Scratch.lean`.

## Key Changes

- **Added helper lemmas for `Stmt.eval` unfolding**: Six private theorems (`eval_zero`, `eval_skip`, `eval_assign`, `eval_seq`, `eval_if`, `eval_while`) that provide fine-grained control over the recursive definition without over-eager simplification.

- **Proved monotonicity of bounded evaluation**:
  - `Stmt.eval_mono_succ`: Adding one unit of fuel preserves successful evaluations
  - `Stmt.eval_mono`: Increasing fuel preserves successful evaluations (generalized version)

- **Proved bidirectional equivalence**:
  - `bigstep_to_eval`: Every big-step derivation is witnessed by some bounded evaluation with sufficient fuel
  - `eval_to_bigstep`: Every successful bounded evaluation yields a big-step derivation
  - `eval_bigstep_true`: Main equivalence theorem stating big-step semantics agrees with bounded evaluation

- **Removed placeholder**: Deleted the `sorry` stub from `Examples/Scratch/Scratch.lean` and moved the theorem to its proper location in `Semantics.lean`.

## Implementation Details

The proofs use structural induction on both the fuel parameter and statement structure. The key insight is that fuel acts as a bound on recursion depth, and the monotonicity lemmas allow us to normalize fuel amounts when combining evaluations of sub-statements. The bidirectional proofs handle all statement constructors (skip, assign, sequence, if-then-else, while loops) with careful case analysis on boolean conditions and option values.

author: copilot
body:
The app stores highly sensitive personal financial data with no authentication and no containerized deployment path. This adds a complete local hosting setup: Docker Compose spins up the backend and a nginx frontend that enforces HTTP Basic Auth on every route, keeping port 3001 internal to the Docker network.

## Changes

### `backend/Dockerfile`
- Multi-stage Node 20 alpine build: stage 1 installs `python3/make/g++` to compile the native `better-sqlite3` addon; stage 2 is a lean runtime-only image with no build tools.

### `frontend/Dockerfile` + `nginx.conf` + `entrypoint.sh`
- Multi-stage build: Vite compiles the React app, output is copied into `nginx:alpine`.
- `nginx.conf` enables `auth_basic` on all routes and reverse-proxies `/api/` to the backend container.
- `entrypoint.sh` generates `/etc/nginx/.htpasswd` at container start from `BASIC_AUTH_USER`/`BASIC_AUTH_PASS` env vars using `printf | htpasswd -i` (avoids password exposure in process listings). Credentials are never baked into the image.

### `docker-compose.yml`
- `backend` service: no host port exposed — only reachable from nginx via the internal Docker network.
- `frontend` service: exposes port 80, receives Basic Auth credentials via environment.
- Named volume `net-worth-tracker_data` persists the SQLite database across restarts and rebuilds.

### `.env.example`
- Single root-level template combining Basic Auth credentials and optional AI PDF-parsing keys (forwarded to backend via `env_file`).

### `README.md`
- New "Docker Compose (recommended for local hosting)" section with copy-paste quickstart ahead of the existing manual dev instructions.

## Usage

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# set BASIC_AUTH_USER and a strong BASIC_AUTH_PASS

docker compose up --build -d
# → http://localhost  (browser prompts for credentials)
```

author: ooples
body:
## Summary

Full implementation of Issue #212 (FFT and spectral parity with torch.fft).

Ships:
- **Core kernels** — iterative radix-2 Cooley-Tukey + Bluestein chirp-z for arbitrary length, single dispatch through `FftKernels.Transform1D`. Fixes the standing correctness bug where the prior `CpuEngine.FFTCore` silently zero-padded non-power-of-2 inputs to `NextPowerOf2` and returned a different transform than callers asked for.
- **Public `Fft` module** — 1D/2D/ND complex (`Fft1/IFft1/Fft2/IFft2/FftN/IFftN`), real (`RFft/IRFft/RFft2/IRFft2/RFftN/IRFftN`), Hermitian (`HFft/IHFft/HFft2/IHFft2/HFftN/IHFftN`), shift (`FftShift/IFftShift`), frequency grids (`FftFreq/RFftFreq`). Three norm modes — Backward/Forward/Ortho — with PyTorch-exact semantics.
- **Windows suite** — 11 window functions matching torch.signal.windows: Hann, Hamming, GeneralHamming, Blackman, Nuttall, GeneralCosine, Bartlett, Cosine, Gaussian, Exponential, Kaiser (Bessel I₀ via inline power series).
- **Stft/Istft** — torch.stft parameters (hop_length, win_length, window, center, pad_mode ∈ {Reflect, Constant, Replicate}, normalized, onesided); ISTFT uses weighted overlap-add for COLA-compliant perfect reconstruction.
- **Autograd** — closed-form backward for `Fft1/IFft1/RFft/IRFft` with correct dual-norm rule and factor-of-2 handling for the Hermitian-packed bins. Validated against finite differences.
- **FftConv** — FFT-based same-padding convolution (Conv1D + Conv2D multi-channel w/ bias) matching PyTorch Conv cross-correlation semantics via kernel spatial flip. Bit-for-bit identical to direct conv within roundoff.

Supply-chain independent: no cuFFT / rocFFT / clFFT bindings. The entire numerical surface is the two kernels (Cooley-Tukey + Bluestein).

## Test plan (177/177 green)

Five complementary test layers:

| Layer | Tests | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `FftKernelsInvariantsTests` | 125 | Round-trip × 3 norms, linearity, Parseval × 2 norms, shift theorem, conjugate-symmetry for real input, DC bin, delta spectrum, sinusoid → single bin. 13 lengths including 7 Bluestein (non-pow2) cases. |
| `FftApiTests` | 14 | Batched Fft1 round-trip, RFft/IRFft at n=8/32/100 (Bluestein), ortho unitarity, FftShift/IFftShift, FftFreq/RFftFreq match numpy, Fft2 + RFft2 roundtrip, HFft↔IHFft. |
| `StftIntegrationTests` | 7 | COLA reconstruction (Hann, multiple hop configs), FFT-based conv matches direct conv to 1e-9 (incl. non-pow2), Parseval preservation under `normalized=true`. |
| `FftParityTests` | 10 | numpy-golden values for Fft/RFft, Hann/Hamming/Bartlett hand-computed, Kaiser(β=0) constant, pure-cosine spectral peak. |
| `FftGradcheckTests` | 13 | Finite-difference validation of all 4 autograd rules × 3 norm modes to 1e-5 relative tolerance. |
| `FftConvTests` | 11 | Conv1D/Conv2D vs direct conv to 1e-9, multi-channel with bias, non-pow2 Bluestein path. |

- [x] All 177 FFT tests pass on net10.0
- [x] Clean build on net10.0 + net471
- [x] No external FFT library dependency
- [x] Non-power-of-2 correctness bug fixed via Bluestein

## Closes
- Closes #212

author: facuparedes
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `localtuya.update_dps` service that sends the Tuya `UPDATEDPS` (`0x12`) protocol command to request fresh datapoint values from a device
- Accepts an optional `dps` parameter to specify which DP indexes to refresh (defaults to all detected and whitelisted DPs)
- Enables on-demand DPS refresh from automations and scripts without requiring a constant `scan_interval`

## Motivation

Currently, the only way to trigger the `UPDATEDPS` command is via the periodic `scan_interval` timer. This means users who want fresh energy monitoring data (current, power, voltage — typically DPs 18, 19, 20) must configure a fixed polling interval that runs continuously, even when the device is idle.

By exposing `update_dps` as a service, users can build smarter automations that only poll when needed — for example, refreshing energy DPs every few seconds only while a smart plug is actively in use, and stopping when it's off.

### Example automation
```yaml
automation:
  - alias: "Poll energy only when plug is on"
    trigger:
      - platform: time_pattern
        seconds: "/10"
    condition:
      - condition: state
        entity_id: switch.my_plug
        state: "on"
    action:
      - action: localtuya.update_dps
        data:
          device_id: "my_device_id"
          dps:
            - 18
            - 19
            - 20
```

## Changes

- `__init__.py`: Added `SERVICE_UPDATE_DPS` schema, `_handle_update_dps` handler, and service registration
- `services.yaml`: Added `update_dps` service definition with `device_id` and optional `dps` fields

## Test plan

- [x] Manually tested on a Tuya smart plug — calling the service updates `last_updated` on energy sensor entities
- [ ] Verify behavior with sub-devices (gateway + node_id)
- [ ] Verify behavior when `dps` parameter is omitted (should refresh all whitelisted DPs)
- [ ] Verify error handling when device is disconnected

author: thomasjiangcy
body:
## What was changed
This changes the generated Codex runtime config so our proxy-backed OpenAI provider is named `OpenAI` instead of `Proxy`. Codex `0.120.0` gates remote compaction on the provider name, so this makes sandbox sessions use the remote `/responses/compact` path instead of the local compaction path while keeping the existing `proxy` provider key and transport wiring intact.

Original symptom this addresses:
```text
Sandbox sessions were emitting `contextCompaction` items locally and continuing to use the normal `/responses` path even when the runtime was backed by OpenAI through Mistle's proxy. That meant we never exercised Codex's remote `/responses/compact` endpoint in these sessions.
```

- `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/compile-runtime.ts`: changes the generated provider display name from `Proxy` to `OpenAI` so Codex treats the proxy-backed provider as OpenAI for compaction decisions.
- `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/compile-runtime.test.ts`: adds an explicit assertion that generated Codex config now contains `name = "OpenAI"`.
- `apps/control-plane-api/integration/sandbox-profiles-compile-runtime-plan.integration.test.ts`: updates the runtime-plan expectation to match the new generated provider name.
- `packages/sandboxd/src/sandboxd_state.rs`: updates the representative config fixture used in sandboxd tests to keep the sample Codex config aligned with runtime generation.

## How to review
Start with `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/compile-runtime.ts`, because that is the behavioral change. Then check the two TypeScript tests and the sandboxd fixture update to confirm the config contract is consistent everywhere we assert or document it.

If you want to validate behavior locally, review in this order:
- `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/compile-runtime.ts`
- `packages/integrations-definitions/src/agent-runtimes/codex/compile-runtime.test.ts`
- `apps/control-plane-api/integration/sandbox-profiles-compile-runtime-plan.integration.test.ts`
- `packages/sandboxd/src/sandboxd_state.rs`

Useful local validation commands:
- `pnpm validate:changed`
- `pnpm run ci`

## What the implication was
After this change, Codex should treat Mistle's proxy-backed OpenAI runtime as OpenAI for compaction selection, so sandbox sessions can use remote compaction instead of falling back to local compaction solely because the provider was labeled `Proxy`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Generated Codex config] --> B{Provider name is OpenAI?}
    B -- yes --> C[Codex selects remote compaction]
    C --> D[/responses/compact/]
    B -- no --> E[Codex selects local compaction]
    E --> F[Normal /responses path with local summary rewrite]
```

This keeps the existing proxy route and credentials model unchanged. The only semantic change is which Codex compaction path becomes eligible.

## Checks and tests performed
- `pnpm validate:changed`
  - What is being tested: repo-required changed-scope format, lint, typecheck, and test coverage for the affected workspaces.
  - Expected outcome: the changed Codex runtime config and its dependent packages remain green under the repo's scoped validation flow.
  - How it is implemented: the repo's `scripts/dev/validate-changed.ts` planner ran the required workspace checks for the modified files.
- `pnpm run ci`
  - What is being tested: the same end-to-end local CI contract enforced before push in this repo.
  - Expected outcome: full TypeScript and Rust CI lanes pass with the provider renamed to `OpenAI`.
  - How it is implemented: the repo's top-level CI script ran `ci:ts` and `ci:rust`, including formatting, linting, OpenAPI drift checks, typechecking, dashboard build, and workspace test suites.

body:
## Summary

Set `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: 'true'` on the `security` job. Seven added lines in `ci.yml`, all inside the job's new `env:` block plus an explanatory comment.

## Why

After #166 merged, every run of the `security` job surfaces this warning:

> Node.js 20 actions are deprecated. The following actions are running on Node.js 20 and may not work as expected: `actions/cache@0400d5f6…`

The flagged action is **inside** `aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0.35.0` (which is the latest — there's no newer release that bumps the internal `actions/cache` pin). We can't SHA-rotate our way out of this without aquasecurity cutting a new release.

`FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24` is GitHub's official opt-in env var for exactly this case: it tells the runner to execute any JS action declaring `node16` / `node20` on the installed `node24` binary anyway. GitHub's deprecation notice recommends this as the interim workaround.

## Scope

Scoped to the `security` job only via `jobs.security.env`. Other jobs run first-party actions (`actions/checkout@v6`, `actions/setup-go@v6`, `actions/attest-build-provenance@v4`) that are already on node24 natively, so they don't need the flag.

## Removal condition

Drop the env block once `aquasecurity/trivy-action` ships a release with `actions/cache@v5` (or whatever the node24 successor ends up being) internally. Comment in the YAML documents this.

## Test plan

- [ ] Push triggers CI; the `Security scan (Trivy)` job no longer shows the node20 deprecation warning.
- [ ] Trivy still runs and the SBOM artifact is still produced.

body:
Executive Summary
This Pull Request formalizes the statistical validation phase of the Crypto ML Predictor project. We have
confirmed the existence of a statistically significant relationship between volume anomalies and future price
movements.

Technical Implementation
 - Statistical Framework: Implemented Z-Score calculation with 7-day and 30-day rolling windows to identify
   market anomalies.
 - Hypothesis Testing: Executed Spearman rank correlation analysis across multiple time horizons (T+1, T+7,
   T+30) to evaluate predictive signal strength.
 - Event Study: Developed a radiography tool for "Extreme Volume Events" to inspect historical price
   performance following volume climaxes.
 - Feature Engineering: Integrated calendar-based seasonality features (Day of Week, Month End) to capture
   potential institutional rebalancing patterns.

Key Findings
 - Statistical Significance: Confirmed a negative correlation between 30-day Volume Z-Scores and 30-day price
   returns for major assets (Bitcoin, Ethereum), with p-values < 0.05.
 - Pattern Recognition: Identified a structural "Market Exhaustion" pattern: extreme volume spikes (> 3.0
   Z-Score) consistently preceded significant price corrections in the studied period.
 - Predictive Horizon: The 30-day horizon shows higher predictive reliability than the 7-day horizon,
   supporting a trend-following approach over short-term reactive trading.

author: primiano
body:
- Remove the timeout on flush: this is unnecessary and
  adds just another timing parameter that makes the code
  harder to reason about. If aflags takes too long, the
  existing code in both TracingServiceImpl (5s) and
  ProbesProducer (1s) will take care of it.
- Unify some of the code paths that handle error cases.
- Added Subprocess::Kill (without Wait). This is to avoid
  suspending traced_probes' main thread waiting for the
  termination of a process in case of timeouts: if aflags
  takes too long, the trace will be finalized, hence the
  AndroidAflagsDataSource will be destroyed. By default
  the Subprocess dtor does a KillAndWait (and cannot
  do otherwise to avoid zombie processes). So we try
  to reduce the chance of waiting by allowing up to
  10 seconds between the kill and the waitpid().

docs/proposals/2026-04-20-sme-open-questions.md — new document with one section per question:

  Q1. Low-OCI ellipse-suppression cutoff.
      Proposal: keep provisional 3.0; calibrate at Phase 4b to the
      30th-percentile of the real OCI distribution (or to a natural
      gap if one exists); finalize as one coordinated PR touching
      the TS config constant, schema-level references, methodology
      prose, and DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3.3.5 per the existing §7
      coordination commitment.

  Q2. Saturation-N × compute budget.
      Proposal: use the saturation-derived operational N; do not
      reduce N below it. If compute becomes a v2 bottleneck, reduce
      B from 500 to 200 before reducing N — N is load-bearing, B is
      elastic in bootstrap literature.

  Q3. Human-OCI bootstrap treatment for purposive samples.
      Proposal: add human_oci_sample_type enum field to GroundingRef
      (purposive / representative / random / unknown), plus a
      binding methodology-page caveat block on every human-OCI
      baseline. Disambiguates "narrow because correlated draws"
      (model case) from "narrow because sample doesn't cover
      population" (purposive human case). Schema-level change ready
      now; operationally binds when the first researcher submission
      with pile_sort_raw.csv arrives (Phase 6+).

  Q4. G2 rename sufficiency.
      Proposal: two-tier vocabulary. Keep "inter-model similarity
      dispersion permutation test" in code / DATA_DICTIONARY.md /
      open data bundle. Use "structure test" with a one-line gloss
      in dashboard body text and methodology-page body. Technical
      audit trail stays precise; public surface stays readable.

  Q5. "Mismatch is the finding" methods-page lead.
      Proposal: draft the lead paragraph now (~120 words, included
      verbatim in the proposal) rather than waiting for Phase 5.
      Gets the framing into review early. Shakedown's first real

Each section carries the question restatement, proposed resolution, rationale, resolvability-by-shakedown-vs-Phase-4-etc disposition, and a "what the CDA SME needs to decide" checklist. author: dib-adhoc
body:
Pin remaining mutable action tags to exact commit SHAs to prevent supply
chain attacks via tag poisoning (CVE-2026-31976).

Previously `pre-commit/action` and `actions/github-script` were pinned,
but three actions still used mutable tags:

| Action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | `@v4` | `@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5` |
| `actions/setup-python` | `@v5` | `@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065` |
| `actions/cache` | `@v4` | `@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830` |

All actions in the workflow are now pinned to a commit SHA. A compromised
or force-pushed tag can no longer silently inject malicious code into the
runner.

References:
- CVE-2026-31976 (Xygeni-action — tag poisoning in third-party actions)
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions

author: xmfcx
body:
- Replace the deprecated `rosbag2_cpp::get_typesupport_library` and `rosbag2_cpp::get_typesupport_handle` calls in [planning/planning_debug_tools/src/perception_replayer/perception_replayer_common.cpp](https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_tools/blob/6106a5c361240fe3abfd0d47a99fa5e46ec7b135/planning/planning_debug_tools/src/perception_replayer/perception_replayer_common.cpp) with their `rclcpp` counterparts.
- Swap the include from `<rosbag2_cpp/typesupport_helpers.hpp>` to `<rclcpp/typesupport_helpers.hpp>`; dereference the `shared_ptr<rcpputils::SharedLibrary>` since the `rclcpp` variants take a reference, not a `shared_ptr`.
- Gate the handle call on `ROS_DISTRO_HUMBLE` (a compile definition set by `autoware_package()`), because the function was renamed between distros.

## Why
The `rosbag2_cpp` typesupport helpers are deprecated in Jazzy:

> This function will be deleted in the next 'Lyrical Luth' ROS release. Please use the rclcpp counterpart functions.

With Autoware's `-Werror=deprecated-declarations` policy, this broke the `autoware_core` `build-and-test-jazzy-above` CI job. The `rclcpp` helpers are the upstream-recommended replacement.

### Cross-distro detail

The handle function was renamed between Humble and Jazzy in `rclcpp`, while the `rosbag2_cpp` and `rclcpp` variants already differ in their 3rd argument (shared_ptr vs. reference):

| API | Humble | Jazzy |
|---|---|---|
| [`rclcpp::get_typesupport_library`](https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/blob/humble/rclcpp/include/rclcpp/typesupport_helpers.hpp#L38) | returns `shared_ptr<SharedLibrary>` | returns `shared_ptr<SharedLibrary>` |
| [`rclcpp::get_typesupport_handle`](https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/blob/humble/rclcpp/include/rclcpp/typesupport_helpers.hpp#L50-L54) | takes `SharedLibrary &` | **deprecated**, renamed to `get_message_typesupport_handle` |
| `rclcpp::get_message_typesupport_handle` | does not exist | takes `SharedLibrary &` |
| [`rosbag2_cpp::get_typesupport_handle`](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/humble/rosbag2_cpp/include/rosbag2_cpp/typesupport_helpers.hpp#L40-L46) | takes `shared_ptr<SharedLibrary>` | deprecated |

So on Humble we call `rclcpp::get_typesupport_handle(..., *library)`, and on Jazzy `rclcpp::get_message_typesupport_handle(..., *library)` — both take the `SharedLibrary &`, hence the dereference.

---

## Test plan

- [ ] Build on Jazzy:
  ```bash
  source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && \
    colcon build --symlink-install --event-handlers=console_cohesion+ \
      --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      --packages-select planning_debug_tools
  ```
  Expect: `Finished <<< planning_debug_tools` with no `-Wdeprecated-declarations` errors (previously failed at `perception_replayer_common.cpp:83` and `:87`).
- [ ] Build on Humble with the same command (sourcing `/opt/ros/humble/setup.bash`); expect no `get_message_typesupport_handle is not a member of rclcpp` error.
- [ ] Re-run the `autoware_core` `build-and-test-jazzy-above` workflow after the sub-repo pin is updated; job should pass the Build step.

author: appixo
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #134 / #135. User's smoke after #135 still showed task row columns visually misaligned — action icons and status pills in the wrong column.

**Root cause:** column widths summed to more than the viewport at typical laptop sizes.

- checkbox 36px + site 96px + profile 140px + proxy-group 140px + status 160px + actions 144px = 716px of fixed widths.
- Plus `width: 38%` on the product column.
- At a ~1050px content area (typical after the sidebar), 38% ≈ 399px → 1115px total → ~65px overflow. Under `table-layout: fixed`, that breaks cell-to-header mapping.

**Fix:** drop the 38% on `.task-row-product`. Under `table-layout: fixed`, the column without an explicit width absorbs remaining space. Product is the flex column; every sibling has a pixel width. This makes product auto-fill correctly at any viewport.

Also ships Sanne's prior branch work: strengthened td-count / thead-tbody parity tests (18 → 19 tests in TaskRow.test.tsx).

author: sergiotejon
body:
Fixes #117

## Problem

When `auto_implement` creates a PR from an issue, the PR was never stored in the local SQLite DB. The poll loop might eventually find it, but often with an empty title — causing blank entries in the Activity view.

## Root cause

`CreatePR()` only returned the PR number, discarding the GitHub ID and URL. The pipeline never called `UpsertPR()` after creation.

## Fix

1. **`CreatePR` returns `*CreatedPR` struct** (number + id + html_url) instead of just `int`
2. **Pipeline stores the PR immediately** after creation via `UpsertPR` with the correct title, author, URL, and state

## Files changed

- `daemon/internal/github/repos.go` — `CreatedPR` struct, updated return type
- `daemon/internal/issues/pipeline.go` — `UpsertPR` call after `CreatePR`, updated interface
- `daemon/internal/github/repos_test.go` — updated mock responses and assertions

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a production-ready, mocap-less pipeline that converts a 2D video into an auditable 3D scene + per-frame manifest for downstream DCCs. 
- Enable robust identity selection and mask tracking (SAM) combined with 33-point MediaPipe pose extraction and monocular depth to lift poses into a metric 3D space. 
- Reduce common failure modes for single-camera capture by fitting a ground plane and snapping feet to it while preserving a traceable timeline for frames where the target is lost.

### Description

- Add `src/scene_processor.py` which implements `IdentityScanner` (SAM ROI + optical-flow tracking), `DepthEstimator` (DepthAnything V2 with a `transformers` fallback), `GroundPlaneEstimator` (RANSAC plane fit + projection), and `SceneProcessor` that outputs a structured JSON `Manifest` containing per-frame `FrameTransform` entries (translation, rotation, scale, confidence, lost-target flag, and named 33 keypoints in 3D meters). 
- Add `blender_scripts/blender_bridge.py` which implements `Global_Transform`, a `ManifestImporter` that builds simple environment meshes, constructs a metarig from first-frame keypoints, and keys the root transform frame-by-frame while applying global scale/rotation/location adjustments. 
- Add `README.md` with the exact folder layout and explicit dependency/install commands for a clean virtual environment, optional DepthAnything checkpoint instructions, and usage examples for both the scene processor and Blender import. 
- Implement lost-target handling and defensive checks across the pipeline (e.g., insufficient tracker features, missing pose landmarks, missing SAM checkpoint, and plane-fit failures) and provide a CLI with arguments for video, SAM checkpoint, device, target id, and output path.

### Testing

- Ran static compilation checks with `python -m py_compile src/scene_processor.py blender_scripts/blender_bridge.py`, which completed successfully.

author: mojzis
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a new `--focus-args` flag to enable seamless integration with the `pre-commit` and `prek` frameworks. The flag interprets positional arguments as focus files (files to narrow the clone report to) rather than scan paths, with the scan root implicitly set to `.`. This allows pre-commit hooks to pass changed files directly as trailing arguments without requiring explicit `--files` flags.

## Key Changes

- **New `--focus-args` flag**: Mutually exclusive with `--files` and `--files-from`. When set, positional arguments are treated as focus files and the scan root is always `.`
- **Refactored positional argument handling**: Changed from a single `path: PathBuf` to `positionals: Vec<PathBuf>` to support multiple focus files and flexible argument parsing
- **Added `scan_path()` method**: Resolves the scan root based on whether `--focus-args` is set and validates positional argument counts
- **Updated `resolve()` method**: Now returns both the resolved `Config` and the scan path to avoid duplicate computation
- **Enhanced `focus_files()` method**: Extended to handle the new `--focus-args` option alongside existing `--files` and `--files-from` modes
- **Pre-commit hook definitions**: Added `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` with two hook configurations:
  - `biston`: Runs `scan --focus-args` for clone detection on changed files
  - `biston-stats`: Runs `stats --focus-args` for pair count reporting
  - Both include `require_serial: true` to prevent parallel batching that would miss cross-file clones
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added 11 new tests covering:
  - Equivalence between `--focus-args` and `--files` modes
  - Empty focus list handling (silent pass)
  - Conflict detection with incompatible flags
  - Pre-commit style invocation patterns
  - Filtering behavior (only reporting clones involving focused files)
- **Documentation updates**: Enhanced `docs/src/commit-hooks.md` with pre-commit framework integration instructions and examples

## Implementation Details

- The `--focus-args` flag uses `conflicts_with_all = ["files", "files_from"]` to enforce mutual exclusivity at the CLI level
- Empty positional lists with `--focus-args` are valid and produce empty reports (matching the behavior of `--files-from -` with empty stdin)
- The scan still processes the entire repository tree; focusing only narrows the output report to clones involving the specified files
- All three focus modes (`--focus-args`, `--files`, `--files-from`) return `Option<Vec<PathBuf>>` where `None` means no filtering and `Some(vec)` means apply focus (even if empty)

body:
## Summary

The setup wizard derives the first receive address via `deriveaddresses(desc, [0, 0])` (pure descriptor math — bypasses Core's label registry). When a user plots to that address and opens the forging-assignment page, their address is missing from the dropdown (`getaddressesbylabel("")` only returns labeled addresses), and clicking "Generate new address" returns a **different** address because index 0 now counts as used.

Fix: after deriving, call `setlabel(addr, "")` if the address isn't already labeled. The derived address belongs to the wallet's active descriptor, so `setlabel` is guaranteed to succeed.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh wallet → setup wizard → confirm the displayed plotting address has `labels: [""]` after save (check via `getaddressinfo` RPC or directly in a Core console).
- [ ] Receive coins to the plotting address → open forging-assignment → plotting address **is** listed in the dropdown.
- [ ] Open setup wizard a second time → no duplicate `setlabel` call (idempotent guard via `labels.length === 0`).

author: patrick-hermann-sva
body:
## Summary
Release-time: copy `tests/kcl-deploy-profile.yaml` to a temp path and `sed config.image` to the actual tag being released before handing it to `stuttgart-things/dagger/kcl push-kustomize-base`. Source profile stays untouched so local dev (`make run`, `kcl run kcl/`) still works.

## Why
`tests/kcl-deploy-profile.yaml` pins `config.image: ghcr.io/stuttgart-things/clusterbook-operator:latest`. The release workflow uses that profile verbatim when rendering the kustomize bundle — so the Deployment spec written into `cluster-operator-kustomize:<any-tag>` always points at `:latest`. Consequence:

```bash
flux pull artifact oci://…clusterbook-operator-kustomize:v0.7.2 --output /tmp/cbk
kubectl apply -k /tmp/cbk
# -> "deployment.apps/clusterbook-operator configured"
# -> no rollout (image name unchanged), pod keeps running whatever
#    :latest layer the node cached
```

Observed in the wild during the first smoke test: had to `kubectl set image deployment/clusterbook-operator manager=…:v0.7.2` by hand. Now `apply -k` on a tagged bundle will actually roll.

## Diff
```diff
+      - name: Stage release KCL profile (pin image tag)
+        if: steps.version-after.outputs.new_release == 'true'
+        run: |
+          VERSION="${{ steps.version-after.outputs.version }}"
+          mkdir -p /tmp/release
+          cp tests/kcl-deploy-profile.yaml /tmp/release/profile.yaml
+          sed -i "s|^config.image:.*|config.image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${VERSION}|" /tmp/release/profile.yaml

       - name: Push kustomize base
         …
-            --parameters-file ./tests/kcl-deploy-profile.yaml
+            --parameters-file /tmp/release/profile.yaml
```

## Test plan
After merge, next release cut (v0.8.x):
- Stage profile step logs show `config.image: ghcr.io/stuttgart-things/clusterbook-operator:v0.8.x`
- `flux pull artifact oci://…clusterbook-operator-kustomize:v0.8.x --output /tmp/cbk && kubectl kustomize /tmp/cbk | grep image:` prints the pinned tag
- `kubectl apply -k /tmp/cbk` on a cluster running an older version actually triggers a rollout

## Follow-ups (out of scope)
- Once #54 (docs) is merged + this lands, remove the "apply -k is a no-op between versions" caveat from `README.md` and `docs/install.md` in a cleanup PR
- `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` stays — with tagged images there's no reason to use `Always`

Closes #53

author: agustin-manessi
body:
## Summary

- Implements `config-parse` subcommand: reads `commit-types.yml` + `defaults.yml` + `.versioning.yml`, deep-merges them (replicating `yq eval-all * *` semantics), applies `commit_type_overrides`, writes `/tmp/.versioning-merged.yml`.
- Adds `internal/config` merge engine: `LoadRaw`, `deepMergeMap`, `LoadAndMerge`, `ApplyOverrides`, `WriteMergedConfig`.
- Adds `config.Parse()` (no defaults) alongside `config.Load()` (with defaults) — distinction: `Load` for raw sources, `Parse` for pre-merged configs where explicit values must not be overwritten.
- Adds integration test `test_go_config_parser.py`: 21 fixtures, semantic diff (yaml.safe_load + dict equality), tests override update/add/bump-change, fallback chain, and malformed YAML.

### Post-audit fixes (mandatory scope)

**(a) Schema-aware versioning (FINDING MEDIUM):** `NextVersion` rewrote from `Masterminds/semver` fixed 3-slot to a slot-based model driven by `VersionConfig`. `BumpMinor` now increments the patch slot (3rd active component). Cold start `feat:` on `epoch+major+patch`: bash `v0.0.1`, Go now `v0.0.1`. `xfail` removed from `test_feat_development_release`.

**(b) 3 duplicate loaders unified:** `detection.LoadConfig`, `guardrails.LoadConfig`, `notify_teams.loadNotifConfig` all replaced with canonical loader. Side-effect fixes: detection was missing the `[Hh]otfix/*` default keyword pattern; `notify_teams` had `OnSuccess=true` default (bash default is `false`); `notify_teams` now uses `Parse()` so explicit `enabled: false` is honored.

### Behavior delta vs bash (accepted)

- **Merged YAML comments:** bash preserves source comments (yq), Go omits (yaml.v3). Getters read values, not comments.
- **Unicode escape representation:** bash mixes `\U...` and raw UTF-8, Go normalizes to UTF-8. Same codepoints.
- **Key ordering:** yaml.v3 may reorder keys. Getters do keyed lookups — order irrelevant.
- **Tests use semantic diff** (`yaml.safe_load` + dict equality), not byte diff.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make lint` — clean
- [ ] `make test-unit` — 498/498 bats pass
- [ ] `go test ./...` — all Go unit tests pass (config merge engine + schema-aware versioning)
- [ ] `test_dual_run_calc_version.py::test_feat_development_release` — passes as normal assert (not xfail)
- [ ] `test_go_config_parser.py` — 21 fixtures semantic diff pass
- [ ] `test_go_notify_teams.py::test_disabled_no_post` — enabled: false honored

author: xzavrel
body:
## Summary

Add the modern **Streamable HTTP transport** (MCP spec 2025-03-26) alongside the existing legacy SSE transport, and upgrade the MCP Kotlin SDK from `0.8.1` to `0.11.1`.

Closes #22

## Changes

### SDK Upgrade
- `io.modelcontextprotocol:kotlin-sdk` upgraded from `0.8.1` → `0.11.1`
- SDK `0.11.1` includes `StreamableHttpServerTransport` which was not available in `0.8.1`

### Dual Transport Support

The server now exposes **both** MCP transport protocols simultaneously:

| Endpoint | Protocol | Spec | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST/GET /mcp` | Streamable HTTP | [2025-03-26](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/2025-03-26/transports/#streamable-http) | ✅ Recommended |
| `GET /sse` + `POST /` | Legacy SSE | [2024-11-05](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/2024-11-05/transports/#http-with-sse) | ⚠️ Deprecated, kept for backward compatibility |
| STDIO | Standard I/O | — | Unchanged |

### Code Refactoring
- Extracted shared `buildMcpServer()` function to avoid duplicating server creation logic across transport types (STDIO, Streamable HTTP, Legacy SSE)

## Why

The legacy SSE transport (dual-endpoint: `GET /sse` for discovery → `POST /message` for messages) was deprecated in the MCP specification as of 2024-11-05. The replacement — **Streamable HTTP** — uses a single endpoint model with better infrastructure compatibility, scalability, and error handling.

This was recently highlighted when [Moltis had to add explicit legacy SSE client support](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/805) specifically for servers like lox-mcp.

By supporting both protocols, we ensure:
- **New clients** can use the modern Streamable HTTP transport at `/mcp`
- **Existing clients** (that only support legacy SSE) continue to work via `/sse`

## Verification

- [x] `./gradlew clean compileKotlin` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- [x] `./gradlew test` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (all tests pass)
